He spent 1997-2002 in London working as a freelance artist, a researcher at the Royal College of Arts and an external lecturer at the London Institute. He gained a PhD in electro-acoustic composition from City University London and currently works as a researc her at the Austrian Institute for Artificial Intelligence (OFAI) and teaches at the Vienna University of Music and Performing Arts.

Thomas Grill (AT), born 1972, studied technical physics in Linz, as well as Computer music and electronic media and interactive electronic instruments in Vienna. Since 2003, lectureships at the University for Music and Performing Arts and the University for Applied Arts, Vienna. Development of commercial and open-source media Software. Scientific associate at the Austrian Research Institut for Artificial Intelligence.

128320.name: The Turbulence Sound Matrix: Signe
128320.description:
The “TSM” uses digital recordings of the wind in the form of continuous cascading wave patterns to amplify and diffuse any sound source through the powerful 64 channels of the TSM’s unique speaker array. This adaptation creates a vivid, highly articulated and totally immersive sonic environment for the listener. Signe is created with three distinct layers of sound (wind-generated sine waves, a 1946 Royal Quiet Deluxe typewriter and a grand piano), all augmented by the flowing wave patterns of the wind.
“Signe” fully engages the sound potential of the Turbulence Sound Matrix, creating an audio art composition that is in constant motion, morphing itself through time and space at very high resolution, riding the waves of the air and the wind. “Signe” completely immerses us, creating a mesmerizing and completely hypnotic and immersive fabric of sound
128320.credits: "The Turbulence Sound Matrix" (2008) and the composition "Signe" (2008) were conceived, designed, and created by Steve Heimbecker, Montreal, Canada. Max MSP Programming: Etienne Grenier & Simon Laroche, Montreal, Canada
128320.biography: Steve Heimbecker (CA) is an intermedia audio artist and composer. He studied fine arts at the Alberta College of Art (1980), Calgary, CA. He creates multi-channel sound installations, compositions, and sound systems / instruments of his own design and concept, since his first such work in 1987. He has developed many sound-space diffusion concepts such as acoustic mapping process and wind-space architecture. http://www3.sympatico.ca/qubeassm/

128327.name: Le Tombeau de Freddie / L' Internationale
128327.description:
“Le Tombeau de Freddie / L’Internationale” consists of two components: one is a concept text entitled “Six Perspectives in Digital Music”. In this text we present our theoretical conclusion concerning “presence via apparatus” in today’s digital technology. The name “Rokugaku” proposed here is historically the first term for “recorded music”, which distinguishes it from music in general.
Another component is the acoustic realization of “Roku-gaku” in “L’Internationale” based on the well-known revolutionary song to the music composed by Pierre C. Degeyter in 1888. It is sung in Japanese by a computer-generated voice of wellknown rock star Freddie-M.
The voice is synthesized in real time by the original software programmed with Max/MSP, not using any sampling techniques but a perfectly rule-based formant of synthesis techniques alone. The brothers’ interest is in creating an acoustic reproduction of the real world. The challenge of “Le Tombeau de Freddie / L’Internationale” is to bring an origin of sounds “which-has-been-there” into existence through synthesized sounds alone.
“Le Tombeau de Freddie / L’Internationale” asserts the “fact” that Freddie-M has actually sung “The Internationale” in Japanese.
128327.credits: Concept by the Formant Brothers (Nobuyasu Sakonda & Masahiro Miwa). Acoustic Realization: Nobuyasu Sakonda (based on a song composed by Pierre C. Degeyter in 1888). Music Video: Hiromitsu Murakami
128327.biography:
Masahiro Miwa (JP), born 1958. Composer. In 1995 he was appointed as a lecturer at the Academy of Media Arts Cologne and since 2000 he has been a professor at IAMAS (Institute of Advanced Media Arts and Sciences) in Gifu, Japan

Nobuyasu Sakonda (JP), born 1961, musician / media artist. Associate professor (Computer music /sound media art / media theory) at the Department of Visual Media, Nagoya University of Arts and Sciences, http://web.mac.com/nsakonda/

128353.name: Tetraktis
128353.description:
“Tetraktis” is a Pythagorean term that symbolizes the first four whole numbers that together add up to ten.
The idea of four as a structure that contains other intrinsic numeric relationships has become the starting point to generate this string quartet. As in other electro-acoustic pieces with instruments that I have realized, my principal interest is to work on the material qualities of the instrumental timbres I am working with.
In the case of strings, I could say that along with the human voice they are the most complex of all instruments, due to the quantity of non-periodic sounds that can be generated. On the other hand, the electronic sounds of the work were made starting from samples recorded from the quartet instruments (violin, viola and cello).
The electronics of the piece are constituted by four digital tracks, with all the sounds spatialized. This is an extremely important quality of this composition, since the electronics exist in three dimensions, sounds moving all around the concert hall with the people in the middle of them
128353.credits: A Commission of the Arditti Quartet by the Ernst Von Siemens Foundation.
128353.biography: Manuel Rocha Iturbide (MX), born 1963, studied composition at the Escuela Nacional de Müsica at UNAM. He completed an MFA in electronic music and composition at Mills College. In 1999 he completed his PhD in Computer music at the University of Paris VIII. He has worked at various studios such as UPIC, GRM, IRCAM, LIEM, BANFF and lMEB. He worked as a researcher at IRCAM developing GiST (1994-95) and later as a professor at the University of Paris VIII (1995-96).

128430.name: Physiological Mechanics Fantasy
128430.description:
All through the piece there is a constant counterpoint between the physiological world (that of living organisms) and the metal mechanical world. On one hand there is an energy core as an expression of the essence of life, and on the other there are many objects that are working as truly artificial mechanisms. Life undergoes minuteperturbations and alterations as it progresses through different steps, phases or mechanical universes, which finally amounts to reaching a new condition.
Additionally this piece makes use of the spectrum as a means to create a dialectic between saturation and vacuum, which will be in permanent conflict with one another. The drama is all about forcing them to coexist, thus establishing a structural tension. However, the last section of the piece overcomes this conflict, and saturation and vacuum identify with each other. The opposites ultimately prove to be equal. That is to say that the magnet repulsion is eventually solved and magnets are able to reach an equilibrium point through the union of north and south poles. Identification is then attained through difference.
Saturated electronic sounds are mainly generated with timbre alterations obtained not only through spectrum manipulations but also by means of simple changes in sample quality and by time stretching and compression. The result is in some cases a quasi-synthetic sound and always takes up a large portion of acoustic space.
128430.biography: Lucas Fagin (AR), born 1980, studied composition with Daniel Montes and Ricardo Martinez until 2003 in Buenos Aires. From 2003 until 2007 he studied composition with Marco Stroppa, Stefano Gervasoni and Luis Naón at the Conservatoire National Superieur de Musique de Paris.

128483.name: Nabaz'mob - Opera for 100 smart rabbits
128483.description:
100 Nabaztag smart rabbits play an opera together specially composed by Antoine Schmitt and Jean-Jacques Birgé. Inviting John Cage, Steve Reich, Conlon Nancarrow and György Ligeti, this musical and choreographic score in three movements, transmitted via wi-fi, plays on the tension between the orchestral ensemble and the individual voices to create a strong and involved showpiece. This opera questions the issues of working together, organization, decision and control, which are increasingly central and difficult in our contemporary world.
Schmitt and Birgé are respectively the behavior designer and the sound designer of the Nabaztag rabbits, constructed by Violet. They have chosen to twist the industrial object into an artwork in which the choreography of the ears, the play of light and the hundred small loudspeakers hidden in the stomachs of each rabbit create a composition with three voices built on time-delay and repetition, programming and disrespect for rules.
128483.credits: Choreography and music: Antoine Schmitt. Jean-Jacques Birge; With the support of Violet, after an original initiative by Guylaine Monnier (Web Flash Festival)
128483.biography:
Antoine Schmitt (FR) is an artist, programming engineer and designer who questions the modalities of the free human in a complex world through minimal, monumental, abstract, generative, interactive, audio and visual installations. He considers programmed things as a radically new artistic material which he confronts to other fields of art such as architecture, dance, literature, music and cinema. His work has been exhibited and awarded internationally.

Jean-Jacques Birgé (FR), is a music composer ("Un Drame Musical Instantané"), film director ("Sarajevo: A Street Under Siege"), multimedia author ("Alphabet, "LeCieleEstBleu", "Somnambules") and sound designer. He considers sound as a counterpoint to pictures and dialog, an extraordinary off-stage landscape and a wide-open window to imagination. An improviser, he has been playing electronic music since 1965, has recorded more than 30 albums and received many awards in all these fields.

128512.name: Scherzo
128512.description: “Scherzo” is an aural and visual montage that explores the limits of human virtuosity and the convergence of man and machine. Energetic textural and melodic fragments were recorded by cellist Rubin Kodheli, whose performance was filmed from ten different camera angles (camera:Andrew Federman). These fragments have been edited into an impossibly extended musical climax.
128512.credits: Joe Diebes: composer and filmmaker; Rubin Kodheli: cello performance; Andrew Federman: cinematographer. Originally commissioned by the Create @ iEAR Residency Program at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute. Additional funding from The Experimental Television Center’s Finishing Funds program which is supported by the Electronic Media and Film Program at the New York State Council on the Arts.
128512.biography: Joe Diebes (US). His work converges around the categories of contemporary music, conceptual art and video. From 1996 to 2003, as a core member of the hybrid art collective "GAIe GAtes et al." (New York), Joe Diebes created the sonic element for over 20 collaborative performance projects. Since then he has composed a range of works including operas, unclassifiable hybrid pieces, music for theatre and dance, and sound installations for venues across the US, Europe and Asia.

128519.name: "Active Field" for ten violins and ten-channel 1-bit music
128519.description:
“1-Bit Music” is a project by artist and composer Tristan Perich that combines his classical training in music with primitive, hand-programmed electronics that investigate the foundations of digital sound.
In 2005, Cantaloupe Music released “1-Bit Music”, custom-built electronics packaged inside a standard CD jewel case, which synthesize an album of electronic music, illustrating the structure of the circuit and combining that transparent aesthetic with the lowest-fidelity sound. Since that release, Perich’s work has shifted towards compositions for traditional classical ensemble with 1-bit audio accompaniment.
The live musicians are paired with a set of speakers on stage, creating a hybrid multi-part work for acoustic and electronic sound. Connecting microchips directly to speakers, the resultant ensemble’s sound is “mixed” in the air, treating the speakers as a form of acoustic instrument, approaching the concept of electronic sound as a physical phenomenon.
128519.biography: Tristan Perich (US). In all of his creative activities Perich is inspired by the aesthetics of math and physics, and works with simple forms and complex systems. The challenge of elegance provokes his compositions for solo instruments, small ensemble and orchestra. As a visual artist, he works primarily with machines to create pen-on-paper drawings that explore the limits of traditional drawing through randomness and order. His recent activities include electro-acoustic pieces for 1-Bit Music with instrumental accompaniment. His experimental electronic music group, the Loud Objects, has performed in Germany, Japan, Italy (Screen Music 2), Norway (Piksei), England (Evolution) and in the US (including at the NIME festival).

128528.name: Sound as a medium - Klang als Medium
128528.description:
In our daily lives, our eyes and ears are constantly working together as a closely linked team to form our perception of the world. Traditionally practitioners in the plastic arts have adjusted this perception through vision, forming with shape and color. I on the other hand work with our sense of hearing.
The world of sound, which we inhabit daily, contains only a minuscule part of the sound universe our ear minds are capable of understanding. The part of it that is literal is limited to the things in our world that make sounds—footsteps, cars, dogs, and the like. Its other part is made up of two codified areas, spoken language and music. Both of these occupy only small points in the spectrum of sound possibilities. The sounds I create are in the large sound space around and in-between these sounds of everyday life.
The essence of what I do when I build a sound work lies in the nature of the sounds I build into a given context, what I call the character of the sound. We all have a sense of sound character. We are born with it perhaps, or learn it at a very early age. It is inherent in our language, though unconscious; we use it as another layer of meaning on top of verbal language. It tells the listener how to interpret the verbal meaning. We do it without thinking by shaping the contours of tone and emphasis in our speech and also by adjusting the sound of different parts of the words. Our response to these nuances is highly refined. Through minute differences in sound character we are often able to pinpoint the birthplace of a speaker. One could describe sound character as having several continuums of meaning lying between distant points, say, harsh and smooth or rich and thin or warm and cold, superimposed upon one another. In the area between these points, within the nature of the sound itself, lies an immense zone of meaning. Its expressions are transcultural; they are neither literal nor codified. In music this dimension is called sound color. It was introduced with the emergence of orchestration as a musical dimension, the idea that there is aesthetic meaning inherent in the nature of the sound itself, not just the melody and harmony. You don’t have the same work if you play just the melody and harmony of an orchestrated work on the piano.
In music, though, it is only part of the meaning. We can still recognize the piece without the orchestra if we play it on the piano. I have been interested in going further, distilling this essence, this inborn language, letting it be the sole carrier of meaning in a sound work. That’s what I do when I construct a work’s sound. (Max Neuhaus, August 9, 1939 – February 3, 2009)
128528.biography: Max Neuhaus (US), born 1939 in Beaumont, Texas; died 2009 in Maratea, Italy. From 1957 to 1962 studied percussion under Paul Price at the Manhattan School of Music, New York. In the early 1960s gave solo concerts with artists including Pierre Boulez and Karlheinz Stockhausen in Europe and the US. Neuhaus went on to pioneer artistic activities outside conventional cultural contexts and began to realize sound works anonymously in public places, developing art forms of his own. 1966:" Listen; Public Supply", first acoustic network through a Radio Station; 1967: "Drive-In Music"; 1971-74: "Water Whistle"; 2004: "Auracle". 1977- present: first permanent sound installation "Times Square" in New York. Max Neuhaus is credited with being the first to extend sound as a primary medium into the field of contemporary art. His work has been exhibited internationally in museums and galleries, including exhibitions at the Museum of Modern Art, Whitney Museum and P.S.1 in New York; The Menil Collection; Musée d’art moderne de laville de Paris; Kunsthalle Bern and Basel; Castello di Rivoli and many others. It has also been included in Documenta VI (1977) and IX (1992), and the Venice Biennale (1999). Several of Neuhaus’s sound works are permanently installed in public venues and museums in Europe and the United States, (see: http://www.max-neuhaus.info

128580.name: TENKIPAN - Toaster to Understand Today's Weather
128580.description:
The project examines the question of how objects of daily life can be turned into information carriers. This topic is dealt with in a convincing fashion, especially because it uses the energy anyway consumed in a household to make information available for which we would normally require additional media.
Using a simple, delightful example, Tatsuya Narita (JP) demonstrates how the vision of the ubiquitous provision of information may be turned into ideas that are ready to be produced and marketed immediately: weather forecasts are received via Yahoo RSS feeds and baked onto normal, edible slices of toast—in the form of symbols that are easy to decipher (e.g., an umbrella, the sun). Without consuming extra energy, 64 pixels may be used to depict a wide range of information—turning the latest data into a “natural” component of a computer- free environment.

Links: http://cutarena.com

128584.name: Open_Sailing
128584.authors: Martin Gautron, Nasser Moustakim, Nadine Freischland, Adrien Lecuru, Rupert Spann, Narito Harada, Jorge Guberte, Yoko Kasai, Abigail Palmer, Sinta Tantra, Pano Kroko, Open_Sailing_Crew, Ollie Palmer, colet castaño, Cesar Harada, Hiromi Ozaki
128584.description:
“Open_Sailing” aims to design an attractive technological lifestyle to overcome any possible natural or man-made disaster, stimulating people’s ingenuity and sense of solidarity. Whether it is from overpopulation, global warming or energy conflicts, we are living in a time where “apocalypse” beckons. We need to collectively invent and spread bootstrapping DIY technologies for the forthcoming challenges, not only to survive but to re-invent. In the process we are developing and testing numerous novel technologies, such as Instinctive Architecture, Energy Animal and Life Cable, within an innovative nomadic ecosystem. The Swarm Search Engine is a distributed operating system that suggests a general safest location and a form for the overall structure, which constantly reconfigures itself in order to provide intelligent distribution of supplies, energy and information.
We are trying to create a truly “open architecture”. This is a drifting village of solid and comfortable shelters surrounded by flexible ocean-farming units: fluid, pre-broken, reconfigurable, sustainable, pluggable, organic and instinctive. “Open_ Sailing 02”, for five people, is about 30m in diameter.
“Open_Sailing” aims to ask questions about the way we currently inhabit our planet. Can we reach a harmonious dynamic state of interdependence with each other and the earth? Is this the next step for civilization, a natural step for post-industrialization? Will we disassociate our concept of progress from rigid infrastructure and metropolis? We believe that we can, and we are taking the first step!
We are a constantly growing, multidisciplinary, international team of about 15 people designing and engineering the prototype that is being built now in the UK, France and Morocco under the mentoring of numerous experts.

Links: www.opensailing.net/ars
128584.biography: Open_Sailing is an open-source, globally coordinated project with input from experts in many fields. The team are from a variety of backgrounds, with overall coordination by designer Cesar Harada from the Royal College of Art’s Design Interactions Lab. The core team is Hiromi Ozaki, Colet Castaño, Ollie Palmer, Martin Gautron, Nasser Moustakim, Nadine Freischland, Adrien Lecuru, Rupert Spann, Narito Harada, Jorge Guberte, Yoko Kasai, Abigail Palmer, Sinta Tantra, Pano Kroko, and many more—we’re growing every day!

128585.name: Climate Scope
128585.authors: Anu Osva, Erich Berger, Laura Beloff
128585.description:
The subject matter and conceptualization of the project “ClimateScope” by Erich Berger (AT/FI), Laura Beloff (FI) and Anu Osva (FI) illustrates an innovative and sustainable type of community building. With the long term in mind, real locations are linked to an online map and this generates a multi-dimensional representation of georeferential, environmentally relevant data, as well as stories, and building blocks of knowledge. The members of the community—potentially each and every inhabitant, as well as diverse sensor technologies— form the interface between real and virtual space.
Everyone interested participates in scientific field research on the topic of climate change and global warming by collecting, evaluating and sharing data in an active network. This input data is collected and depicted on three different levels. The first level is “Citizen Stories” and consists of personal stories, thoughts, questions, and observations by individuals on events related to climate change. The object is to achieve a level of person exchange between citizens, scientists, and politicians.
“Citizen Science” is the second level and it is being developed in collaboration with scientists. The public is requested to observe specific phenomenon in nature, like the distribution of certain plants, animals, or insects that are significant for the work of a scientist on climate change. Based on an already existing beta platform called meipi, different channels are being set up for observations at specific locations or on specific topics. Moreover, anyone can suggest new themes for channels. Hence a new kind of tool is being developed for scientists and hobby researchers, one with which the otherwise extremely timeconsuming activity of collecting field data can be distributed across a large network of participants. Crowdsourcing for the environment!
The third level—“Citizen Sensors”—is based on real-time data streams generated by networked sensors. These sensors can either be sponsored by interested companies or developed, according to building instructions that can be found on the platform for community members, as do-ityourself technology. Closely linked networks of sensors are to observe climate data in order to generate a high-resolution picture of the specific data sets for, e.g., a city. To achieve this goal, two kinds of sensors are planned: permanently installed sensors that provide a constant stream of data via WiFi, and mobile sensors for people with GPS-enabled cell phones. It will thus be possible for data to be recorded and visualized over the course of time, on the one hand; and as a spatial path through an environment, on the other.
The extreme interconnectedness of virtual and real communities in this project also raises environmental awareness and, in the form of selforganized activities and measures, makes it possible to directly push for the necessary change in human behavior.

128588.name: UbuWeb
128588.description:
“UbuWeb” is the internet’s largest site dedicated to the exhibition of avant-garde and related materials. The site currently features over 500 artists from dozens of countries and hosts nearly a terabyte of media materials. “UbuWeb” is dedicated to the free and unimpeded exhibition of materials that generally have had little traditional economic worth but which have great artistic and historic merit. Types of work featured are experimental music, sound poetry, concrete and visual poetry, full-length books of innovative writing, plays, ethnopoetics, outsider art and music, film and video, radio arts and a wealth of scholarly papers on these disciplines.
Most importantly, “UbuWeb” functions on no money: all the work is done by volunteers. Our server space and bandwidth is donated by several universities, who use “UbuWeb” as an object of study for ideas related to radical distribution and gift economies on the web. In terms of content, each section has an editor who brings to their area of expertise the site. “Ubu” is constantly being updated but the mission is different from the flotsam and jetsam of a blog; rather, we liken it to a library that is ever-expanding in uncanny— and often uncategorizable—directions. Twelve years into it, “UbuWeb” hosts over 500 artists and several thousand works of art. You’ll never find an advertisement, a logo, or a donation box. “UbuWeb” has always been and will always be free and open to all.

Links: http://ubu.com
128588.biography: UbuWeb was founded in November of 1996, initially as a repository for visual, concrete and, later, sound poetry. Over the years, UbuWeb has embraced all forms of the avant-garde and beyond. Its parameters continue to expand in all directions.

128629.name: PAD.MA
128629.description:
“Pad.ma” is an online repository of densely annotated video material, mostly footage and unfinished films. The video material is freely available for download and non-commercial reuse. The archive itself has a number of features that allow for a deep engagement with video footage: searchability, timecode-based operation, layered annotation, torrent-based downloads, maps and many other features.
“Pad.ma” is an online repository of deeply-annotated video material. It began as a way of dealing with the immense resources “left-over” from the digital film-making process, parallel to the growth of video online, in the last 10 years. “Pad.ma” thus archives (mostly uncut) footage, and unfinished films. In doing so it seeks to open up a space beyond the finite film and the online video clip, a space where video material is densely written over, debated and viewed alongside textual material. This makes it not only a technically unique database but also an unprecedented tool for documentary and film studies, image-based research, and more generally a way to handle a medium that has become “democratic”.
“Pad.ma” is a deeply collaborative effort, involving five groups and over 15 individuals in its inception stage alone. A special license (version of the GPL) has been developed for “Pad.ma‘s” video material. See http://pad.ma/faq for more. At the moment Pad.ma contains about 380 fully transcribed and annotated “events”. This is expected to grow quickly in its new phase.

Links: http://pad.ma
128629.biography: The Pad.ma project was initiated by a group consisting of oil21 .org from Berlin, the Alternative Law Forum from Bangalore and three organizations from Mumbai: Majiis, Point of View and Chitrakarkhana/CAMP.

128647.name: FLOSS Manuals
128647.description:
“FLOSS Manuals” is a collection of manuals that explain how to install and use a range of free and open-source software. The manuals are userfriendly and simple, and they are intended to encourage people to explore the wide range of free, open-source alternatives to expensive and restrictively licensed software. At “FLOSS Manuals” you can find instruction guidelines for free and open-source software such as office applications, as well as web editing and browsing and tools for playing, making, streaming and sharing audio and video.
“FLOSS Manuals” make free software more accessible by providing clear documentation that accurately explains their purpose and function. Each manual explains what the software does and what it doesn’t do, what the interface looks like, how to install it, how to set the most basic configuration necessary and how to use its main functions. To ensure the information remains useful and up to date, the manuals are regularly developed to add more advanced uses and to document changes and new versions of the software.
You can read and use the manuals in a number of different ways. They can be read online in separately indexed chapters, and you can use the website as a reference base in this way. You can also view, download or print each manual as a PDF file. It is also possible to “remix” manuals to create a version that only includes specific aspects of a particular manual or that combines chapters from two or more manuals in a single document. These can be downloaded and printed, added to websites and used for any purpose. You can also print a manual or an individually “remixed” manual, as a book via the print-to-order service of Lulu.com.
The manuals on “FLOSS Manuals” are written by a community of people who do a variety of things to keep the manuals as up to date and accurate as possible. Anyone can contribute to a manual— to fix a spelling mistake, to add a more detailed explanation, to write a new chapter or to start a whole new manual.
There are over 500 people involved. We have manuals in English, Farsi, Dutch, Spanish, Portuguese, Brazilian Portuguese, German, Catalan, Arabic, Chinese, Russian, Afrikaans, Italian and French, and soon in Hebrew

Links: http://www.flossmanuals.net
128647.biography: In 2007 Adam Hyde, a digital artist, started FLOSS Manuals with the aim of producing high-quality, free documentation that would aid in the adoption and spread of free software. Already in 2005 material was put into a wiki with the help of Aleksandar Erkalovic, and Lotte Meijer did the design. In 2006 Lotte and Adam applied for and received funding from Digital Pioneers to extend FLOSS Manuals. In 2006, FLOSS Manuals was registered as a non-profit foundation. In October 2007 we launched our website at a party at Montevideo Time Based Arts (Amsterdam). In 2008 we created the Farsi Version of FLOSS Manuals (http:// fa.flossmanuals.net) and started our first Book Sprints. Now there are over 40 manuals on free Software in English, 60 translated manuals in many languages and 500 registered contributors and a healthy and active mailing list.

128663.name: Feral Trade
128663.description:
“Feral Trade” is a public experiment in trading goods—primarily groceries—through social networks. Goods are sourced direct from their producers, using the surplus freight potential of social, peer and art-world movements, including artists’ and curatorial travel, to transport grocery products intercity. An online courier database coordinates the movements of all products and couriers and generates freight documents on the fly and a rich product biography including routes traveled, transit anecdotes and social negotiations specific to each consignment. The data collected enables the globally traveling feral trade product to conduct a broader array of information than typically relayed by products on the market.
The project was established in 2003 with the test import of 30kg coffee to the Cube Microplex (a cooperatively run cinema art space in Bristol, UK) from the Codecano coffee cooperative in El Salvador. The import was negotiated entirely through mutual acquaintances, e-mail, bank transfer and SMS. After six years in operation “Feral Trade” now forms a functioning underground freight and grocery supply network spanning the UK, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Australasia, with social connections and cultural routes as its primary mechanisms.

Links: feraltrade.org
128663.biography: Feral Trade is run by soie trader Kate Rieh and relies on the active engagement of social peers—friends, often other artists, curators and magazine editors; their interns, parents, mechanicsand bank managers—around 80 active agents and organizations who act as suppliers, hosts, couriers, depots, distributors and customers and who form the core infrastructure of the grocery business.

128671.name: Voces Bolivians
128671.description:
“Voces Bolivianas” (Bolivian Voices) is a projectthat teaches the use of citizen media such as blogs, digital photos and videos to under-represented groups in Bolivia. These groups include indigenous groups, women and groups from the rural areas. These new bloggers become a part of the Bolivian blogosphere, where they connect with other Bolivians regardless of ethnic, geographic or class lines. This creates a digitalcommunity based upon mutual respect and understanding, something that is difficult to establish in “real life”.
The common goal of “Voces Bolivianas” is to teach the use of citizen media to under- represented groups so that they can become a part of the local, national, and global conversation. The internet can become a great equalizer in a very polarized country. It allows people regardless of ethnic, racial, geographic or class lines to connect with one another without the filter or stereotypes often found in Bolivia.
The project finds way to connect the community virtually but also physically. In January 2009, “Voces Bolivianas” organized its first summit, where 27 members of the community from across the country came together in the city of Cochabamba to meet and learn from one another. They also took part in a planning session to determine the project’s future.

Links: http://www.vocesbolivianas.org
128671.biography: Voces Bolivianas started in September 2007 with a series of workshops in El Alto, Bolivia, with young people of Aymara descent. Each of the participants created and maintained their own personal blogs, which allows them to express themselves and represent their own communities. The project started with a small start-up grant from Rising Voices, but is now operating on many hours of volunteer labor. From there, interest grew and with the help of volunteer bloggers it spread to other cities across the country including six of the country’s nine departments.

128680.name: Ashoka's Changemakers
128680.description:
Building on Ashoka’s 26-year history of discovering and funding social innovators, “Changemakers” developed an online community to expand the search for social solutions. Originally based solely around online competitions, in response to our community’s needs we are now building a set of tools so that our community can continue to engage and communicate beyond and outside of the competition process.
“Changemakers” is a global community of social innovators seeking to discover the cutting-edge innovators from around the world. We have built the world’s first global online open-source community that competes to discover the best social solutions, and then collaborates to refine, enrich and implement those solutions. “Changemakers” begins by providing an overarching intellectual framework for collaborative competitions that bring together individual social change initiatives into a more powerful whole.
To keep the framework dynamic, the online “Changemakers” community identifies and selects the best solutions and helps refine them. The result is global action frameworks, drawing on the work of social entrepreneurs, which seed collaborative action and visibility on a global scale— making a big difference, field by field.
The Open Sourcing Social Solutions model aims to challenge the traditional focus of issues such as human trafficking and conflict resolution with a broader, more complete set of stakeholders. As such, each one serves as a platform for building a practitioner- and investor-engaged community that sparks new waves of innovation around problems stuck on conventional approaches.
As the diverse group of stakeholders come together and see the way their work and concerns overlap and inspire each other, unexpected and important outcomes typically ensue, which the “Changemakers” model makes possible but could never predict.
“Changemakers”‘ collaborative competitions have produced new partnerships between India’s largest bank and one of India’s largest rural women’s programs; the connection of thousands of rural farmers to low-cost healthcare providers; and the scaling of an affordable Thai housing solution by the world’s largest cement manufacturer. These are just three examples that represent the strength inherent in a change-making community. And they signal the way an entire sector can broaden its focus and integrate a powerful set of solutions and stakeholders bent on change.

Links: http://changemakers.net
128680.biography: Changemakers is a global team of approximately 30 individuals. We have a global community of 60,000 registered users, who range from grassroots innovators to professional organizations working on solutions to pressing global needs.

128684.name: Canchas. spontaneous soccer fields.
128684.description:
“Canchas” is an anthropological, social and cultural project combining multimedia and local stories to describe “spontaneous soccer fields and their human side” around the world. It is an open and international project to find a new medium of meeting and exchange. It can be seen as one response to the latest trends in the content and web field to combine art, sport and culture in a modern and participative way—online and virtual. The project addresses everybody who is interested in human stories and cultures, in traveling or soccer, in participating or just watching.
The multi-language website www.canchas.org has been online since November 2007. Its 2,700 pictures, 30 video and audio reports from 180 people in 100 countries make “Canchas” the biggest archive of pictures and stories of common soccer in the world.
During the 2008 European Cup, an exhibition was held at the Uefa Fan Camp with up 5 x 3-meter pictures. There was a street performance and various media actions (postcards, competitions) and “Canchas” pictures were digitally presented at public events in Vienna and Innsbruck. Various media in Germany, Austria and Argentina reported the project, and cooperation with journals and newspapers guarantees an ongoing media presence.
The “Canchas” is supervised by international media and IT experts of the proLoka NGO (www. proLoka.org). ProLoka works worldwide in the fields of media and culture, among others, with Unicef and on EU projects.
“Canchas” will organize a series of projects in connection with the 2010 soccer World Cup in South Africa, internationally and on site. Projects comprise interactive exhibitions, a documentary film, a book, art performances, presentations of “Canchas” of all 64 African countries around the globe and alternative live reporting during the World Cup. From March to October 2009 the project will be presented to selected partners in the fields of media, sponsoring and equipment.

Links: www.canchas.org
128684.biography: The Canchas project was started in 2004 by Andreas Matt and Gaston Silberman, sharing the same enthusiasm about humans being connected through one theme (i.e. football) and stories around common topics (i.e. spontaneous football fields) all around the world. Since November 2007 the multi-language website www.canchas.org has been online. 2,700 pictures, 30 video and audio reports from 180 people in 100 countries were submitted by scouts, mainly from Europe (Austria, Germany, Switzerland, France, Spain), South America (Argentina) and some African and Asian countries (Mozambique, Morocco, Pakistan).

128696.name: WikiLeaks
128696.description:
WikiLeaks is developing an uncensorable Wikipedia for untraceable mass document leaking and analysis. Our primary interest is in exposing oppressive regimes in Asia, the former Soviet bloc, Sub-Saharan Africa and the Middle East, but we are of assistance to people of nations who wish to reveal unethical behavior in their governments and corporations. We aim for maximum political impact. Our interface is identical to Wikipedia’s and usable by all types of people. We have received over 1.2 million documents so far from dissident communities and anonymous sources.
We believe that transparency in government activities leads to reduced corruption, better government and stronger democracies. All governments can benefit from increased scrutiny by the world community, as can their own people. We believe this scrutiny requires information. Historically that information has been costly—in terms of human life and human rights. But with technological advances—the internet and cryptography— the risks of conveying important information can be lowered. WikiLeaks opens leaked documents up to stronger scrutiny than any media organization or intelligence agency can provide. WikiLeaks provides a forum for the entire global community to relentlessly examine any document for its credibility, plausibility, veracity and validity. Communities can interpret leaked documents and explain their relevance to the public. If a document comes from the Chinese government, the entire Chinese dissident community and diaspora can freely scrutinize and discuss it; if a document arrives from Iran, the entire Farsi community can analyze it and put it in context.
In its landmark ruling on the Pentagon Papers, the US Supreme Court ruled that “only a free and unrestrained press can effectively expose deception in government.” We agree. We believe that it is not only the people of one country that keep their government honest, but also the people of other countries who are watching that government. That is why the time has come for an anonymous global avenue for disseminating documents the public should see.

Links: http://wikileaks.org
128696.biography: WikiLeaks was founded by Chinese dissidents, journalists, mathematicians and start-up company technologists from the US, Taiwan, Europe, Australia and South Africa. The WikiLeaks team is made up of internationally recognized technologists, legal and anti-corruption experts as well as accredited journalists. The WikiLeaks advisory board includes figures with unparalleled political and technical credentials and its members represent every populated continent.

128710.name: Wikiartpedia-La Libera Enciclopedia dell'Arte e le Culture delle Reti Telematiche
128710.description:
“Wikiartpedia” is a free encyclopedia of art and network cultures. It focuses on net art, digital art, media art, hacktivism and digital culture, but also on all the other ambits of art and culture that are increasingly connected to them in the past and present.
“Wikiartpedia” is an open instrument to write and read, in which every net user can participate writing new entries or modifying the existing ones. The result is something that goes beyond the addition of the individual knowledge of the participants, because it adds the implicit negotiation of a common agreement about the significance of every single item.
The “Wikiartpedia” model is pluralist in order to provide information free of censorship, which is therefore fluid and negotiable.
“Wikiartpedia” is part of the Center for Research and Documentation on Art and Network cultures— uCAN (pronounced “you can”), which Tommaso Tozzi runs at the Academy of Fine Arts of Carrara, whose aim is the research, documentation and promotion of this field of culture through the free participation of the users.
Students from Tommaso Tozzi’s classes write the entries for the encyclopedia. Through this, the results of the online creations of the New Technology Art School (three-year course in multimedia arts and two-year course in net art and digital) of the university and of the other schools are interconnected with the network and at the same time become the instrument for the following students to learn and create new knowledge.
A new culture is coming into existence, which, though interconnected with the global culture of the network, is assuming its own physiognomy and the specific local character of the community of the school. This culture is in part characterized by the real relationships and in part distributed in the virtual archives and relationships. The local community of the school renders and participates in the global community, providing the results of its studies on the net, free and without any conditions.
The contents of the encyclopedia are mainly the result of students’ research. So far, about 1,000 students have been involved and there are 1,500 users of “Wikiartpedia”.

Links: www.wikiartpedia.org
128710.biography: Wikiartpedia continues the experience that began with BBS Hacker Art, founded by Tommaso Tozzi in 1990 and continued in 1993 with the Fiorence-based Strano network’s activity on communication, art and digital rights. In 1997 Tommaso Tozzi started Web Disk—Una Bio-Enciclopedia (http://www.strano.net/wd/welcome.html), which continues from 2000 in the Hacker Art website (http://www.hackerart.org) and from the 2002 in the online database Archivio Hacker Art (http://www.ecn.org/ hackerart), also created by Tommaso Tozzi. He started the Wikiartpedia project in 2004, hosted in the European Counter Network (http://www.ecn.org) Server with the collaboration of the people at ECN. Since 2004 many of the old entries in the Hacker Art Archive and others of Tozzi’s projects have been moved to the new Wikiartpedia, a transfer that is still continuing.

128759.name: female:pressure
128759.description:
"female:pressure" is an international database for female djs, producers and visual artists, related to the electronic music world, that can be searched by various criteria. It is first and foremost a tool to ensure the existence of women in this apparently entirly male dominated field and to improve communication. The database / website is considered to be a publicly accessible source of information. Meanwhile "female:pressure" can be proud of approximately 1030 members from 52 countries, most of them can be contacted by e-mail and are hyperlinked to their own webpages and to the record labels they release on where applicable. Additional information comprises location, profession and musical style.
"Why are there so few female activists in the electronic music scene?"—each one of the listed artists has heard this question a hundred times. However, experience demonstrates that women are not less active. Their activities are just less recognized and also easily forgotten.
"female:pressure" emphasizes the practicality and the necessity of networking and communicating especially in this area and serves as a representational platform to the world, an established standard to be consulted and used as a reference. The database can be searched by regions, countries, styles, professions and names. This makes it easy for people to obtain information about well known artists as well as up-and-coming women who work in the fields of electronic music around the globe.
All djs, producers, singers, mcs, videoartists, graphicdesigners, photographers and other visual artists can log into the site and individually update their own profiles, so the information available remains relevant and can be used effectively.

Links: http://www.femalepressure.net/
128759.biography: female:pressure has been designed and founded by Vienna based Electric Indigo in 1998 as a technological answer to the recurring complaints of there hardly being any female producers or djs. The programming and continuous advancement of the female:pressure database has been carried out by Viennese open source expert Andrea Mayr.

128763.name: Maneno
128763.description:
In Swahili, “maneno” means “words”. Words form the core of everything important to “Maneno”, a site built completely from the ground up to be a blogging and communication platform to meet the needs of the Sub-Saharan blogger and writer. But why yet another blogging system when there are so many already? Of the total number of users on the internet, only 1 percent are from Africa, and of that amount even fewer are bloggers. Maneno is working to overcome what other systems see as nuisances, converting them into the foundation of a powerful content-delivery system for Sub-Saharan Africa.
Initially based upon a lightweight framework created and personally used by the founders, “Maneno” was founded in 2008. It allows those with limited or narrow-bandwidth internet to use a system that is lightweight and straightforward in functionality. But while being fast to access, “Maneno” is also a system that is full-featured and gives those who join the ability to have their own, personalized space on it, writing in a way that is as unrestricted as they see fit.
On a continent with over 2,000 languages, crosscommunication is an issue that is often forgotten about. “Maneno” is a system where multiplelanguage versions for articles can sit on top of one another for immediate access. The interface for the site has also been also translated in to as many languages as possible to remove linguistic barriers, which are seen more and more in an increasingly Anglophonic web.
Constantly building upon these cornerstones, “Maneno” strives to be a continually free system that aggregates and promotes the content within it so that those using it are not just writing in a vacuum but for an audience.

Links: www.maneno.org
128763.biography: Maneno’s board of directors are Rebecca Wanjiku, a journalist and blogger from Kenya (http://dispatchesfromafrica.maneno. org), Elia Varela Serra, a journalist and photographer (http://twiga.maneno.org), and Saul Wainwright, a South African with experience as a finance manager, a researcher and strategist. Miquel Hudin Balsa, a web developer, leads technology development (http://subsaharska.maneno.org).

128772.name: Mute - Culture and Politics after the Net
128772.description:
“Mute” is a hybrid print and online magazine dedicated to exploring culture and politics after the net. The publication has existed in print (with a series of accompanying websites) since 1994 but in 2006 it relaunched as “Volume 2” to permit a more dynamic and community-oriented publishing model. At its new location, Metamute. org, “Mute” now manages several types of commissioned and open-publishing content. These run in parallel and feed into a quarterly print title, Mute, which is available for sale or free-to-download in PDF form.
“Mute‘s” primary activity consists of researching and commissioning articles around thematic clusters (the knowledge commons; the global expansion of slums; web 2.0). This thematic editorial is complemented by reviews—of exhibitions, books, conferences, music etc. The magazine also manages several open-submissions areas, namely News & Analysis (where users can highlight and annotate external articles, or indeed publish texts of their own), an image gallery (where users can submit works related to print-issue themes), a calendar (where events can be submitted) and a “torrent” (the Public Library), where larger media files can be up/down-loaded.
Finally, “Mute” has started extending the capabilities of the print-on-demand technologies it uses for its own print magazine to its user-base. Currently, this means users can compile their own Mute by grouping and sequencing articles from anywhere on the site, have them sequenced, enhanced with a table of contents and formatted as PDFs. Over the longer term we aim for this process to make a fully-designed PDF available, which is automatically sent to print and then sent to the user’s registered address.
In line with this the magazine has developed a series of ancillary software projects, all of which attempt to share lessons learned or knowledge gained, tackling the practical issues involved in creating and distributing the magazine. To date, these include Openmute.org (a portal for microsites grouping collaborative-working tools), a print-on-demand consultancy (currently processing an average of three books per month), a print-on-demand gateway (in development at Picopress.net) and an alternative distribution site for independent media (in development at Moreismore. net).

Links: http://www.metamute.org
128772.biography: Mute magazine was founded as an art and technology newspaper in 1994 by Pauline van Mourik Broekman and Simon Worthington but, after four successive format changes, now exists as a hybrid web-print publication at http://www.metamute. org.

128779.name: Piratbyrån
128779.description:
“Piratbyrån” (The Bureau for Piracy) might internationally be best known for starting up The Pirate Bay, which is now the world's largest bittorrent tracker and the subject of a controversial court case. (“The Pirate Bay” has long since been an independent entity, even if collaborating closely with “Piratbyrån”).
While to some extent powered by the brute force of (“The Pirate Bay”, “Piratbyrån” has established itself as a blend of theorists, artists, consultants, activists and pranksters, not only influencing Swedish opinions, decision-makers and initiatives but also more and more participating in formulating European discourses on topics that not only include file-sharing alone but the larger impact of digital information abundance on the creation of cultural meaning, cultural production and economics and urban life.
One basic assumption of “Piratbyrån's” works is that copying is a fact. The files have already been downloaded and uploaded. We live in an age of cultural abundance, of anything which can be digitalized, which makes it an urgent and exciting task to explore the heterogenous possibilities of creating meaning and economies by connecting this digital abundance to what is not really abundant, like time and space. Thus, one objective is really about re-exploring the notion of performative value, as an alternative to the “creative industries” ideology which tends to reduce culture just to “content”.
At the same time, “Piratbyrån” is ceaselessy scrutinizing the role of copyright enforcement today, developing critiques of how it evolves into new mechanisms for control of the very infrastructure of the internet, and how it tends to move from the level of actual copyrighted data towards the level of metadata, tools and protocols. An area of special interest has always been on the grey zones of copyright, as it is today very clear that copyright in the digital realm operates more by inserting uncertainty and fear than by imposing a blackand- white scheme of legal and illegal. “Piratbyrån” is not focused on reforming (or abolishing) copyright law, even if we are frequently collaborating with people working in that direction, including Swedish mainstream politicians from a number of parties.

Links: http://www.piratbyran.org http://thepiratebay.org
128779.biography: Piratbyran (SE). The most active members are a motley crew consisting of up to a dozen people with very different backgrounds (hacking, horses, music, philosophy, art, etc.), the majority having been in the project since the beginning. Depending on different projects, an outer circle of supporting personnel are involved. But Piratbyrän shoudn’t be viewed as an organization fueling its own process. Rather Piratbyrän mostly operates via interventions, collaborations and inspirations.

128803.name: Buddytown
128803.description:
Zu meinem sechsten Geburtstag bekam ich eine SNES- (Super Nintendo Entertainment System)-Konsole geschenkt. Ich war begeistert von Mario, Yoshi, Luigi und den anderen Nintendo-Charakteren, doch bald begann ich zu hinterfragen, wie ein solches Spiel funktioniert. Ich habe heute noch Skizzen von damals. Mit zehn kaufte ich mir den „Game Maker Pro“ – eine Game-Design-Umgebung für DOS-Spiele. Als Windows XP kam und damit DOS kaum noch verfügbar war, wurde der Game Maker uninteressant. Ich stieg auf Dark Basic um und lernte MilkShape 3D. Mit dem Release von Windows Vista entschied ich mich, auf Mac OS X umzusteigen. Ich konzentrierte mich auf Flash und lernte ActionScript. Die Teilnahme an u19 war dann ausschlaggebend dafür, die Idee „Buddytown“ umzusetzen. „Buddytown.at“ ist ein Mix aus Online-Spiel, RPG (Role Playing Game), Simulation und Social Network. Alle Szenen und Buddies wurden in CINEMA 4D gerendert. „Buddytown“ ist eine Metropole irgendwo im Ozean auf einer Insel. Sie ist die Hauptstadt von „Buddyland“ und der Treffpunkt für alle jungen Buddies.

Links: www.buddytown.at
128803.biography: Daniel Stocker, geb. 1991, besuchte von 2001 bis 2005 das Realgymnasium Schwaz Lebende Fremdsprache Französisch und seit 2005 bis heute (Abschluss 2010) die HBLA-West Innsbruck Medieninformatik.

128817.name: European II Ways
128817.description: Nachdem man in vier europäischen Großstädten Eintrittskarten zu kulturellen Ereignissen gesammelt hat schafft man es mit etwas Glück und Geschick in das kulturelle Zentrum Europas – Linz 2009 Kulturhauptstadt Europas. Nach einem Klick auf die Europakarte startet das Spiel im 1. Level, Athen. Zwischen Akropolis und anderen antiken Sehenswürdigkeiten sucht man nach Eintrittskarten und sammelt diese. Dabei muss man sich allerdings, wie jeder Tourist, vor den Menschenmassen in Acht nehmen. Hat man alle zehn Eintrittskarten gesammelt, kommt man nach Madrid von dort aus weiter nach London und Berlin. Gespielt wird zwischen Häusern und Sehenswürdigkeiten, wie etwa dem Berliner Fernsehturm. Ziel ist das kulturelle Zentrum Linz 2009 Kulturhauptstadt Europas. In diesem Bonuslevel versucht man, zwischen Nibelungenbrücke und dem Donauhafen wie auch in den Levels davor den Menschenmassen auszuweichen und genügend Eintrittskarten zu sammeln.
128817.biography: Franz Fellinger, geb. 1993 in Linz, 6. Klasse im Kollegium Aloisianum. Schon immer hatte ich Interesse im Bereich Technik. Mein Interesse in Richtung Computer erweckte ein langjähriger Freund, der mich auch in die Kunst des Grafikdesigns und Web-Development eingeführt hat. Außerdem fühle ich mich in den Bergen wohl. Im Winter fahre ich gerne Schi und mache gerne die eine oder andere Schitour. Im Sommer wandere ich gerne.

128834.name: Robot Control with Mobile Phone Motion
128834.description:
Schon im Laborunterricht des 4. Jahrganges hat meine Klasse Übungen mit dem frei in C programmierbaren und käuflich zu erwerbenden Asuro-Roboter (Another Small and Unique Robot from Oberpfaffenhofen) durchgeführt. Während dieser Übungen kam mir die Idee, diesen über ein Handy zu steuern – daraus wurde mein Maturaprojekt.
Mithilfe der „Mobile Sensor API (JSR256)“ ist es möglich, über ein Handy bestimmte Sensorwerte, wie zum Beispiel die aktuelle Beschleunigung in jede Achsenrichtung, auszulesen. Weiters untersuchte ich die „Contactless Communication API (JSR257)“, welche es erlaubt, über das Handy mit RFID-Tags zu kommunizieren. Ziel dieses Projekts war es, den Asuro-Roboter durch eine möglichst einfache und intuitive Bewegungssteuerung eines Mobiltelefons in die gewünschte Richtung zu lenken. Außerdem vibriert bei einer Kollision des Asuro-Roboters das Mobiltelefon, ähnlich wie bei Konsolencontrollern.
128834.biography: Leo Höckner, geb. 1990, besucht die HTL Braunau, Abteilung Elektronik/Technische Informatik, Ausbildungszweig Mobile Computing & Software Engineering. Er hat u. a. ein Praktikum bei Comneon - An Infineon Technologies Company gemacht.

128835.name: Sieben auf einen Streich
128835.description: Die Kinder der dritten und vierten Schulstufe haben im und außerhalb des Unterrichts kleine Programme gestaltet. Ich als Lehrer bin im Internet zufällig auf die Programmierumgebung „Scratch“ gestoßen. „Scratch“ ist eine kostenlose grafische Programmierumgebung für Kinder ab acht Jahren und ist für Windows und Mac OS X verfügbar. Sie wird von der Lifelong Kindergarten Group des Media Lab am MIT entwickelt und ermöglicht einen einfachen Einstieg in die Grundkonzepte des Programmierens. Ich habe mit den Kindern zuerst die „Scratchcards“ bearbeitet und dann versucht, sie zu eigenen Projekten anzuleiten. Einige Kinder haben sofort begonnen, selbstständig interaktive Programme zu entwickelt, andere haben die vorgegebenen Scripte abgewandelt und so die eigenen Ideen umgesetzt. Schon nach kurzer Zeit waren Einzelne unter ihnen „Experten“, die allen anderen mit Rat und Hilfe zur Seite standen. Ein Kind kam an einem Morgen in die Schule und begann gleich zu arbeiten: „Mir ist daheim noch eingefallen, wie ich es noch lösen könnte. Das möchte ich jetzt ausprobieren.“
128835.biography: Unsere Schule wird zweiklassig geführt. Die Kinder, die sich an diesem Projekt beteiligt haben, sind im Schuljahr 2008/09 in der 3. bzw. 4. Schulstufe. Sie haben sich im Unterricht und manchmal auch nachmittags mit der Programmierumgebung Scratch beschäftigt.

128836.name: Sound Machines
128836.description:
Die 5A der HLW des Schulvereins der Kreuzschwestern entwickelte 16 individuelle, höchst unterschiedliche „Sound Machines“. Diese kleinen interaktiven Arbeiten wurden mit Flash programmiert und funktionieren in jedem Browser. Der User kann mit unterschiedlichen Geräuschen und Musikfragmenten experimentieren, es geht darum, diese zu ordnen, neu zu arrangieren und damit zu komponieren.
In einem Zeitalter des Remixens können wir uns selbst als DJs versuchen. Erleichtert wird uns der Zugang durch verschiedene Sound-Muster, eine Visualisierung des Gehörten – jeder wird etwas finden, das ihn/sie anspricht, vom „Fäden ziehen“ über Jodeln in den Bergen, Harfe spielen oder der allseits beliebten Jukebox, bis hin zu Scratching an den Turntables ist hier alles dabei, was ein wahres Musikerherz erfreut. Der Gruppe von SchülerInnen geht es neben dem möglichst intuitiven Mixen von Klängen aber vor allem auch um den spielerischen Umgang mit Lizenzrechten.
128836.biography: Die Projektgruppe besteht aus 16 Schülerinnen aus dem 4. Jahrgang der HLW für Kommunikations- und Mediendesign am Schulzentrum der Kreuzschwestern in Linz.

128837.name: In den Tiefen
128837.description:
Eines Tages habe ich auf meinem Computer ein Programm entdeckt – Cinema 4D. Neugierig habe ich dieses geöffnet und versucht, etwas damit zu modellieren. Als ich herausfand, dass man dort auch Animationen machen kann, wollte ich unbedingt einen Film damit gestalten. Doch bald musste ich feststellen, dass das extrem viel Arbeit bedeutet. Daher habe ich nach Unterstützung gesucht. Ich konnte einen Freund von dieser Idee überzeugen und zeigte ihm, was ich bereits über Cinema 4D wusste. Ein Film über Außerirdische, das war unser Ziel. Da wir aber viele Dinge nicht umsetzen konnten, haben wir nach etwas Einfacherem gesucht. Da kam uns der Ozean als Schauplatz für unsere Handlung gerade recht. Ich schrieb ein Drehbuch, doch beim Animieren selbst wurde dann improvisiert. Mein Freund modellierte zwei Fische, der Rest kam von mir.
„In den Tiefen“ handelt von drei Fischen, die, dem ewigen Dunkel der Tiefsee überdrüssig, zur Suche nach Licht aufbrechen. Genauer, nach dem geheimnisumwitterten „Großen Licht“, das sich irgendwo weit über ihnen befinden soll. Auf dem Weg dorthin treffen die drei einen Clownfisch, der sie auf die Gefahren hinweist, die ihnen oben durch den Menschen drohen. Alle Warnungen in den Wind schlagend, setzen die drei ihren Weg fort. An der Oberfläche angekommen, werden ihnen die Rümpfe und Schiffsschrauben der vorbeischnellenden Tanker beinahe zum Verhängnis, doch alles geht gut, und endlich blicken die drei ins gleißend helle Weiß der Sonne. Kurz entschlossen, das „Große Licht“ mit in die Tiefsee zu nehmen, schießen sie eine Harpune nach der Sonne und beginnen, diese nach unten zu ziehen. Kaum eingetaucht ins Nass des Meeres, erlischt die leuchtende Kugel, und den drei Freunden bleibt nur die Rückkehr ins ewige Dunkel der heimatlichen Tiefsee.
128837.biography: Matej Petrek, geb. 1991 in Bratislava, besucht seit 2002 das Gymnasium in Bratislava. Derzeit ist er in der 7. Klasse (die gleichzeitig die 6. Klasse des Bundesrealgymnasiums in Bruck an der Leitha ist). Er interessiert sich für Sport (Tischtennis, Fußball, Schifahren) Computer (Cinema 4D,Gimp) sowie Malen und Zeichnen.

128861.name: Having A Wonderful Time
128861.description:
„Having A Wonderful“ Time ist ein comichaftes, animiertes Musikvideo zu einer gleichnamigen Nummer von Herberto Buckingham Khaury, besser bekannt als Tiny Tim. Der 1996 verstorbene US-amerikanische Popmusiker und Entertainer gilt als eine der schillerndsten und zugleich obskursten Gestalten der Popgeschichte.
Im Sommer 2007 habe ich mit der Arbeit zu diesem Streifen begonnen. Mein Interesse galt der verrückten chaotischen Seele des Liedes, die ich in ein animiertes Video zu übertragen versuchte. Als ich „Having A Wonderful Time“ zum ersten Mal hörte, war ich erstaunt, welch extrem gute Laune ich danach genoss. Es ist ein Lied, das Menschen immer glücklich machen wird und ein ungeheures Suchtpotenzial aufweist. Ich versuchte, diese Wirkung durch meinen Flash-Cartoon noch zu verstärken. Er soll genauso schnell und verrückt sein wie das Lied selbst.
128861.biography: Tarek Kalifa, geb. 1991, besucht seit 2002 das Amerlinggymnasium in Wien.

128908.name: IOCC - Die Polizei im Rennen gegen die Zeit
128908.authors: David Wurm, Alexander Niederklapfer, Magdalena Wurm, Ehrentraud Hager, Krmpf Krmpf
128908.description:
Im Herbst 2006 begannen wir, die Geschichte zu entwickelten, vor allem unter technischen Gesichtspunkten: was drehen, was ausprobieren. Die Idee, Legomännchen auch auf dem Wasser agieren zu lassen bzw. Szenen mit Feuer einzubauen, entstand relativ bald. Dem Genre nach ist IOCC ein – wie wir es nennen – Miniblockbuster.
Im Film geht es um eine Verbrecherorganisation (IOCC), die die Londoner Polizei auf die Schaufel nimmt. Eine E-Mail kündigt die Sprengung des Big Ben in der Silvesternacht an. Der Hintergrund ist jedoch ein anderer: der Geburtstag des Polizeipräsidenten am 1. Jänner, jedes Jahr kommt zu diesem Anlass ein „Geschenk“ der IOCC. Sie gibt vor, den Big Ben sprengen zu wollen, in Wirklichkeit aber hat sie es auf das Auto des Polizeipräsidenten abgesehen. Der Big Ben wird nur angehalten (genau um Mitternacht). Die Polizei hat sich mit ihren Sicherheitsmaßnahmen so sehr darauf konzentriert, dass es der IOCC gelingt, das Auto des Polizeipräsidenten zu sprengen.
Der Film besteht aus über 17.000 Einzelbildern, die zu einem flüssigen Film mit durchschnittlich 16 Bildern/ Sekunde zusammengefügt wurden.
128908.biography: Die Krmpf Krmpf Studios, das sind Magdalena Wurm, Ehrentraud Hager, David Wurm und Alexander Niederklapfer. Das erste Filmprojekt war „Abenteuer - Arbeitsweg“, mit dem das Team die Goldene Nica von u19 - freestyle computing aus 2006 gewann. David und Magdalena besuchen beide das BRG Fadingerstraße, Ehrentraud geht in die Kreuzschwesternschule in Linz, und Alexander ist Schüler des Petrinums in Linz.

128931.name: Music Robot
128931.description:
Vor etwa einem Jahr habe ich begonnen, mir das Programm Maya selbst durch Tutorials aus dem Netz beizubringen, ein halbes Jahr später machte ich das gleiche mit dem digitalen Synthesizer-Programm Reason. Da Musik und 3D-Animation zu meinen Hobbys gehören, hat es nicht lange gedauert, bis mir die Idee kam, diese beiden Bereiche zu kombinieren.
Zu Beginn stand für mich im Vordergrund, ein gutes Konzept für den Charakter zu erstellen. Meine Ideen begann ich mit Bleistift zu visualisieren. Die Musik entstand vorerst unabhängig vom Film in Reason. Die Skelettierung und Modellierung des Roboters war mit Maya relativ leicht. Schwierig war vor allem die Animation, ich hatte vorher noch nie Video mit Audio synchronisiert. Indem ich mich selbst durch all die auftauchenden Probleme gekämpft habe, konnte ich viele neue Erfahrungen sammeln. Jetzt bin ich stolz darauf, dass ich das trotz so vieler Hindernisse geschafft habe.
128931.biography: Johannes Masanz, geb. 1990, besucht seit 2000 das Bundesrealgymnasium „Auf der Schmelz“ in Wien. Seine Hobbys sind Sport, 3D-Design, Musik. Johannes möchte einmal als 3D-Designer arbeiten.

128951.name: Semantic Tag Cloud
128951.description:
Im Internet kommt es zu einer Dateninflation – nie zuvor standen so viele Informationen zur Verfügung und nie war es so schwierig, daraus das wirklich Relevante zu filtern. Neue Technologien, basierend auf aktuellen Forschungen in der Informatik, werden es für die Benutzer künftig einfacher machen, genau die Information zu finden, die sie tatsächlich brauchen. Wie der Informatik-Visionär Stephen Wolfram in seinem Blog zur kommenden Super-Suchmaschine (Wolfram|Alpha) schreibt, ist es dazu notwendig, Methoden und Modelle zu finden, um die Billionen vorliegender Textdaten mathematisch verarbeitbar zu machen. Ausgehend von dieser Vision haben wir in unserem Projekt eine mathematische Verarbeitung von Kundenrezensionen von Online-Shops entwickelt, die es dem Benutzer ermöglicht, aus einer Vielzahl rein textueller, qualitativer Aussagen (z. B. „Der Sound ist super“) eine quantitative Bewertung eines Produktmerkmals (Sound: 9/10 Punkte) zu erhalten.

Links: wechselwirkungen.biz/stc/
128951.biography:
Jasmin Haider, geb. 1998, war von April 2008 bis September 2008 außerordentliche Studentin an der TU Wien (Medizinische Informatik) und hat 2009 ihre Matura an der HTL Donaustadt in Wien gemacht.

Sinja Hemer, geb. 1990, beginnt ihr Studium an der FH Wien am Währinger Gürtel für die Studienrichtung Journalismus und Medienmanagement.

129072.name: Lego Chemie
129072.description: Zehn SchülerInnen der 2. Klasse Hauptschule mit dem Schwerpunkt BioTeC (Biologie, Technik und Computer) haben sich freiwillig gemeldet, beim Projekt „Messroboter“ mitzumachen. Ziel war es, gemeinsam einen Roboter zu konstruieren, der eine farblose Flüssigkeit auf ihren pH-Wert überprüft und dann entweder dem Platz „sauer“, „neutral“ oder „basisch“ zuordnet. Dieses Unternehmen hat sich als schwerer als gedacht herausgestellt, und wir mussten uns schlussendlich mit der Möglichkeit der Farbzuordnung begnügen. Aber auch das war Herausforderung genug. Die Programmierung und Konstruktion von einfachen Lego-Robotern wurde im Unterricht der 1. und 2. Klasse besprochen und geübt. Jetzt galt es nur noch, die Chemie mit den Messgeräten und den Lego-Teilen zu kombinieren. Und natürlich das fehlende Chemiewissen aufzuholen.
129072.biography: An der Dr.-Aloys-Weißenbach-Hauptschule in Telfs gibt es seit 2003 den Schwerpunkt BioTeC (Biologie, Technik, Computer). In diesen Klassen haben die Schülerlnnen Biologie, Physik, lnformatik und NKP(Naturkundliches Praktikum)von der 1. bis zur 4. Klasse. Lego-Roboter bauen und programmieren findet im Schulfach NKP statt. Für das Projekt „Lego Chemie" meldeten sich freiwillig zehn SchülerInnen, und diese verbrachten 32 Stunden außerhalb der Unterrichtszeit mit der Entwicklung des Roboters.

129090.name: CityFlow - Urban Climate Simulation
129090.authors: Andreas Mursch-Radlgruber, Oliver Spies, Michael Kappel, Stefan Pozar
129090.description:
Metropolen sind konstruierte Welten, in denen der Mensch seine Umwelt selbst bestimmt, leider nicht immer zum Besten. Die Idee, eine spielerische, leicht verständliche Stadtklima-Simulation zu entwickeln und als Matura-Projekt umzusetzen, wurde inspiriert durch einen Professor an der Universität für Bodenkultur Wien.
Mit „CityFlow – Urban Climate Simulation“ wollen wir vor allem eines, Interesse an der oft unterschätzten Thematik „Klimaschutz im urbanen Raum“ wecken. Mit dem 3D-Stadt-Editor lässt sich schnell und einfach ein Stadtteil mit einem selbst erweiterbaren Baukasten aus zusammenhängenden Geometrien (z. B. Bäume, Parks, komplexere Gebäude usw.) erstellen. Auch Oberflächeneigenschaften können rasch definiert und geändert werden. Mit einem Klick kann die erstellte Umgebung simuliert und analysiert werden. Man erhält innerhalb von Sekunden die sich aus der gewählten Struktur ergebende Klimaänderung.
129090.biography: Stefan Pozar, Michael Kappel, Andreas Mursch-Radlgruber, Oliver Spies - 5. Klasse HTL für Informationstechnologie, TGM - Die Schule der Technik, Wien. Alle vier scheinen für alles offen zu sein, aber für nichts Zeit zu haben: vom Schi- und Radfahren über Schwimmen, Reiten, Kunst, Kultur und Architektur bis zum Fotografieren, 3D-Modellieren, Computerspielen oder Animationen erstellen.

129108.name: Melt
129108.description:
Ich hab die Idee solange in meinem Kopf herumgetragen und alles genau geplant, so sehr, dass die Bilder, die ich jetzt mit Müh und Not erschaffen habe, dagegen eigentlich nur ein Schatten, ein schwaches Abbild sind.
Ich stellte mir eine Welt aus Eis vor, alle Menschen sind erstarrt. Nur ein Mädchen nicht, sie findet Eislaufschuhe. Und weil man beim Eislaufen eine Spur hinterlässt, hab ich mir vorgestellt, sollten es zauberhafte Eislaufschuhe sein, in deren Spur alles wegschmilzt. Man sollte Menschen sehen, die wieder zu leben beginnen, die erwachen, als wäre alles nur ein Traum. Ich hab den ganzen Tag gezeichnet, in der Schule, zu Hause, immer, wenn Gelegenheit war. Ich hab versucht, möglichst viel Abwechslung reinzubringen, also nicht nur Zeichnungen, auch Fotos, Gefilmtes, Gemaltes. Erst am Ende dreht sich die Eisläuferin um und sieht, was sie „angerichtet“ hat. Alles ist erwacht, aufgebrochen, kein Eis mehr zu sehen. Mein Gedanke war, es ist doch ein ewiger Kreislauf, wo Leben entsteht, muss auch eines enden.
129108.biography: Nana Susanne Thurner, geb. 1992, besucht das Gymnasium Freistadt. Ihre Interessen sind Film, Musik, Fotografie, sie möchte später Regisseurin werden.

129128.name: Stop Motion Lightshow
129128.description: Der Beginn meines Projektes „Stop Motion Lightshow“ lässt sich auf den Medientechnikunterricht in meiner Schule zurückführen. Unser Lehrer ermutigte uns, zu Hause ein Stop-Motion-Video anzufertigen. Dabei kam ich nach langem Überlegen auf die außergewöhnliche Idee, mein Video mit Teelichtern zu realisieren. Ich kaufte mir 300 Teelichter und klebte diese auf ein großes Plakat. Dazu baute ich mir ein improvisiertes Stativ, um die Kamera genau über dem Mittelpunkt dieses Rechtecks platzieren zu können. Nach einer kurzen Planungsphase folgte die Umsetzung, welche aber zahlreiche Probleme mit sich brachte. Die größte Schwierigkeit war, dass sich die Kamera während des ganzen Projektablaufes kein bisschen bewegen durfte. Außerdem ist die enorme Hitzeentwicklung dieser Teelichter nicht zu unterschätzen, was auch meine Finger zu spüren bekamen. Nach tagelanger Arbeit war ich mit dem Ergebnis zufrieden und begann damit, die rund 500 Einzelbilder zu überprüfen und daraus ein Movie zu gestalten.
129128.biography: Thomas Niedermaier, geb. 1991, besucht seit 2005 die HTL Leonding für EDV & Organisation. Er hat bereits eine „Mensch ärgere dich nicht“-Simulation entwickelt und arbeitet zurzeit an seinem Maturaprojekt-Game „Space2Go - 2nd World“.

129133.name: www.daskonzept.at
129133.description:
„www.daskonzept.at“ galt lange als Plattform für die gleichnamige Schülerzeitung. Jedoch entstand, nachdem die ersten „Gründerväter“ Abgänger des Gymnasiums Zwettl waren, ein im Waldviertel mittlerweile bekannter Verein mit dem gleichen Namen. Der Kulturverein brauchte einen Web-Auftritt, deshalb wurde „www.daskonzept.at“ in zwei Bereiche getrennt: „verein.daskonzept.at“ und „zeitung.daskonzept.at“. Mit Erfolg! Bereits in den ersten Wochen verzeichneten wir einige hundert Besucher. Grund dafür: ein Großereignis namens „IWENT“. Unter „Verein“ gibt es nicht nur einen öffentlichen Bereich, in dem User multimedial über sämtliche Aktivitäten informiert werden, sondern auch einen Bereich, welcher nur für Vereinsmitglieder zugänglich ist. Wichtigste Module sind das eingerichtete Forum, in dem über Probleme und Ideen diskutieren werden kann, sowie eine Private-Message-Funktion. „Zeitung“ ist ein Online-Archiv aller unserer (preisgekrönten) Schülerzeitungen. Darin nachzulesen sind die verschiedensten Interviews sowie diverse Reaktionen so mancher nicht wenig bekannter ÖsterreicherInnen.

Links: www.daskonzept.at
129133.biography:
Fabian Todt, geb. 1993, besucht seit 2003 das BG/BRG Zwettl. Seine Hobbys sind Skateboarden, Basketball, Fußball, EDV, ehrenamtlich/politisch engagieren, Musik entdecken und hören. Mountainbiken, Laufen, Basketball u. v. m.

Maximilian Zinner, geb. 1994, besucht seit 2004 das Bundesgymnasium und Bundesrealgymnasium Zwettl. Seine Hobbys sind Sport: Golf (GC Weitra), Mountainbiken, Laufen, Basketball u. v. m.

129568.name: Mortal Engine
129568.authors: Paula Levis, Damien Cooper, Gideon Obarzanek, Chunky Move, Robin Fox, Ben Frost, Frieder Weiss, Chunky Move
129568.description:
“Mortal Engine” is a performance work created in 2007/8 by the company Chunky Move under the direction of Gideon Obarzanek and a team of outstanding artists working in areas that already placed interdisciplinarity at the core of their creative processes. It is not a dance work, nor is it a piece of theater, or a piece of digital music. It is neither an interactive work nor a synaesthetic experience. In essence, it is all of these things melded together to create an exploratory hybridity, a coalescence of human and technological forms.
The work is in flux: “Mortal Engine” has a hybridity that results in a series of simultaneously existing states that are yet to collapse into a singularity. Even gravity is compromised as dancers attempt to navigate a sloped stage area that doubles as a modular projection surface. In “Mortal Engine”, the limits of the human body are an illusion. Kinetic energy fluidly metamorphoses from the human figure into light image, into sound and back again in a constant state of becoming. Emanating from within, crackling light and staining shadows represent the most perfect or sinister of souls. Connection and disconnection, isolation and togetherness, duets are seen both as couples and as singular selves struggling to escape inner darkness— mortality, sexuality, desire. Drawing on the kinetics of the interior, enveloping lasers and movement-responsive video projections paint an ever-shifting, shimmering world. Witnessing moments of exquisite cosmological perfection or grotesque evolutionary accidents of existence, we are ceaselessly driven forwards by the reality of permanent change.
129568.credits: Direction and Choreography: Gideon Obarzanek; Interactive System Design: Frieder Weiss; Laser and Sound Artist: Robin Fox; Composer: Ben Frost; Costume Design: Paula Levis; Lighting Design: Damien Cooper; Supported by: The Australia Council for the Arts, Arts Victoria, The Sydney Festival.
129568.biography:
Damien Cooper (US) has designed lighting for diverse dance Companies.

Gideon Obarzanek (AU), independent performer and choreographer. Founder and artistic director of Chunky Move.

Ben Frost (IS), composer, produces gallery-based installations, scores commissioned for film, contemporary dance and large-scale multimedia productions.

Frieder Weiss (DE) is an engineer in the arts and expert for real-time computing and interactive computer systems in performance art.

Paula Levis (AU) fashion designer, has designed for numerous production companies including Victorian Opera, Danceworks, Dancehouse, DanceNorth, Red Stitch Actor’s Theatre and La Mama.

129576.name: bios [bible]
129576.authors: Jan Zappe, robotlab, Martina Haitz, Matthias Gommel
129576.description:
The installation “bios [bible]” consists of an industrial robot that writes down the Bible on rolls of paper. The machine draws the calligraphic lines with high precision. Like a monk in the scriptorium it creates the text step by step. Starting with the Old Testament and the books of Moses, “bios [bible]” produces the whole book continuously within seven months.
