_The 120 days of *buntu_ project exists in three different forms:

- OS modification workshop where participants learn how to modify their desktop environments

- _120buntu.com_ online community offering complete repository of our software

- Exhibition setup, comprising all created operating system running as Live sessions

Links: http://www.120buntu.com/
169993.biography: _The 120 days of *buntu_ is a project by Gordan Savicic (AT/NL) and Danja Vasiliev (RU). Gordan is an artist who plays with software algorithms, experimental media and fine art. His works includes game art, interactive/passive installations and speculative hardware. Danja Vasiliev is a Russian-born computer artist, engineer and researcher. His work and experiments touch on topics of digital life and everyday technology, networked environments, computer operating systems, machine-to-human interfaces, data forensics, reality hacking and others.

170019.name: Fundación Ciudadano Inteligente
170019.description:
_Fundación Ciudadano Inteligente_ (Smart Citizen Foundation) is a non-profit social organization based in Chile that promotes transparency and encourages active citizen participation through the web and other information technologies. Its goal is to reduce information asymmetries in Latin America that currently produce a gap in citizens’ relations with politics, the market and other social encounters. The organization conceives web technologies as a key tool for gathering, organizing, illustrating and sharing information through the social web, with the aim of promoting informed citizen actions and accountability.

Our web platform _www.ciudadanointeligente.cl_ hosts various apps that are used as citizen tools to promote transparency and citizen participation:

_www.votainteligente.cl_: the online congress accountability website that acts as a watchdog to monitor congress information. It tracks every bill being debated, providing updated information about the contents and the parliamentarians who support them (or not), the debate, both at plenary and committee levels, and the potential interests behind the legislative work. It also has a Profiles section, where web users can track each member of congress individually. _Votainteligente_ is also a blogging space for citizens who aim to publish information, opinions or columns related to issues of political accountability and transparency.

_www.accesointeligente.cl_ is a web application that allows citizens to request public information from any government-dependent agency, all from a single window that acts as a one stop shop. It connects automatically with each public agency’s online form, it publishes answers as searchable data-bases, and it keeps statistical information of all requests.

_www.donar.cl_ is a website that helps citizens find the right organization to make a donation to. It is a catalog of NGOs based on institutional information about organizations and on the transparency of budget-management information and performance.

_Fundación Ciudadano Inteligente_ was born in 2009, before Chile’s presidential election. The platform started out as a unique place to find all the information about each candidate: CVs, stances, views on subjects, etc. Users could compare the candidates’ positions side by side, through the sites’ candidate comparison app, which served as a resource in the decision-making process.

Links: http://www.ciudadanointeligente.cl/
170019.biography: Fundación Ciudadano Inteligente (CL) has been founded by Felipe Heusser, a Lawyer from the Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. It has a solid team of people, all young professionals from different fields: lawyers, political scientists, journalists, sociologists and researchers, together with a large group of interns who help us with our investigations and legislative monitoring.

170045.name: x_msg project
170045.description:
The _X_MSG project_ is about sex-work activism, social telephony and rewired technology. The project is a collaboration between two amateur technological tinkerers and a group of sex-work activists. Together we have put forward our energy to create DIY SMS-based software system for women involved with the sex industry. Ultimately, the _X_MSG_ software system is the outcome of an ongoing experiment between amateur coding and the pedagogy of sex work activism that allows for a new exploration of media systems.

The premise of the _X_MSG_ system is simple: a piece of amateur-coded open-source software that redirects text messages to its networks of sex work activists, while only costing them the price of a single text message. The system operates via a cheap DIY telephony server and uses a second-hand mobile phone with an O2 pay-as-you-go “unlimited” texts service. The phone is connected via a USB cable to a recycled computer that operates the server.
This software assemblage has been developed in consultation and collaboration with the London-based sex-worker-led collective x:talk and is aimed at women involved with the sex industry. The system is designed to respond to the most prominent social problems that the women in the industry face. It meets the need for anonymity, considers language barriers and uses the most common, but private, technology: the mobile phone. As a key feature, the system overcomes the risks and difficulties of women meeting in a geographical location and avoids the safety issues connected to online environments. As our collaboration partner, x:talk members are the primary participants at this stage in the _X_MSG project_.

The _X_MSG_ system is evidence of a social coding practice that relies on a communal exchange between the programmer and the user group as its first premise. The aim is to investigate coding, not as a functional solution but as a political tool in its encounter with the social environment of the sex industry. Hence we share the feminist objectives and interests of x:talk, who “consider that a feminist analysis and practice is crucial to changing the sex industry. Women represent the majority of workers in the industry and gendered sexualised and reproductive labour have historically constituted a central part in the structures that subordinate and oppress women.” (www.x:talkproject.net) As a group organized from within the industry, x:talk seeks to break the license on sex-worker’s voices currently held by third-sector organizations and health professionals. Likewise, we seek to move beyond functional coding and design aesthetics and work with software by bringing back the user as a central component of development.

The core team of our project consists of Cliff Hammett, Alexandra Jönsson and the x:talk collective.

Links: http://xmsg.org.uk/
170045.biography: Cliff Hammett, Alexandra Jönsson and the x:talk collective have been collaborating on the _X_MSG project_ since 2009. They are technology tinkerers and critical media researchers in the field of socially engaged media art. They work to develop software methodologies to work with communities in a practical manner while they critically interrogate the norms and limitations of commercial software and services in order to subvert and rewire them. Sustainability is at the centre of their collaboration, both for their technical experiments and their engagement with communities.

170077.name: Ushahidi
170077.description:
_Ushahidi_ is a non-profit technology company that specializes in developing free and open-source software for crowd-sourcing, visualization and interactive mapping. We build tools for democratizing information, increasing transparency and lowering the barriers to individuals sharing their stories.

_Ushahidi_ started as an ad hoc group of technologists and bloggers hammering out software in a couple days, trying to figure out a way to gather more and better information about the post-election violence in Kenya in January 2008.

Since then, we have open-sourced the _Ushahidi_ platform and made it available for free to individuals and organizations. The tool is now being utilized by organizations big and small all over the world. In short, _Ushahidi_ has shown what a small team of dedicated people can do, leveraging technology to impact and create change all over the globe.

Some examples of this have been seen in places such as Haiti, where 80,000 SMS reports were received, 3000+ reports thousands published to the map, and hundreds of people helped by local relief groups due to this new source of real-time information. In essence, _Ushahidi’s_ work with partners in Haiti served as the de facto emergency SMS system, connecting those in need with the major relief organizations, including the Red Cross, UN, US State Department and many others.

The platform played a decisive role in Russia during the fires of summer 2010, where the citizens self-organized using _Ushahidi_ to coordinate their efforts. Media organizations such as Al Jazeera, the BBC, the _Guardian_, Internews, and the _Washington Post_ have deployed _Ushahidi_ for various reasons.

Links: http://www.ushahidi.com/
170077.biography: _Ushahidi_ is a disruptive organization that is willing to take risks in the pursuit of changing the traditional way that information flows. The core team is Erik Hersman (co-founder and director of strategy and operations), David Kobia (co-founder and director of technology development), Juliana Rotich (co-founder and executive director).

170117.name: Bloody Map 血房地图
170117.description:
“China’s property sector, with its forced evictions and sometimes bloody confrontations, has long been described as something akin to a war zone. Now a team of online volunteers, led by an anonymous Chinese blogger, has launched a map-based project that brings that simile into stark relief.
“Called ‘the Blood-Stained Housing Map,’ the project uses Google Maps to plot violent housing evictions and land grabs across the country. ” (Josh Chin, Wall Street Journal)

The _Bloody Map_ project was launched on October 8, 2010, inspired by a forced eviction case that took place that autumn afternoon—the village of Baihutou, at Beihai, Guangxi, was going to be demolished.

I got the idea from our talking on Weibo (a Chinese twitter-like site). That night, I registered the anonymous ID “Xuefangditu, or Bloody Map” on Gmail, and used the e-mail address on that site. I edited six cases on the map in the first night and released it on Weibo as “Xuefangditu”.

In the following week, I collected reports on forced evictions in which people died in the previous few years. The first case I found on the Internet happened in 2003. Friends and strangers noticed the map, and from the second week they started to help. More and more strangers wrote to me, providing reports or cases that had not yet been reported. I also got an e-mail from the son of a man who had died for their house years before. He told me he cried when he found his father's name was on my map.

We recorded about 80 cases by the end of October, and the media noticed the project. It attracted many reports, from state-owned Xinhua agency to Nanfang News, but only two days later no one could talk about it in the media. People could not even search it as a key word for a couple of months, and my original account on Weibo was also removed.

We set up a QQ group for volunteers, which allows people to talk and exchange information—most of them are reporters, lawyers and people who have suffered or are still suffering from forced evictions.

A graphic Wikipedia of land-grab thuggery, the open version of this project has so far attracted more than 760,000 views and over 200 contributions. Users have used a variety of icons to describe different types of property-related violence: volcanoes for mass protests, beds for when property owners were killed, and flames for when those resisting eviction set themselves on fire.

Links: http://maps.google.com/maps/ms?ie=UTF8&msa=0&msid=212261269395391329707.0004921f02f43f6c4f07e&ll=35.317366, 111.357422&spn=16.751302, 43.286133&z=5
170117.biography: The open version of _Bloody Map_ of land-grab thuggery, the open version of this project has so far attracted more than 760,000 views and over 200 contributions. Users have used a variety of icons to describe different types of property-related violence: volcanoes for mass protests, beds for when property owners were killed, and flames for when those resisting eviction set themselves on fire.

170119.name: Afrikanet.info
170119.description:
Afrikanet.info is the first information portal on the web about people of African descent in Austria, Germany and Switzerland. It was first established in 2000 as a mailing list to inform people of African descent in Austria. Afrikanet.info journalists now inform about the lives of people of African origin in Germany, Austria and Switzerland, it rarely provides information on Africa. Because of its excellent work, in October 2005 Afrikanet.info was awarded the Austrian International Cultural Award. A year later, in recognition of its work against racism, the editor-in-chief, Simon Inou, received the European Union’s prize “For Diversity. Against Discrimination”.

Links: http://www.afrikanet.info/
170119.biography: Afrikanet.info was founded by Simon Inou (AT), a journalist living in Austria since 1995. He studied sociology in Cameroon and journalism in Austria. He was co-founder and editor of Le Messager des Jeunes, Cameroon’s first youth newspaper, chief editor of Radio Afrika International and “Informationsportal Afrikanet”, and project director of Black Austria. He is initiator of the Austrian project “Migrant journalists writing for Die Presse”.

170143.name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team
170143.description:
_Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team_ (HOT) was initially an informal group within _OpenStreetMap_. After the January 2010 earthquake in Haiti, this group worked as part of the greater technologist and volunteer effort to help assist remotely to provide maps to the organizations responding on the ground in Haiti. Within the first month in Haiti over 640 individuals from all over the world helped edit infrastructure information, as well as creating digital tools to utilize the map data. In March 2010, members of HOT began traveling to Haiti to teach those living and working there how to utilize the data and how to update it themselves. In 2010 they trained over 400 people and helped develop a local team of Haitians working within the International Organization for Migration. This team was very quickly able to switch over to mapping possible cholera treatment facilities as needed in the fall of 2010.

HOT is now beginning to work in other countries that are risk prone, to help map them before disaster strikes in order to make the crisis response faster and more effective.

HOT believes that in a disaster open geospatial data can be of benefit to anyone. The real power is allowing communities to map themselves. Key to realizing this is making use of the _OpenStreetMap_ data easily accessible and usable. Our group creates training materials, holds training classes and develops software to accomplish this goal.

Links: http://hot.openstreetmap.org/
170143.biography: _Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team_. There is a core group of five board members that handle proposal writing and project planning within HOT. The board is elected by the HOT membership. Membership of HOT is by existing members nominating other volunteers for their work helping HOT throughout the year. While membership is by nomination, anyone can help volunteer for the _Humanitarian OpenStreet Team_, and those active volunteers end up being nominated for membership.

170145.name: NairoBits Digital Design School
170145.description:
_NairoBits_ is a non-profit organization that trains youth in creative multimedia design as a means of self-expression and as a way to fight extreme poverty. It targets youth from the informal settlements of Nairobi who have little or no chances in life. The idea is to equip them with marketable creative multimedia and other skills to enable them live off their skills.

45% of urban Kenyans live in slums (approx 13.5 million). In Nairobi, 60% of residents are slum dwellers. According to the UN the population of Nairobi has been steadily growing (4.5% 2005‐2010). The largest slums are Kibera, Mathare Valley, Kawangware/Dagoretti and Korogocho. According to the 1999 population census, Kibera, which is considered the largest informal settlement in Africa, had a population of 287,000, Kawangware/Dagoretti 87,000, Mathare Valley 69,000 and Korogocho 44,000. These areas are characterized by limited access to water, sanitation, electricity and road infrastructure. The _Atlas of poverty in Nairobi_ indicates that between 50% and 70% of the population in these areas lives below the poverty line. _NairoBits_ targets youth in these slums. These youths are taken through the basics of what a computer is, and by the end of a year they have already been taught about branding, website design and development using tools such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Flash, PHP/Mysql and are able to make logos and websites and carry out multimedia projects for various audiences.

_NairoBits_ then places these youths in multimedia design companies for internships and employment or supports them in setting up their freelance design business. It was registered in 1999.

Due to its success, the model has been replicated in Zanzibar (_ZanziBits_), Ethiopia(_AddisBits_) and in Kampala, Uganda (_KampaBits_). The success is attributed to the philosophy of an open, creative environment where the youth are allowed to explore and learn by doing. It is a very practically oriented course, which is fun and engaging.

Links: http://www.nairobits.com/
170145.biography: _NairoBits_ is open to the community, with over 30 community organizations and 30 multimedia companies involved. We have an alumni network of over 6000 youths. We have transferred the training from a central location and now partner with community organizations to set up training centers in seven of the major slums. The trainers are all former students of the organization. Apart from ten trainers, there is a manager, an accountant and an office administrator. At the highest level is a board of trustees, who advise and guide the management team.

170153.name: Seaquence
170153.description:
_Seaquence_ is an experiment in web-based musical composition and community. Adopting a biological metaphor, users can create and combine musical life-forms, resulting in an organic, dynamic composition. These compositions become part of a growing collection that can be browsed, modified and re-appropriated by others.
_Seaquence_ was developed during a residency at Gray Area Foundation for the Arts in San Francisco, CA. Originally emerging out of a discussion around creating a community-based fundraising project for the new arts organization, the project quickly took a life of its own as an open web platform for music creation. Since 2009, _Seaquence_ has continued to evolve through various iterations—each of which has sought to tackle the technical and methodological challenges of making an intuitive yet versatile online tool for the creation and sharing of musical compositions. The official online launch in October 2010 was met with an unexpected amount of engagement. *
*_Seaquence_ is an original Gray Area Labs project created by Ryan Alexander, Gabriel Dunne, and Daniel Massey, with support from Gray Area Foundation for the Arts.

Links: http://seaquence.org/
170153.biography: _Seaquence_ is an original Gray Area Labs project created by Ryan Alexander, Gabriel Dunne, and Daniel Massey, with support from Gray Area Foundation for the Arts. Since the launch of _Seaquence“, there have been 25,000+ compositions contributed by thousands of anonymous users online. _Seaquence_ is open for anyone to use. While users are anonymous, we’ve learned from feedback that the project has engaged a wide demographic— young and old, with or without musical experience, from all over the globe.

170183.name: Pikunikku
170183.description:
_Pikunikku_ ピクニック bedeutet „Picknick“ auf Japanisch. Ich habe diesen Namen gewählt, weil meine Webseite genau das sein soll – ein buntes Picknick für die Augen im großteils grauen World Wide Web. Ich möchte, dass meine Besucher einen Moment innehalten und genauer hinsehen. Und Japanisch, weil ich die japanische Kultur liebe.

_Pikunikku_ ist eigentlich nur aus Langeweile und Spaß am Designen und Coden entstanden. Das Layout habe ich in Photoshop Elements 4.0 erstellt. Ich weiß, es ist ziemlich vollgestopft und chaotisch – daher auch der Untertitel _insomnia_ („Schlaflosigkeit“) – und vielleicht nicht jedermanns Sache, doch ich liebe diesen Collagenstil.

Dann habe ich alles gecodet und die Inhalte erstellt. Es ist mir wichtig, auch kleine Goodies für die Besucher anzubieten – z. B. niedliche Pixel, die gegen Rücklink auf der eigenen Homepage ausgestellt werden dürfen, oder selbst erstellte Icons, die man z. B. in Foren verwenden kann. Außerdem haben die Besucher die Möglichkeit, mir Nachrichten zu hinterlassen oder mir Fragen zu stellen, die ich natürlich auch beantworte.
Ich habe mich entschlossen, alle Texte komplett auf Englisch zu verfassen, weil ich damit ein internationales Publikum erreichen kann. Über das Internet habe ich schon viele Menschen aus aller Welt kennengelernt – das ist eine tolle Sache.
170183.biography: Selina Fanninger, geb. 1993, lebt in Wien. Ihre Interessen sind Zeichnen, Webdesign und Japan. Sie möchte später Grafikdesignerin werden.

170212.name: Flugundfall
170212.description: Ton:Zu hören ist ein Geräuschetrack bestehend aus gesampelten Geräuschen aus dem Haushalt, (zb. Waschmaschine, Staubsauger). Bei der Erstellung der Geräuschkulisse wurde noch nicht auf das visuelle Potential der Geräusche geachtet. Die Animation wurde erst geplant und ausgeführt nachdem der Track fertig war.Bild:Von der Geräuschkulisse ausgehend wurde das Bild gestaltet. Es wurde besonders darauf geachtet, das der visuelle Part sich nicht auf die Geräuschquellen (Besen, Staubsauger etc.) bezieht. So wurde zum Beispiel die Waschmaschine durch ein Flugzeug dargestellt etc.Das Video beginnt sehr abstrakt und wird über die Zeit immer konkreter und realitätsgebundener, bis es sich zum Schluss wieder zu einfachen Farbflächen abstrahiert.

170271.name: Bikemap iPhone App
170271.description:
„Egal wo ich bin, möchte ich Radrouten finden können, die andere schon erprobt haben und empfehlen.“ Diese Idee setzt das Portal _Bikemap.net_ seit 2007 erfolgreich um. Ich habe die Firma bei meiner Ferialpraxis 2010 kennen gelernt und kam auf die Idee, eine iPhone/iPad App dafür zu entwickeln.

Mittels Eingabe eines Ortes oder durch Lokalisierung können Radrouten (derzeit weltweit 420.000) gefunden werden. Die Darstellung auf einer Karte und die ergänzenden Beschreibungen und Informationen vermitteln dem Anwender einen Eindruck von der Strecke.

Die Routen können offline und online als Navigationshilfe beim Abfahren eingesetzt werden.

Login über Facebook oder ein _bikemap.net_-Account sowie übliche Funktionen zum Favorisieren und Austausch von Strecken mit Freunden komplettieren den Funktionsumfang. Mit Version 2.0 kann der Radfahrer mit dem iPhone die von ihm gefahrene Route aufnehmen und direkt online verfügbar machen.
Die technische Umsetzung erfolgte mittels Titanium, welches Javascript Code in Objective C umwandelt.

Innerhalb von zwei Monaten wurde die App bereits mehr als 20.000 Mal heruntergeladen und war in Österreich, Tschechien und Qatar die Nummer 1 in der Kategorie Sport und darüber hinaus in Deutschland, den Niederlanden, der Schweiz und Belgien unter den Top 5 und in den USA an der 15. Stelle.
_Futurezone.at_ hat am 1. April, und der _Kurier_ am 13. Mai 2011, über meine App berichtet.

Links: http://bikemap.felixkrause.at/
170271.biography: Felix Krause, geb. 1994, besucht die HTL Wr. Neustadt, interessiert sich für Programmierung, Robotik, Tennis und Golf. 2010 hat er Österreich bei der Robocup Weltmeisterschaft in Singapur im Soccer Junior Wettbewerb vertreten. Sein Berufsziel ist, Entwickler in einem kalifornischen Start-up Unternehmen zu werden.

170273.name: MicrosizeMe
170273.authors: Andreas Daniliuc, Simon Prochazka, Jürgen Spandl, Patrik Susko, Sasan Haji Hashemi, HTL Ottakring
170273.description:
Ziel des Projektes ist es, mit Hilfe eines 3D Computerspiels, welches auf unserer Schulhomepage präsentiert werden soll, die HTL Ottakring vorzustellen. Gleichzeitig möchten wir dadurch zum einen Wissenswertes über unsere Schule zu vermitteln, zum anderen auch Interesse und Neugier an einer technischen Ausbildung wecken.

Um dieses Erlebnis so realitätsgetreu wie möglich zu gestalten, wurde ein 3D-Modell von der Schule erstellt. Besonders wichtig war es uns, das Spiel ohne jegliche weiteren Applikationen über den Browser online spielbar zu machen. So lässt sich einerseits eine größere Zielgruppe ansprechen, andererseits kommt die Idee besonders bei jungen Besuchern der Schulhomepage gut an.

Zusätzlich haben wir auch einen Multiplayer-Modus entwickelt, bei dem mehrere Benutzer nach einem klassischen Capture-The-Flag-Prinzip gegeneinander antreten müssen. Der Multiplayer-Modus soll speziell die Leute ansprechen, die den normalen Modus bereits durchgespielt haben.
_MicrosizeMe_ entstand als Diplomarbeitsprojekt einer diesjährigen fünften Klasse der HTL Ottakring in Wien.

Links: http://www.microsizeme.at/
170273.biography: Das Team hinter dem Projekt _MicrosizeMe_ besteht aus fünf Schülern der Informationstechnologie-Abteilung der HTL Ottakring: Andreas Daniliuc, Sasan Haji Hashemi, Simon Prochazka, Jürgen Spandl, Patrik Susko.

170279.name: Klimakids
170279.description:
**Warum haben wir dieses Thema gewählt?**

Es geht uns alle an. Wir alle leben auf dem Planet Erde. Er besteht zu 70 % aus Wasser, zu 10 % aus Wald und 20 % aus Erde. Umgeben ist er von einer dünnen Luftschicht – der Atmosphäre. Wir wollen ihn soweit wir können schützen und sauber halten. Wir haben dazu gemeinsam ein Weblog im Internet programmiert: _klimakids.blogspot.com_

**Warum haben wir einen Blog verwendet?**

Weil so ein Blog ganz einfach zu bedienen ist. Wir verwenden dafür das Programm Windows Live Writer. Das Internet hat auch den Vorteil, dass wir unser Wissen allen Menschen auf der Welt gratis zur Verfügung stellen können.

**Wie haben wir das gemacht?**

Zuerst haben wir Informationen über das Wetter gesammelt und uns als Meteorologen versucht. Über einen Zeitraum von vier Wochen haben wir das Wetter beobachtet. Die Ergebnisse haben wir in Tabellen eingetragen. Parallel dazu informierten wir uns über die Atmosphäre, die Sonne, die Klimazonen, den Treibhauseffekt, die Folgen der Klimaveränderung. Außerdem haben wir kleine Informationssendungen aufgenommen, diese anschließend am PC bearbeitet und dann auf YouTube hochgeladen und mit unserem Blog verlinkt.

**Worin besteht also das Problem für unser Klima?**

Wir erzeugen zu viel CO2, dadurch verändert sich unser Klima. In manchen Ländern wird es wärmer, in anderen kälter. Überschwemmungen, Dürrekatastrophen können die Folge sein. Alle Länder der Welt sollten gemeinsam einen Plan machen, wie sie weniger CO2 erzeugen, um den Treibhauseffekt zu verringern.

Links: http://klimakids.blogspot.com/
170279.biography: Das Klimakids-Team sind: Magdalena Berger, Sophie Biziak, Tamara Bogicevic, Corinna Eisenreich, Andre Fuhry, David Grömer, Matthias Hartner, Alexander Hess, Navina Haselmaier, Sara Müllner, Lisa Petrovic, Kathrin Pirgmayer, Sophie Plaß, Andrea Prissnitz, Oliver Reiter, Konstantin Rökk, Daniela Salak, Ronja Sandtner, Sebastian Schitnik, Julia Siffert.

170333.name: Digitale Schriften
170333.authors: Höhere graphische Bundes- Lehr- und Versuchsanstalt Wien
170333.description:
Das Ziel der acht Schülerinnen und Schüler der Graphischen Bundeslehranstalt war, das typografische Spannungsfeld zwischen analog und digital auszuloten. Sie versuchten eine Annäherung in zwei Schritten: erstens die Digitalisierung der eigenen Handschrift und zweitens die Rekonstruktion einer Pixelschrift mit den Vektorwerkzeugen einer Software zur Schriftgestaltung.

Die Herausforderung bei den handschriftlichen Fonts lag darin, die Natürlichkeit und den Schwung der Hand ins Digitale umzusetzen. Unter anderem haben die Schülerinnen und Schüler dabei moderne OpenType-Techniken eingesetzt, um Eintönigkeit im Schriftbild zu vermeiden. So haben sie etwa Ligaturen und alternative Glyphen in ihre Schriften eingebaut.

Bei den Pixelfonts dagegen stand das Spiel mit der Form im Vordergrund. Die Schülerinnen und Schüler mussten unter der einschränkenden Prämisse eines Pixelrasters ihre individuellen, kreativen Lösungen finden. Dabei entstanden oft ganze Schriftfamilien mit unterschiedlichen Pixelformen.
170333.biography: Die acht Schriftgestalterinnen und Schriftgestalter - Regina Hochmeister, Marianne Korec, Tanja Lenk, Jessica Maierhofer, Petra Sedlaszek, Bernhard Stegbauer, Jakob Stubner, Katarina Udel - besuchen die vierten Klassen der Abteilung Grafikdesign an der Höheren Graphischen Bundeslehranstalt in Wien XIV.

170455.name: WiSoMe - Wind and Solar Power Measurement
170455.authors: Florian Pfeffer, Michael Schmidt, Lukas Kirchner, HTBLuVA-Salzburg

170464.name: Rotkäppchen
170464.description:
Eines Tages erzählte uns unser damaliger Englischprofessor die „wahre“ Geschichte des Rotkäppchens. Er informierte uns darüber, dass es zwei Versionen dieses Märchens gibt: eine für Jugendliche bis 14 und die andere für Jugendliche ab 14 (wenn Sie wissen, was gemeint ist). Damals waren wir zwischen 13 und 14 Jahre alt und unsere Interessen lagen bei solchen Themen. Wir, die Schülerinnen der damaligen 4A (2006/2007) des BG/BRG Judenburg, beschlossen, die „wahre“ Geschichte des Rotkäppchens (jugendfreie Version) zu einem Zeichentrickfilm zu machen.

Die Idee war geboren, doch aller Anfang ist schwer. Wir gingen mit dieser Idee zu unserem damaligen Professor für Bildnerische Erziehung und erzählten ihm davon. Wir begannen noch am selben Tag mit den ersten Zeichnungen und bauten unsere Ideen weiter aus. Die Zeit verging wie im Flug, und nach einem Schuljahr war unser Film über das Rotkäppchen fertig geschnitten, synchronisiert und bereit, gesehen zu werden. Doch ehe wir noch einen passenden Termin für die Premiere vereinbaren konnten, war das Schuljahr schon vorbei. Außerdem wechselten viele Schülerinnen aus der 4A anschließend in andere Schulen.
Das war auch der Grund dafür, dass unser Film über das Rotkäppchen ein klein wenig in Vergessenheit geraten ist und erst später zum Prix Ars Electronica eingereicht wurde. Jetzt haben wir aber den Beweis, dass sich die Arbeit an diesem Film wirklich gelohnt hat!
170464.biography: Wir, die Schülerinnen der damaligen 4A, besuchten im Schuljahr 2006/2007 das BG/BRG Judenburg mit dem Schwerpunkt Sprachen: Teresa Jagiello, Sarah Himmelsbach (heute Nestelbacher), Kathrin Kleemaier, Julia Sonnberger, Janine Nöst, Tanja Promebner, Lisa Pichler, Lisa Hödelmoser, Kerstin Kletzmayer, Stefanie Müller, Kathrin Rieser, Carina Lesser, Sandrina Harrer, Jennifer Schmalzer, Eva-Maria Zechner, Marlene Schrunner, Martina Liebfahrt, Lisa Genger, Carina Poier, Kristina Felfer, Bettina Kundegraber, Haslebner Julia

170512.name: Disco Dance
170512.description:
Ich liebe jede Art von Elektronik. Mich begeistert die Licht- und Tontechnik bei diversen Shows oder wie sie auch in großen Discos vorkommen. Da ich sehr gerne tanze und Musik bereits fix zu meinem Leben gehört (ich nehme auch Klavierunterricht) habe ich mich zu _Disco Dance_ entschlossen.

Ich habe mittlerweile alles zu Hause, was man für eine Disco braucht: angefangen von Sub-Booster, Mischpult, Stereoanlage, Discokugel, diversen Lichteffekten, Spots und Laser bis hin zu Nebelmaschine, Blaulicht und Stroboskop! Mit dem Computer verändere ich auch sehr gerne die Musik.
Ich freue mich auf jeden Fall wahnsinnig, dass ich gewonnen habe. Vor allem da ich nur einen Bruchteil meiner High-Tech-Geräte dazu verwendet habe.
170512.biography: Alexander Doubrava, geb. 2001, besucht die 4. Klasse der "Ökovolksschule Wienerwald". Seine Interessen sind: Chemie, Computer, Elektronik und Musik! Er möchte später Computertechniker und Programmierer werden.

170542.name: Lyzander
170542.description:
Es war Dienstagnachmittag. Ich war auf dem Heimweg, völlig fertig mit schwerer Schul- und Sporttasche. Man muss wissen, dass ich seit einigen Wochen programmieren konnte, und in Gedanken war ich gerade bei ein paar Codezeilen.

Auf einmal sah ich etwas: eine Linie, ein farbiges Etwas und ein Hindernis. Damit war die Idee geboren. Als ich zu Hause ankam, setzte ich mich sofort an den Computer und fing an, meine Idee zu verwirklichen. Tja, und als ich meinem Informatik-Lehrer zwei Tage später das Ergebnis zeigte, wollte er mir zuerst gar nicht glauben, dass ich das selbst geschrieben habe, und riet mir, es beim Prix Ars Electronica einzureichen.

Gesagt, getan. Davor noch ein paar Verbesserungen vorgenommen, und herausgekommen ist ein kurzweiliges Spiel, *Lyzander*: Grafisch zwar kein Meisterwerk, dafür aber umso höherer Unterhaltungswert, und durch die einfache Bedienung und leicht zu verstehende Spielidee kann jeder sofort mit dem Spielen beginnen.
170542.biography: Paul Plessing, geboren 1996 in Graz, besucht die 5. Klasse des Bundesgymnasium Carneri in Graz. Sein Hobby ist die Magie: Er ist Zauberkünstler. Und Programmierer: Es ist fantastisch, aus Nichts eine unglaubliche Welt zu erschaffen.

170599.name: Die gut gemeinten Fesseln
170599.description:
**Die Geschichte**

Die Bewohner eines Baumdorfes leben friedlich miteinander. Als sie bemerken, dass sich immer mehr Blätter verfärben und von den Ästen fallen, glauben sie, dass ihr Baum krank ist und umfallen wird. Daher beschließen sie, den Baum mit Seilen zu sichern. Doch die Seile sind so stark gespannt, dass der Baum verbogen wird und alle Baumhütten schief stehen. Sie können nicht mehr dort leben, und es bleibt ihnen nichts anderes übrig als auszuziehen.
Mit gepackten Koffern sitzen sie traurig unter einer Baumwurzel. Die Blätter fallen auf sie herab und bilden eine Höhle, in der sie überwintern können.
Ein Igel will sich auch im schützenden Laub vergraben und schneidet dabei mit seinen spitzen Stacheln ein Seil durch. Damit befreit er den Baum von seinen Fesseln und die Äste richten sich wieder auf.

Im Frühling, als die Bewohner aus ihrer Blätterhöhle hervorkommen, erblicken sie ihren Baum in neuer Pracht.

**Die Entstehung des Projektes**

Ausgangspunkt war meine Vorstellung von einer schönen Miniaturwelt in einem Baum. Ich versetzte mich in die Bewohner dieser Welt hinein und überlegte, was sie beschäftigen könnte. So entstand nach und nach die Geschichte. Weil ich in die Zeichentrickwelt mehr Details bringen wollte, habe ich die Hintergrundbilder mit Wasserfarben gemalt. Damit ich festlegen konnte, welche Hintergründe ich brauchen würde, erstellte ich zuerst ein Storyboard auf Papier.

Dann scannte ich die Bilder ein, fügte sie in Adobe Photoshop zusammen und bearbeitete sie dort nach. Anschließend importierte ich sie in Adobe Flash. Mit diesem Programm habe ich alle weiteren Objekte erstellt und animiert. Den Schnitt und das Einfügen der Musik führte ich in After Effects durch.
170599.biography: Bernhard Riedl, geb. 1998 in Wien, besucht seit 2009 das Realgymnasium GRG 15 „Auf der Schmelz“ in Wien. Beim Red Button Videofestival 2009 hat ein Video, das er mitgestaltet hat, die Silver Cam für den besten Film in der Kategorie „Animation / Bild“ gewonnen.

170605.name: Apaçi-Styler
170605.authors: tugay sevim, Murat Gürcü, Furkan Hatip
170605.description:
Ursprünglich wollten wir ein Online-Game machen, aber dann kamen wir auf Apaçi, das wir auch schon tanzten bevor wir das Video machten. Apaçi stammt ursprünglich aus der Türkei.

Als schließlich alle von der Idee des _Apaçi-Styler-Styler_ begeistert waren, besprachen wir unser Vorhaben mit unserem Lehrer. Er besorgte uns eine Greenbox-Folie und wir begannen gleich zu tanzen. Nach ca. vier Wochen war der Film fertig und wir reichten ihn – sehr knapp – ein.

Der Clip entstand im Rahmen der unverbindlichen Übung Multimedia.

Links: http://schulen.eduhi.at/hs.stadlpaura/
170605.biography: Die drei Jungs der Projektgruppe _Apaçi-Styler_ (Tugay Sevim, Furkan Hatip, Murat Gürcü) sind Schüler der Hauptschule Stadl-Paura, sie besuchen derzeit die 3. Klasse.

170732.name: Weltherberge Schulhaus
170732.description:
Das Projekt _Weltherberge: Schulhaus_ bezieht sich auf die Grund-Metaphorik der Begegnung mit dem Anderen bzw. mit dem Fremden. In der Gastfreundschaft und in der Beherbergung findet diese Begegnung ihren exemplarischen Ausdruck, deren markante Orte die Türe, der Tisch und das Bett sind. Im übertragenen Sinn verweisen die Objekte auf die Begegnung, auf das Ein- und Zulassen, auf die Gastlichkeit beim Tischgespräch und auf die Beherbergung von (fremden) Gästen, denen Ruhe, Intimität und friedliche Nächtigung geboten werden soll.

Die Konzeptbeiträge stammen aus den Fachbereichen: Mediale Darstellungsverfahren, Bildbearbeitung, Graphik und Malerei, textiles Gestalten, Deutsch und Mikroelektronik.

Das Objekt „Bett“ tritt als Speicher von Erinnerungen auf, indem Traumgeschichten als gesprochene Texte und Körpersilhouetten mittels Mehrfachbelichtung aufgezeichnet und überblendet werden. Sozusagen als Verwandlung des intimen in einen öffentlichen Ort, an dem sich die Erinnerungsspuren skizzenhaft ansammeln.

Bebilderte Raumteiler und Rollups verwandeln sich in Projektionsflächen, auf denen bleibende und vergängliche Spuren unterschiedlicher Erinnerungen und Assoziationen aufeinandertreffen; zugleich steuern Bewegungsmelder in Kombination mit Record-Funktionen Mediendateien, die
BesucherInnen interaktiv mit zusätzlichen Beiträgen erweitern können.

Ein Tisch birgt sowohl Alltagsspuren als auch Geräusche und Geschichten, auch diese mit Sensortechnik gesteuert. Die verschiedenen medienspezifischen Narrationen - erlebnisauthentisch mundartlich, märchenhaft, als Appell oder Kommentar, als Bild oder (verhülltes) Objekt - verweben sich durch die textilen Hüllen hindurch mit dem interaktiven Verhalten der BesucherInnen.

In der Projektgruppe, bestehend aus mehr als 80 SchülerInnen mit vielen altersspezifischen Eigenschaften und kaum überbietbarer Vielfalt, sind Erfindungen und Konzepte, Phantastisches und Handfestes, Metapher und Realität eine Verbindung eingegangen. Grenzen mussten überwunden werden, damit sowohl die technischen als auch die gestalterischen Ansprüche erfüllt werden konnten. Dies funktionierte auf Grund der Neugier, Innovationsbereitschaft und des Spaßes am weitläufigen Phantasieren. Die ProjektteilnehmerInnen aus zwei sehr verschiedenen Schultypen konnten sich somit ideal ergänzen.

Links: http://hblakunst-typo3.schule.at/index.php?id=24#c65
170732.biography: Die SchülerInnen der Höheren Bundeslehranstalt für künstlerische Gestaltung Linzbesuchten im Schuljahr 2010/11 die Klassen 2b, 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b mit dem Ausbildungsschwerpunkt: Objekt – Bild – Medien. Die Schüler der Höhere technische Bundeslehranstalt (HTBLA) in Leonding besuchten im Schuljahr 2010/11 die Klassen 4AFEL und 3YHEL mit dem Schwerpunkt Elektronik und Technische Informatik, bzw. Mikroelektronik.

170738.name: Future Building
170738.description:
_Future Building_ makes giving online as simple and transparent as volunteering in person. Projects range from schools and clinics to wells and houses. The limits are yours to define and then exceed. And anything that can be built in the real world can be constructed using _Future Building_.

Imagine a school, and what it takes to make it real. A retired war veteran in Atlanta buys the beams, a 15-year-old high-school student in Prague buys the nails. A couple in Johannesburg buy the bolts. More people pitch in for the floors, the walls, the windows, the plumbing, the wiring. What if this could all take place online and each person could visualize and share, in real time, the status of their contribution and everyone else's? A couple hundred people from a couple hundred different places see that the school still needs a roof, and they donate enough to build one. Then someone sees that the desks are still missing. She makes a donation for ten. Someone else makes a donation for twenty. Students get desks. Desks get computers. Computers get software. Click by click, a school is built online and off. But it doesn’t stop with a school or a hospital or a village, because what we’re building is a future.

Links: http://www.futurebuilding.org/

Before starting Soup, Josh served as a product manager at Google. In 2005, _Newsweek_ named Joshua as “one of the top 15 college students in America” for the impact he was creating as a result of thoughtful design aimed at fostering social and political awareness. Joshua has BAs in design and communication studies from UCLA.

170754.name: Prometheus Fusion Perfection
170754.description:
The world desperately needs a better energy source.

Nuclear fission produces large-scale clean energy. But the recent Sendai earthquake in Japan reminds us that nuclear fission comes with very real safety hazards. Nuclear fusion on the other hand has the potential to provide clean energy without the meltdown and radiation risks.

In 2006, Robert Bussard introduced a new approach to nuclear fusion, which could change everything: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polywell. Bussard’s reactor is still unproven, but the promise is tremendous. It deserves further research.

This is where *Prometheus Fusion Perfection* comes in: It is an open-source effort to build a working Bussard nuclear-fusion reactor. For the past two years I have been building at Bussard reactor independently in my lab in Brooklyn. This is not hypothetical - this is real research. To date I have fused the atom with a fusor, a precursor to the Bussard Reactor. Everything we learn is open-sourced and immediately published to our blog, for the world to read: http://prometheusfusionperfection.com/.

Links: http://prometheusfusionperfection.com/
170754.credits: Produced by Mark Suppes; shot and edited by Jamie Henson; audio and music by David Dahlquist
170754.biography: Mark Suppes (US) is a serial entrepreneur, web application developer, musician, painter, and now a scientist. He has illustrated a children’s book and helped with the recent Gucci.com relaunch.

170791.name: Haberlandt
170791.description:
_Haberlandt_ is a vending machine for food crops, a bio-reactor for growing a superfood—Arthrospira platensis micro-algae—and an automated avant-cuisine machine. It is an array cyborg, a mechatronic ecosystem where life and technological systems coexist—a sustained but open system with inputs and outputs typical of an entity that depends on a chemical energy exchange. The machine produces algae as the ultimate goal, and it needs recharging with a minimum amount of nutrients, being able to reduce this cycle of exchange to algae for human consumption (output) and waste human urine (input). It is a super-reduction of traditional agricultural systems, synthesized and compacted to produce hyperlocally an engineered product designed to be inserted into today’s society. The dispenser a potential ecotone—a transitional area between two plant communities – for urban citizens committed to a sustainable production and consumption, something so lacking in a globalized and asymmetric world.

Links: http://haberlandt.blablabla.org/
170791.biography: blablabLAB was born out of the development of a prototype framed by the “Lightscapes” workshop (James Clar, Scott Fitzgerald), held in Hangar, Barcelona, at the end of 2008. Over the past two years the group has expanded with contributions from other friends and fields—such as electronic engineering, environmental ecology, fashion design, avant-garde cuisine, visual arts, anthropology and biochemistry—to be engaged in various projects often related to an event.

170802.name: ChokePoint Project
170802.description:
_ChokePointProject_ is meant for people who are curious about transparency and control of the networking technologies, their use and abuse by nation states and corporations leading towards new toolsets being produced to distribute connectivity beyond traditional powers.

Telephony and the Internet have had a huge impact on society, both positive and negative. Following the uprisings in the Middle East in 2011, where the Internet was “turned off”, we aim to provide a close-to-real-time map of leverage points expressed through the power medium of data visualization.

We plan to develop tools and toolkits for exposing choke points. We will also be creating open-source tools which can be used by people to help this project to map networks to monitor and sidestep spying, although this is part of a longer-term initiative.

Components of the project include:

—an interactive data visualization of identified choke points, so that everyone can understand where the vulnerabilities are

—showing the related open projects which aim to remedy those vulnerabilities

—pointing to articles with analysis and strategy to educate and inform the general public and research communities

—releasing datasets and tools used to track down Internet choke points

We will also provide documentation including a tutorial and design patterns that present possible installation ideas for spaces such as museums and transit terminals.

This project should serve as an experimental space for citizens to investigate how governments are tracking them hour-by-hour. Participants should understand how such tools can allow for collaborative expression to reject current levels of scrutiny that are not made transparent by existing government and corporate entities.

Links: http://www.chokepointproject.net/
170802.biography: The P2P Foundation is a non-profit organization founded in 2005, legally based in the Netherlands though global in membership and readership. Its primary purpose is in researching, documenting and promoting p2p practices. (If Napster and torrents are peer-based music-file distribution systems, p2p takes the principle of peer-ing and beams it like a splash damage laser beam on everything it touches, from culture to politics to religion back to technology). Our last five years have been spent building a huge collection of knowledge with 14,424 content pages and 15 million views on the Wiki alone.

170813.name: Kibilight project
170813.description:
The objective of this project was to train young people living in the Kibera slum (Kenya) to assemble portable solar lamps and then test them for daily use, with the aim of starting a small production centre if the pilot phase is a success. The solar lamps will then be produced by these trained young solar technicians and initially sold on the local market. Part of the production run will be exported to Switzerland and sold as a fair-trade product. Prefabricated lamps will be used as solar-energy learning sets in schools and workshops in Switzerland. The youths were also trained to install solar home systems.

The Kibera solar lamp as it is now known emits a bright light, is smokeless and has little or no running costs (batteries), since it is charged by solar energy. The Kibera lamp is portable, uses solar-powered light-emitting diodes (LEDs) and can be used as a flashlight or hung up as a house lamp. The lamp provides an ideal solution for customers who have suffered using kerosene lamps and low-cost, battery-powered flashlights. When charged for six hours by its integrated solar panel it gives a very bright light for up to six hours and a less bright light for another three. The wooden casing is strong and does not need recycling. The casing has been varnished to protect the wood and keep off water.

Links: http://www.solafrica.ch/
170813.biography: Elizabeth Otieno (KE) is a 22-year-old girl from Kibera. After high school, she joined the Kibera Community Youth Program as a volunteer in several projects. In 2009, Greenpeace came together with the Kibera Community Youth Program to train some young people from Kibera in the solar technology. Since early 2010 she has been leading the solar group, and she went to Switzerland for a solar camp, where they installed solar systems both for lighting and for hot water in a youth hostel in St. Moritz.

192422.name: Countdown
192422.description:
I little over two years ago, I began drawing pictures with rockets in them. I do not know why, but one evening I wanted to do an exercise for myself with some constraints, which were: using colors I do not usually use; using a square format (in tribute to the old 8mm format); sometimes it could be abstract, and everything was to be about a rocket. A couple of weeks later I discovered the music of Apparat and the track _Granular Bastard_. I thought it would be amazing to do a three-and-a-half-minute animation of a rocket taking off.

I really wanted an “atmospheric movie”, not necessarily a deep story but just beautiful colors, good composition and a rocket as a main character. It is what I like in Godfrey Reggio’s film _Koyaanisqatsi_, the earth and life is the main character. It is not something we are used to seeing, and that is why it is beautiful. I have even written a script (which I know is crazy for a music video).

I began the animation in summer 2009. I listened to the music repeatedly and first cut the music in different parts, to get an idea of which sequence to put with which part of the music. First there are the computers waking up, then everything starts working, the astronauts enter in the rocket, everything warms up, silence, and finally take off. With one or two exceptions, I drew all the images for the animation in color.

The image of the smoke one was really important for the stylization of the smoke and fire. I really wanted to keep these circle particles to represent the smoke.

I did not really change the animation. I did it at the very beginning and tried as far as possible to stick to it. I think nothing changed for a year and half. The graphics evolved but not the editing. From the beginning to the end this was the kind of editing I wanted.

The beginning of the movie was a tricky part (because at the beginning I really wanted something very abstract in the way of the buttons and computers switching on). It is not something you can do in animation; you can do a rough “placeholder” but it is something that builds by itself while you are doing it.
From beginning to end, Chris Ware, Hans Richter, Len Lye, Stanley Kubrick and Godfrey Reggio’s _Qatsi_ trilogy were huge references.

Links: http://vimeo.com/28760604

192458.name: Fat
192458.authors: Gary Fouchy, Yohann Auroux Bernard, Sebastien de Oliveira Bispo, Supinfocom Arles
192458.description:
Lost in the middle of nowhere, a quiet little farm lives at the rhythm of its daily routine. One morning, the farmer discovers that a very strange phenomenon is spreading around him, hitting one animal after another. He has to adapt to this new environment full of strange and quirky situations and try to keep things going.

Based on the theme of metamorphosis and change, this short aims to be a well-balanced blend of comedy and poetry set in a simple, pretty little world. Suitable for all ages, it was made for enjoyment, to have fun and maybe think about how we deal with the transformations that happen in our everyday lives.

Links: http://www.supinfocom-arles.fr

He likes to tell strange and funny stories using his imagination, and loves to use this media because of the freedom it allows. Yohann Auroux Bernard (FR) has enjoyed creating and drawing new characters since he was a child; now landscapes and storyboard also complete his desires. Sebastien de Oliveira Bispo (FR), born in the Caribbean, has been exposed to cartoons and animated films since his early childhood. Now it has become a real passion to tell a story by creating a graphic universe.

192463.name: L'ère bête
192463.authors: Thomas Caudron, Ingrid Menet, Laurent Mériaux, Clément Tissier, Supinfocom Valenciennes
192463.description:
_L’ère bête_ is a medieval farce dealing with the notions of humanity and bestiality.

In the Middle Ages, a sow and a beggar are invited to a carnival where a crowd of masked men have fun in judging and torturing animals as if they were human beings. Our heroes are arrested and judged in their turn.

The film shows an archaic pagan carnival inspired by Flemish painting as well as surrealism. We follow the two heroes in a universe with its own internal logic that we cannot completely understand and where humanity and bestiality turn out to be intimately related. The illustrative look as well as the original music on ancient instruments contribute to making this crazy vision of ancient times real

192562.name: Aalterate
192562.description:
Diving into a coma, a woman tries to find the cause of her unconsciousness. She experiences extreme inner tension as its mutating silhouette gradually invades an empty canvas to a point of complete saturation. _Aalterate _is an attempt to represent the emergence of memory, intangible by nature, in a concrete, physiological way. By permanent transformations, electric nervous impulses which draw past events and organic forms which compose the elements of memory, in this film the body becomes the visible material of thought.

Rather than describing the events in a linear and frontal narrative, _Aalterate_ promotes seductive evocation so that narrative threads weave into the mind of the audience and find the freedom to stray to other possible readings.

192825.name: Rear Window Loop
192825.description:
By most accounts, Alfred Hitchcock’s 1954 classic _Rear Window_ is as perfectly constructed a film as any the medium has ever produced. It is a “purely cinematic film,” as Hitchcock later described it, whose obvious spatial handicaps both exploited and negated one of the camera’s pre-eminent virtues, its effortless ability to navigate between the proximal and distal. The plot is well-known: world-weary photographer, wheelchair-bound Jeff (Jimmy Stewart) is confined to recuperative leave in his Greenwich Village apartment with only (or mostly) a panorama of the encompassing tenement complex beyond as his company. But as Jean-Luc Godard commented, one never recalls the particulars of any of Hitchcock’s narratives but, rather, only the shots that framed them. In the case of _Rear Window_, however, neither specific scenes nor shots prove more memorable than the architecture and spatial configuration of the famed courtyard set. These have been analyzed to the point of exhaustion, with the chief exegetic points being well familiar to any casual student of cinema, but never have they been seen before like this video time-lapse.

Meticulously assembled by Jeff Desom, using just After-Effects and Photoshop, the video condenses Hitchcock’s masterwork into three breathtaking minutes in which the entirety of the film’s events—sans the dramatic, personal scenes between the protagonists—play out before Jeff’s gaze. Desom’s collage is completely comprised of footage from the film, with the iconic window panorama being neatly tailored and augmented with various photographic effects (tilt-shift, stabilization, “rain”) so as to achieve verisimilitude with the original and to re-create the environmental changes that propel the narrative along. “Since everything was filmed from pretty much the same angle,” Desom writes, “I was able to match them into a single panoramic view of the entire backyard without any greater distortions.
(Text: Samuel Medina)
192825.biography: Jeff Desom (LU) is a director, animator and visual artist. His work combines live-action, found footage and digital effects. The experimental pianist Hauschka is his most frequent collaborator. Together they have produced a range of works, including short films, an audiovisual live show and a number of award-winning music videos.

192917.name: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
192917.description:
The story of _Rise of the Planet of the Apes_ is built around the character of Caesar as he moves from childhood to young adult and undergoes a transformation that gives him supra-human intelligence. This was the first film in the _Planet of the Apes_ franchise to move away from makeup and prosthetics to create the apes digitally. Because the apes needed to look like present-day apes, we could not be constrained by a human’s size, proportions and posture. Also the apes needed to be every bit as emotionally engaging and nuanced in their performances as the humans in the film.

Enhancements we made to our performance capture setup made it more durable, portable and able to be used outside. This meant that the ape performers were able to participate on set with their human counterparts both physically and emotionally.

Performance capture served as the foundation for the ape movements as the actors’ performances. Retargeting and adjusting for the scale difference between the actor and Caesar required subtle adjustments. Broader action sequences that were physically impossible for humans to perform were accomplished with keyframe animation using a video reference library of chimp movements as a guide.

Caesar’s animation required a delicate balance of chimp-like behavior and human gestures and movements. Matching the actor’s performance required an understanding of both human and chimp facial actions and the corresponding emotion being expressed by each.

The quality of Caesar’s skin had to evolve as the character grew from infant to adult. Custom texture treatments combined with specific shader and scattering properties reflecting the evolutionary steps of skin were used to create the final looks.

Caesar’s fur was modeled with a proprietary tool called Barbershop, which was developed during the film. Caesar had hundreds of thousands of strands of fur that could be groomed by an artist using tools similar to real-world hairstyling.

Links: http://www.wetafx.co.nz/features/rise_of_the_planet_of_the_apes/
192917.credits:
Joe Letteri - Senior Visual Effects Supervisor

192917.biography: Weta Digital (NZ) is one of the world’s premier visual effects companies. Led by Senior Visual Effects Supervisor Joe Letteri, Weta Digital is known for uncompromising creativity and commitment to developing innovative technology. From groundbreaking digital characters such as Gollum and Kong, to the revolutionary virtual stage workflow on _The Adventures of Tintin_ and _Avatar_ and the performance capture advancements on *Rise of the Planet of the Apes*, they continue to break down barriers between live action and computer graphics and expand what is possible in film. Weta Digital established its reputation for cutting-edge visual effects with work on blockbusters such as _The Lord of the Rings_ trilogy and _King Kong_. The company began work in 1993 on co-founder Peter Jackson’s film _Heavenly Creatures_ and is based in Wellington, New Zealand.

192947.name: unnamed soundsculpture
192947.description:
The basic idea of the project _unnamed soundsculpture_ is built upon the consideration of creating a moving sound sculpture from the recorded motion data of a real person. For our work we asked a Laura Keil, a Berlin-based dancer to interpret a musical piece—Kreukeltape by Machinefabriek—as closely as possible with the movement of her own body. She was recorded by three depth cameras (Kinect), in which the intersection of the images was later put together to a three-dimensional volume (3D point cloud), which made it possible to use the collected data throughout the rest of the process. The three-dimensional image allowed us a completely free handling of the digital camera, without limitations on the perspective. The camera also reacts to the sound and supports the physical imitation of the musical piece by the performer. She moves to a noise field where a simple modification of the random seed can constantly create new versions of the video, each offering a different composition of the recorded performance. The multi-dimensionality of the sound sculpture is already contained in every movement of the dancer, as the camera footage allows any imaginable perspective.

192947.biography: **Daniel Franke** (DE) works as an artist, designer and music video director. His works challenge the restrictions of conventional spatial frameworks and concepts: digital simulations should no longer be limited to an on-screen-display; instead the digital might be imagined as transferable into real space and thus extend perceptions of “the real”. As a graduate of the Berlin University of the Arts he is currently preparing his main NaFoeG (Junior Scholars Support Program) work with Prof. Alberto de Campo. He is also member of the artist collective ChopChop. **Cedric Kiefer** (DE) studies in communication design at the University of Karlsruhe and Potsdam University of Applied Arts. He teaches generative design and processing at the Hildesheim University of Applied Sciences and Arts, Wiesbaden University of Applied Arts and Mainz University of Applied Arts. He is an author for _Weave_ magazine.

192960.name: Assassin's Creed Revelations
192960.description:
_Assassin’s Creed Revelations_ follows master assassin Ezio Auditore as he walks in the footsteps of his legendary mentor, Altaïr, on a journey to recover five ancient seals that hold the keys to the future of the Assassins brotherhood. It is a perilous path—one that will take Ezio to Constantinople, the heart of the Ottoman Empire, where a growing army of Templars threatens to destabilize the region.

The fourth title from the renowned series debuted on June 6, 2011; at Ubisoft’s E3 press conference and earned Digic the recognition for Best Trailer of E3 2011 by the editors and viewers of gamespot.com, gametrailers.com and 1up.com.

192979.name: Crossover
192979.description:
All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age. (_The Great Commission_, Matthew 28:18-20)

A new European colonial policy began with what is called the Reconquista, when Christians recaptured the Muslim-controlled areas of the Iberian Peninsula. And there was another reason for colonial expansion besides seeking gold: to spread the Christian faith. With the first colonies on the Dark Continent in the 15th century, not only traders and workers arrived in these still largely unknown regions, but also representatives of the church. As time passed, their influence on the populations there grew.

In the short film _Crossover_, I pose questions about religion and identity. Missionary work and the conversion of foreign cultures by representatives of the church are at the heart of this investigation. And yet this complex topic is not analyzed in a factual manner but explored on a more cinematic, symbolic level. In my short film, Christian missionary activity has been transferred to the animal kingdom in the forest. Indigenous populations are represented by fire bugs and set against a garden spider (with a cross-shaped mark on its back) that tricks the insects into converting.

Essentially, religions give orientation and enable people to navigate a world shaped by culture and conventions. A world view that has been formed by religious faith generates values and norms, objectives and purposes, and these form systems of meanings that, in turn, give orientation and so provide specific readings and modes of living. Every religious community defines itself by a number of iconographic allegories and these make it addressable and outwardly unmistakable. In _Crossover_, a pilgrimage – arranged artfully along signposts with the firebug’s image – leads through the forest and ends at the cross, the central symbol of the Occident.

193001.name: The Visual Effects and Animation of Rango
193001.description:
_Rango_ is an original animated comedy adventure that takes moviegoers for a hilarious and heartfelt walk in the Wild West. The story follows the comical, transformative journey of Rango (Johnny Depp), a sheltered chameleon living as an ordinary family pet while facing a major identity crisis. When Rango accidentally winds up in the gritty, gun-slinging town of Dirt—a lawless outpost populated by the desert’s most wily and whimsical creatures—the less-than-courageous lizard suddenly finds he stands out. Welcomed as the last hope the town has been waiting for, new Sheriff Rango is forced to play his new role to the hilt . . . until, in a blaze of action-packed situations and encounters with outrageous characters, Rango starts to become the hero he once only pretended to be.

_Rango_, directed by Gore Verbinski, won the Oscar for Best Animated Film in 2012.

193001.biography: Industrial Light & Magic (US), with locations in San Francisco and Singapore, is a Lucasfilm Ltd. company serving the digital needs of the entertainment industry for visual effects. Founded in 1975 by George Lucas, ILM has created visual effects for nearly 300 feature films, and has been awarded 15 Academy Awards for Best Visual Effects and received 24 Scientific and Technical Achievement Awards.

193002.name: The Fantastic Flying Books of Mr. Morris Lessmore
193002.authors: Moonbot Studios, Brandon Oldenburg, William Joyce
193002.description:
Inspired in equal measure by Hurricane Katrina, Buster Keaton, _The Wizard of Oz_ and a love for books, _The Fantastic Flying Books of Mr. Morris Lessmore_ is a story of people who devote their lives to books and books that return the favor. _Morris Lessmore_ is a poignant, humorous allegory about the curative powers of story. Using a variety of techniques (miniatures, computer animation, 2D animation), award-winning author/illustrator William Joyce and co-director Brandon Oldenburg present a hybrid style of animation that harks back to silent films and MGM Technicolor musicals. *Morris Lessmore* is old-fashioned and cutting-edge at the same time.
_The Fantastic Flying Books of Mr. Morris Lessmore_ was awarded the Oscar for Best Animated Short Film in the 84th Academy Awards.

193002.biography: William Joyce (US) has achieved world-wide recognition as an author, illustrator and leader in the digital animation industry. He was named by _Newsweek_ as one of the 100 people to watch in the new millennium and recognized as the Louisiana Author of the Year in 2008. Joyce has been heavily involved in the world of digital animation since its full-scale inception at Pixar Animation. Joyce is currently co-directing _The Guardians of Childhood_, an animated feature for DreamWorks. He is also the writer, producer and production designer on the Fox Studios feature film based on his book _The Leaf Men_. Brandon Oldenburg (US) was a co-founding member of Reel FX Creative Studios (1995), doing a combination of design and special effects for television and film. Serving as senior creative director for 15 years, he worked with such clients as Troublemaker Studios, Pixar, Disney, DreamWorks and Blue Sky Studios. From 1998 to 2009 Oldenburg oversaw a joint venture with William Joyce and Reel FX. Oldenburg and Joyce’s other collaborations include Halloween decor for Martha Stewart, parade floats for Disney and title design for feature films. Their most recent story is now in production at DreamWorks called _The Guardians of Childhood_.

193009.name: Caldera
193009.description:
_Caldera_ is an animated short film inspired by individuals struggling with psychotic disorders, and it venerates the brilliant minds forged in the haunted depths of psychosis. The story follows a young girl, a victim of a similar fate, who goes off her medication and leaves a bleak metropolis to immerse herself in a vibrant oceanic cove. Ultimately, the story is about the young girl’s impossible predicament, where she cannot live in either the fantastical and haunting world of psychosis or in the marginalizing society that mandates her medication.
_Caldera_ was invited to be made at Hampshire College in 2009 and was one of the first films to be a part of the Computer Graphics Incubator Program. The film was made during its three-year residence at Hampshire and had its world premiere at SXSW in March of 2012.

193047.name: fly tweet
193047.description:
The _fly tweet_ device sends Twitter messages based on the activities of a collection of houseflies. The flies live inside an acrylic sphere along with a computer keyboard. As they move and interact inside their home, they fly over the keys on the keyboard. These movements are collected in real time on video. As a particular key is triggered by the flies, the corresponding character is entered into a Twitter text box. When 140 characters are reached or the flies trigger the “enter” key, the message containing the accumulated characters is tweeted. Thus live Twitter messages are constantly sent in real time based on the simple movements of the community of houseflies. These continually accumulating messages appear as records of random activity within the larger sphere of social media and networking.

193047.biography: **David Bowen** (US) born in 1975, is a studio artist and educator whose work has been featured in numerous group and solo exhibitions nationally and internationally. Bowen’s work is concerned with aesthetics that result from interactive, reactive and generative processes as they relate to intersections between natural and mechanical systems. He is currently Associate Professor of Sculpture and Physical Computing at the University of Minnesota, Duluth.

193063.name: Memopol-2
193063.description:
_Memopol-2_ is a social machine that maps the visitor’s information field. When an identification document such as a national ID card or a passport is inserted into it, the machine starts collecting information about the visitor from (inter)national databases and the Internet. The data is then visualized on a large-scale custom display. People using the machine will be remembered by their names and portraits.

The Cyrillic spelling of the installation’s name refers to George Orwell’s concept of Big Brother from his dystopian novel *1984*. Over the past decades, technology has transformed the surveillance of society. When surfing the Internet, paying with an ATM card or using an ID card, people leave their digital traces everywhere. The Internet and social networks gather and provide a great deal of personal information, and a person’s profile is no longer constituted by his or her physical being alone. Background checks through Internet search engines and social network sites have become routine. _Memopol-2_ enables us to make a thorough background check on ourselves, mirroring our virtual image.

Estonia is well ahead of other countries in governmental data collecting. Estonia has used electronic ID cards for ten years and has built a system that interconnects all governmental databases. Personal ID-card readers provide a simple means of accessing the data. In the government portal, people can see their data, from prescription drugs to high school exams, from tax reports to driving licenses. The online interface has light green, friendly and trustful aesthetics. _Memopol-2_ is a reaction to these developments and uses contrasting aesthetics. It is big and evil, dark and scary. It projects present-day technology into retro-futuristic times. The tools of *1984* are already here, but the question is how do we use them. In peacetime these tools add a lot of comfort to everyday life, but what happens when the political winds change.

Links: http://works.timo.ee/memopol/

These mostly analyze, comment or reflect on developments in (information) society. He also likes working with projects to do with public space. His first solo exhibition was held in 2010 and was the start of the project presented here. His works are documented on his website [www.timo.ee](www.timo.ee "www.timo.ee").

193103.name: Versus
193103.description:
_Versus_ is a sound installation consisting of two kinetic sculptures placed face to face. Each sculpture is made of 12 triangular panels, hinged and powered by six linear actuators, controlled by a specific program. At the center of each corolla, a loudspeaker and a microphone make it possible to play and record sounds.

At regular intervals each sculpture produces a sound, simultaneously recorded and analyzed by the opposite sculpture, which then moves according to the frequencies of this sound.

Like a feedback loop, it then plays back the recorded sound, with the errors and disturbances caused by the reverberating space and the visitors.
By intervening in this conversation the viewers become actors, as they degrade the communication by their presence and the noises they produce. As the panels move back and forth at a pace determined by the environmental sound, they create a non-immediate interaction, where the imperfections of reproduction become creative elements.

The original sound is continuously transformed and becomes something entirely new and unpredictable. The memory of past events is held for a moment, until it is reproduced, degraded, and then forgotten, replaced by the present.

Links: http://www.davidletellier.net/works.html#versus
193103.biography: **David Letellier** (FR), born in 1978, lives and works in Berlin. He studied and graduated in architecture in Rennes and Berlin. His work focuses on the perception of sound and space, on the edge of architecture, sound and art. It ranges from audiovisual performances and sound installations to autonomous machines or conceptual drawings and can be defined as “an attempt to merge sound art and club culture.” He releases music on the German Raster-Noton label under the pseudonym Kangding Ray.

193116.name: Löschen/ DELETE
193116.description:
I have created a language to delete, to compact mental texts and graphics, to eliminate unwanted thoughts and make them personal hieroglyphics.
The performer is seated in front of the audience and simply starts writing on a laptop connected to a screen and stops when he or she cannot think/delete/write any more. The writing must be accompanied by an excessive and incoherent talkativeness. The performer invites the audience to participate and to delete/compact/maintain their own thoughts, keeping up an excessive and uncontrollable flow of words.

To create a language to delete: delete the language between humans and/or machines, hard drives, the memories, the alphabetic convention, textual noise, the “junk” operating systems, the satellite data, the identity online, the identity offline, the algorithmic remains on the hard drives that do not disappear under the hammer. A language to delete what is not possible to delete.

To generate a new alphabet, combine it and say it thinking all the time of erasing what is being said, the possibility of a language as black hole. Thinking and erasing in one action that does not generate remains … or alphabets.

Links: http://vimeo.com/36645107

193168.name: Solar Sinter Project
193168.description:
In a world increasingly concerned with questions of energy production and raw-material shortages, this project explores the potential of desert manufacturing, where energy and material are abundant.

In this experiment, sunlight and sand are used as raw energy and material to produce glass objects using a 3D printing process that combines natural energy and material with high-tech production technology.

Solar-sintering aims to raise questions about the future of manufacturing and triggers dreams of the full utilization of the production potential of the world’s most efficient energy resource—the sun. While not providing definitive answers, this experiment aims to provide a point of departure for fresh thinking.

Links: http://vimeo.com/27002363
193168.biography: **Markus Kaiser** (DE), born 1983. He studied 3D furniture and product design at London Metropolitan University from 2004 to 2008 and continued in 2009 with the study of product design at the Royal College of Art and gained his master’s in 2011. Markus Kaiser Studio was set up in London, UK, in 2011. The aim of the studio is to engage in discussion about opportunities in the production of design involving new as well as forgotten processes and technologies. The studio draws from science, art and engineering and aims to blur the gaps between seemingly separate fields.

193186.name: It's a jungle in here
193186.description:
How would you react if someone started behaving inappropriately, or aggressively? Do you try to pretend it isn’t happening, or protest and take action? This is the question posed by _It’s a jungle in here_, an interactive installation that puts two people into a simulated environment and has them respond to a series of increasingly unsettling encounters.

Participants sit down at an ornate wooden booth and, donning headphones, place their heads in one of two portholes in the front panel. On a screen inside the cabinet they see a stop-motion animation of paper characters on a train, two of which have a live video-feed of the face of each participant from a webcam inside the cabinet.

Three stories unfold, one after the other. Each person is cast as victim or attacker. As the stories progress through user interaction they become more aggressive and tense. At the climax of each scenario the attacker transforms into an animal, cathartically venting our shared anxiety through the iconography of ancient fables.

Participants interact with the work using either a button or a microphone. The person playing the attacker presses a large button to continue their actions at various points. The person playing the victim can shout into a microphone to protest.

Ultimately, _It’s a jungle in here_ investigates the use of power and how it is exercised to intimidate others both in real life and on-screen. It explores the relationship between our real selves and an on-screen persona that allows us to use and abuse our power. *It’s a jungle in here* disrupts the isolation and detachment of this on-screen self by creating an on-screen interaction that is simultaneously a physical interaction with a living, breathing person who is sitting right next to you. Part psychodrama, part multimedia marvel, *It’s a jungle in here* is a confronting tour of the fragile rules that organize our public lives.

Links: http://www.isobelandvan.com/jungle http://www.vimeo.com/isobelandvan/jungle

193193.name: LightType
193193.description:
_LightType_ is an installation questioning links between printed design and interactive design. Its main component is a cube made out of LEDs. Depending on which sides are on, we can create letters. The three-dimensional structure becomes a two-dimensional reading space.

The installation fetches tweets about a specified subject. When a message is tweeted, the structure reacts to it and creates each letter of each word. They are all captured on a webcam and the message is then projected on the wall to create a virtual poster.
