194548.biography: **Joe Davis** (US) is a research affiliate in the Department of Biology at MIT. He is an artist who has done extensive research in molecular biology and bioinformatics for the production of genetic databases and new biological art forms. He has also constructed sculptural installation pieces, laser teleoperator systems and structural welding in mild steel. His teaching experience in the MIT graduate architecture program and in undergraduate painting and mixed media at the Rhode Island School of Design has informed his artistic practice. He has exhibited in the United States, Canada and Europe.

194601.name: 18 Days in Egypt
194601.description:
_18 Days In Egypt_ is a collaborative documentary project to collect stories of the revolution and current events related to Egypt using social media fragments from tweets, to Facebook photos and posts, to Youtube videos, and photos. _18 Days In Egypt_ aims to capture the events of the revolution in an interactive documentary website that everyone can access now and in the future. It empowers Egyptians to preserve the incredible social media they have created—their on-the-ground, eye-witness accounts—and to add their voice to a story that is incredibly important to the world and its quotient of human freedom in these early years of the 21st century.

In the 18 days of the uprising, Egyptians by the thousands did what previous revolutionaries could not do: they personally documented their revolution, as it unfolded, on thousands of personal devices. They not only witnessed history—they recorded it. _18 Days in Egypt_ is an interactive documentary project that tells the story of the revolution, minute by minute, using these personal accounts. We want Egyptians to tell this story themselves, with their footage, their photos, their e-mails, their texts, their tweets and status updates—all created during the 18 days of the revolution.

Our team, based in Cairo and Silicon Valley, has already begun to create a unique social media space to gather and preserve thousands of media fragments from the revolution. Once sourced, the footage and associated stories will live in a searchable central archive on our interactive website[ 18DaysinEgypt.com](http://www.18DaysinEgypt.com " 18DaysinEgypt.com").

Links: www.18daysinegypt.com
194601.biography: **18 Days In Egypt** consists of a team of technologists, journalists and designers. GroupStream is Yasmin Elayat, Jigar Mehta, Caroline Oh, Mohamed ElShinnawy and Emerge Technology. Yasmin Elayat (CEO and co-founder) is a creative technologist and interaction designer. Jigar Mehta (co-founder) is video journalist previously with the _New York Times_, Caroline Oh (creative director) is a graphic and user-experience designer with a particular interest in film and narrative in design. Mohamed ElShinnawy, (technical lead) is a senior software engineer with a decade of experience. Our team also consists of six fellows, who are college-aged Egyptians with an interest in media, journalism and social justice.

194614.name: Safecast
194614.description:
_Safecast_ is a global project based in the US but currently focusing on outreach efforts in Japan. We are working to empower people with data about their environments, primarily by mapping radiation levels and building a sensor network, enabling people both to contribute and to freely use the data collected.

After the 3/11 earthquake and resulting nuclear situation at Fukushima Daiichi, it became clear that people wanted more data than was available. Through joint efforts with partners such as International Medcom and Keio University, _Safecast_ has been building a radiation sensor network made up of static and mobile sensors actively deployed around Japan—both in the exclusion zone around the reactor and elsewhere in the country.

_Safecast_ supports the idea that more data—freely available data—is better. Our goal is not to single out any individual source of data as untrustworthy, but rather to contribute to the existing measurement data and make it more robust. Multiple sources of data are always better and more accurate when aggregated.

While Japan and radiation is the primary focus of the moment, this work has made us aware of a need for more environmental data at a global level and the long-term work that _Safecast_ engages in will address these needs.

Links: http://safecast.org
194614.biography: **Safecast**. While core operations are based out of the Tokyo hackerspace, our team includes members from around the world including, Joi Ito (Cambridge), Bunnie Huang (Singapore), Sean Bonner (Los Angeles), Pieter Franken (Tokyo) and Ray Ozzie (Seattle).

194617.name: YoungAfricaLive
194617.description:
_YoungAfricaLive_ (YAL) is a mobile portal platform designed to communicate life-saving information about HIV/AIDS and sexual health to young people in a way that is engaging, interactive and relevant.

The idea was originally sparked by the discovery that in a country with the biggest HIV/Aids pandemic in the world, none of South Africa’s large mobile portals held a single piece of information about the pandemic—where to get tested, how to practice safe sex and how to avoid getting HIV/Aids. This gap created the opportunity for _YoungAfricaLive_ to be born.

YAL is an entertainment-oriented, fun, interactive and provocative social platform that enables young people to discuss topics close to them while at the same time disseminating important information and promoting sexual health. It does not simply state the facts and “lecture” young people about the dos and don’ts, but rather creates a space where young South Africans can talk about hot topics that affect their daily lives: love, sex, relationships, gender and cultural issues, as well as HIV/Aids. This edutainment approach has been extremely successful as our young audience does not feel it is being lectured but is able to engage in discussions with peers and enjoy time spent on the portal.

The key goals of _YoungAfricaLive_ are to:

1) Share information and educate:

2) Generate discussion, and

3) Promote HIV testing and normalize safe-sex practices
194617.biography: **YoungAfricaLive** (ZA). The core team carrying this project is a combination of writers, engineers and program managers. In each country, the team is made up of local content writers and/or bloggers, as well as content moderators. Centrally, the team is led by an overall content strategist, a lead engineer and a program manager. On 14 February 2012, _YoungAfricaLive_ had 838,800 unique users. YAL users are African young people aged predominantly between 18 and 25. They are predominantly urban, but we also see a lot of rural users on the platform.

194618.name: Dark Glasses. Portrait
194618.description:
_Dark Glasses. Portrait_ is an online campaign to support Chen Guancheng and calling for his freedeom. Chen Guangcheng is a blind civil-rights activist. He exposed the violent treatment of villagers during local-government implementation of China’s one-child policy in Linyi, Shandong province. This angered the authorities. He was sentenced to imprisonment for a fabricated crime of “damaging public property and disrupting traffic.” After he was released, Chen GuangCheng was put under house arrest by the government for no reason. Many supporters attempted to visit Chen and his family, however they were turned away by force, threatened, robbed, detained and in some cases severely beaten.

Chen’s ten-year-old son was forced to live with relatives in order to continue schooling. He was not even allowed to see his family on the Chinese New Year. Chen’s six year old daughter, Kesi, attended school under strict supervision by four to five ‘bodyguards’ following her to all her classes.

On April 20, 2012, Chen Guangcheng escaped from house arrest. On April 23, 2012, he was driven to Beijing. Later, friends took him to the American Embassy. After negotiations between the Chinese and United States governments, Chen Guangcheng was sent to Beijing Chaoyang hospital for medical treatment. On May 19, 2012, he and his family flew to the United States. The family now lives in New York.

The *Dark Glasses. Portrait* campaign calls on Chinese citizens and people around the world to express their concern and support for Chen Guangcheng. Every participant puts on a pair of dark glasses (sunglasses / blindfold), takes a portrait, writes a few words about their thoughts and sends the picture to the campaign. The pictures form a silent picture wall at *http://ichenguangcheng.blogspot.com/* to show our solidarity with Chen.

This campaign now has 636 photos and around 700 participants. People are showing great courage by participating even when they know that the campaign is monitored by the Chinese authorities.

Mosaic posters of the photos are used by NGOs such as China Aids, Women’s Rights without Frontiers, Front Line Defenders, Human Rights in China, The Alliance and activists in China. In the past few months, the mosaic picture spread quickly in China, Hong Kong, Taiwan and America. To show their support for Mr. Chen, people printed the mosaic image on banners, T-shirts, stickers and posters. The image from the Internet campaign thus began to appear on the street in various forms. The mosaic picture also appeared in various media reports, including RFA, China Real Time Report, ISunAffairs, China Files, Global Voices, etc and was mentioned three times in the US congressional hearings on Chen Guangcheng.
194618.biography: **Hexie Farm** (CN) is a freelance editorial cartoonist and author of *Hexie Farm*. He publishes political cartoons anonymously on the Internet. *Hexie Farm* is a series of political cartoons, depicting dictatorship, censorship, and propaganda in contemporary China. It has been banned in mainland China since 2011. He is also a member of the Cartoon Movement. Some his work has appeared in Isunaffairs, China Digital Times, the Cartoon Movement, PRI, Foreign Policy, RFI, Trend, DE, the China Rights Forum and other media.

194623.name: iStreet Lab
194623.description:
The _iStreet Lab_ is a community multimedia tool box, designed to deliver marginalized communities with the tools and skill required to bridge the digital divide. The lab is a stand-alone, operate-anywhere, music/video/digital media production/broadcasting kit inside a 240-liter wheelie bin.

We believe that even the most socially dysfunctional among us have valuable contributions to make to the development of our community/society, and creative media is one of the best methods of bringing about this productivity. This unique project packs digital media technologies inside a wheelie bin to bring technology to the most marginalized and disadvantaged youth wherever they are—street corner, community centre, shopping mall.

The education and engagement programs built around this technology have had significant success in shifting the youth away from drugs, alcohol and gang violence, putting them on a path to mainstream education and social reintegration. We combined these elements of engaging and teaching with a global perspective to create opportunities for young people to change themselves, their communities and the world, through unique and innovative initiatives that support knowledge exchange, skills building and collaboration.

The _iStreet_ skills-exchange project targets hard-to-reach and marginalized young people and will result in significant long-term outcome for individual participants, organizations and communities involved in the project and contribute to trans-literacy, economic and social development in these communities. All workshops are designed and implemented with this target group in mind. We are seeking to refine and design the delivery so there are lessons to be learned from each interaction as the participants themselves fashion their own learning and reinterpret their own margins. Within the _iStreet Lab_ it is our intention to create the technology and accessories necessary for us to break through the glass ceiling and finally go where no one has gone before.

The project was initiated in Jamaica in 2008 as a response to the rising levels of crime and violence in Palmers Cross Clarendon. In 2010/11 this method was successfully implemented in Queensland and New South Wales, Australia, with other outreach workshops and appearances in Canada and the UK.

Links: http://edgeqld.org.au/blog/2011/11/01/launching-the-lab/ http://istreetlab.ning.com/ http://www.dlux.org.au/cms/istreet.html http://istreetbhae.ning.com/ http://www.container-project.net/iStreetComic/Comic.html
194623.biography: **iStreet Lab** has been initiated by Mervin Jarman], a community art activist, and a founding member of the UK’s Mongrel Collective (www.mongrel.org.uk) who in 2003 initiated _The Container Project_ (www.container-project.net), a community media lab in a 40ft shipping container in rural Jamaica. The _iStreet Lab_ core team is an extended group of some 20 multimedia artist and technology developers who act as facilitators on demand for the project. The project acts primarily as a sensitization process and has included over 400 young people worldwide.

194639.name: XinCheJian: The First Hackerspace in China
194639.description:
_XinCheJian_, the first of many hackerspaces in China, is one of the many hundreds of such spaces all around the world. Each hackerspace is an autonomous entity, but they all share the same philosophy of having fun building things.

_XinCheJian’s_ mission is to support, create and promote physical computing, open-source hardware and the “Internet of Things.” To achieve this, _XinCheJian_ has talks, discussions, projects, startups promotion, workshops, competition organization and our own participation in international competitions.

Our long-term goal is to spread the concept and philosophy across China and inspire hackerspaces in every large city from east to west. We are doing this by creating a community loosely federated with the global community of hackerspaces across the world. The community favors fun, creativity, teamwork, problem-solving and openness to provide a learning and development opportunity to the Chinese people and foreigners in China.
We also maintain contact internationally with other hackerspaces, and we apply and participate in ambitious projects such as the Great Global Hackerspace Challenge (spring 2011; an international competition for all hackerspaces) and the 100 Year Starship project (fall 2011). Inside these projects we can build increasingly more complex cyber-electro-mechanical systems.

The community attracts visitors and projects, creating valuable connections between expats, local Chinese and returning Chinese and international visitors. _XinCheJian_ generates new skill sets with technology, valuable projects, innovative ideas and contacts across the tech communities, which offer a whole new pool of opportunities.

Links: www.xinchejian.com
194639.biography: **XinCheJian** (CN) was founded by: Min Lin Hsieh, community manager, who has been contributing her financial, organizational, marketing skills and experience in helping engineering projects and clubs since her college days; David Li, foreman, who has a network of contacts in the local community, is respected for his technical achievements and knowledge of open hardware; and Ricky Ng-Adam, project generator, who has ambitious ideas, engineering experience, strategic planning, community-building and evangelistic skills. As of March 2012, twelve members joined the founding of _XinCheJian 2.0_ with a 12-month pledge, sharing the responsibilities for funding _XinCheJian_ allowing us to move into a new space and operate for another 12 months.

194646.name: Apertus Open Source Cinema
194646.description:
The goal of the _Apertus Open Source Cinema_ project is to create a modular camera system composed from several hardware and software modules. Free (FLOSS) software and open hardware are to be utilized to build a device sporting all the features required by professional filmmakers in both studio and outdoor environments. The _Apertus_ project also sees itself as more than just a hardware/software initiative. It is a burgeoning platform for filmmakers, creative-industry professionals, artists and enthusiasts. _Apertus_ is a community movement, a forum of knowledge, an ecosystem of people supporting each other also advocating freedom. We actively cultivate: free technology, free information, free education, free knowledge, free culture, free arts, etc. This requires that everything we create shall be released to the public and protected with licences that ensure freedom as defined by the FSF (GNU GPL, Creative Commons, etc.).

Film production has long been consigned to the realm of a select few, high-end proprietary manufacturing corporations. Due to the expense involved in research, development and low-volume, high-tech manufacturing, their products were reserved for only the most well-funded clients. This represents the essence of a closed world. Only in recent years have revolutionary changes taken place, with smaller companies creating innovative cameras and other tools at lower prices. However, their technological secrets are protected at all costs, and manufacturers have blocked access to the internal design of their products in fear of losing market share. This has resulted in vague or missing documentation, threats to void warranty—to prevent attempts at reverse engineering–—and artificially crippled features. This leads to the paradoxical situation where the technology for filmmaking is now widely affordable at the expense of the loss of freedom to use these tools.

We at _Apertus_ believe in open development and rely on fulfilling the four essential freedoms: freedom to access, use and study all knowledge; freedom to modify and change anything; freedom to redistribute all original knowledge; freedom to redistribute all modified and changed knowledge. In the beginning _Apertus_ was just about building an open camera. As of 2012, it has become a much broader initiative. It now represents:

—A movement actively spreading the idea of sharing knowledge and working together collaboratively

—A pool of filmmakers and creative-industry professionals collaborating on professional cinema and arts productions

— A missionary, encouraging individuals to develop an active mind, question what has come before them and give back to their respective communities

—A group that researches and publishes knowledge, gives talks, holds workshops and events

—A pool of developers working on free software and open hardware for film- and post-production.

Links: http://www.apertus.org
194646.biography: _Apertus Open-Source Cinema_. The core team currently consists of around 15 people. The membership forum currently has over 100 registered users. Anyone can join the community and engage in interaction/discussion or by contributing to the project. The entire community is very difficult to measure, but in combined social media we have a direct reach of around 1000 people.

194662.name: Europe versus Facebook
194662.description:
It all started when Max Schrems, an Austrian law student, met members of Facebook’s privacy team during his exchange semester at Santa Clara University, California. After being stunned at their “reinterpretation” of European data-protection legislation, he wrote a paper on the issue. To do so he asked some friends in Austria to make an access request at Facebook Ireland, the contractor for all Facebook users outside of US and Canada. After receiving three data sets with up to 1,222 pages of data, it was clear that this ought to be published online. Later it was discovered that the data sets also included massive amounts of “deleted” data. The group of students again asked themselves why no one was doing anything about this. So they decided simply to transform the law-school paper into 22 complaints filed with the Irish Data Protection Commissioner (DPC), who is responsible for Facebook’s operations. At the same time they published a simple explanation of how users could access their data, which soon became viral on the Internet and was linked to by the mass media and copied by blogs all around the world. According to Facebook, by December 2011, 40,000 users had made such a request. The Irish DPC published a first report in December 2011, demanding massive changes by Facebook Ireland. According to Facebook representatives these are among the most far-reaching changes on the privacy front that the company has ever had to undertake.

We are currently working on our goal to get a formal decision that will hopefully be much further reaching than this first report. At the same time the mass media as well as politics has picked up on the project. This enabled us to explain all around the world what data Facebook is gathering and how it uses it. Even Viviane Reding, (EU Justice Commissioner) quoted our case when presenting the new European proposal for stricter data-protection legislation.

Links: www.europe-v-facebook.org
194662.biography: **Europe versus Facebook** is more or less a scattered group of about ten students with one person (Max Schrems) taking the leading role. All complaints are in his name, since he is the group’s only expert on data protection. He is supported by other members who help with press releases, corrections, the web page or by answering e-mails. The group is considering becoming a non-profit organization, especially as it will soon need to manage external funding (so far the only cost is a server). At the same time the complaints and legal action will ultimately have to go through an individual, which is currently Max Schrems.

194667.name: CRONICAS DE HEROES
194667.description:
_Crónicas de Héroes_ is a civic platform of positivism which through technology, art, education, direct insertion and other media focuses and promotes social values—responsibility, honesty, equality, respect, dignity, kindness, solidarity and cooperation. _Crónicas de Héroes_ provides citizens with both online and offline tools to make public, carry out and share with other positive contributions to society.

Since the launch of _Crónicas de Héroes_ in Juarez, Mexico, in December 2010, many newspapers, radio stations and television outlets have picked up and written stories about the more than 1,300 positive citizens reports that have been logged and mapped on our website: http://juarez.cronicasdeheroes.mx. The mapping tool illustrates both the location and density of positive actions happening in this city. The Juárez community has embraced the initiative as a tool to establish public activities aimed at regaining a civic presence in the city, such as collective public paints in collaboration with street artists and the community who have created murals in different spaces around the city inspired by the positive reports on our site.

Currently, _Crónicas de Héroes_ is also being deployed in Monterrey, Mexico, [(http://mty.cronicasdeheroes.mx/](http://mty.cronicasdeheroes.mx/ "http://mty.cronicasdeheroes.mx/")) and Tijuana/San Diego, CA [(http://tj-sd.cronicasdeheroes.mx/](http://tj-sd.cronicasdeheroes.mx/ "http://tj-sd.cronicasdeheroes.mx/")), our first bi-national platform.

_Crónicas de Héroes_ aspires to reach and to influence a broad community of all ages, genders, and economic status in these communities, using new and old media as well as grassroots activism.

_Crónicas de Héroes_ was originally established in New York after the 9/11 events as *Hero Reports*, a project carried out by Alyssa Wright, a student from the Center for Civic Media /MIT Media Lab. It was a reaction to the NY Metropolitan Transit Authority’s “See Something, Say Something” campaign, which focused on reporting suspicious activity. In contrast, *Hero Reports* directed civic energy toward reporting positive activities that encourage constructive societal changes.

Links: www.cronicasdeheroes.mx
194667.biography: **Crónicas de Héroes** is led by Yesica Guerra and local advisory boards from the cities in which is implemented—Juarez, Monterrey, and Tijuana/San Diego. Yesica, a researcher in urban design with a master’s degree in architecture and urbanism from MIT, devotes most of her research to border issues between Mexico and the United States.

194681.name: Meine Abgeordneten
194681.description:
_Meine Abgeordneten_ (My Members of Parliament) is an online database of publicly available information (“dossiers”). on Austrian politicians It lists their CVs, past and present jobs, engagements in companies and NGOs as well as memberships in various politically relevant organizations. The project also lists all parliamentary speeches and press releases, which can be tagged according to pre-defined political topics. By combining the information from the dossier with the actual political agenda of a politician, conclusions on possible conflicts of interest can be drawn.

_Meine Abgeordneten_ came into being at the initiative of the president of the Respekt.net association, Martin Winkler. It is a platform for socio-political involvement that brings people with ideas together with potential supporters. With the project exchange, Respekt.net aims above all to help individual people and groups to find a lively forum for their commitment and to support projects with which citizens and organizations promote private, economic and public life.

The project is expandable in every direction. Currently it lists the members of the Austrian parliament, the Austrian MEPs and members of the Council of Ministers.The target audience of the project is primarily journalistic and academic, although it is already popular with the general public since its very successful launch in November 2011.

Links: http://www.meineabgeordneten.at/ http://twitter.com/MeineAbg
194681.biography: The **Meine Abgeordneten** (AT) platform is a private initiative of Respekt.net. The creation of the platform was funded by 200 individual donations from private donors. _Meine Abgeordneten_ is strictly politically independent and exclusively committed to the creation of political transparency.

194683.name: Syrian People Know Their Way
194683.description:
_Syrian People Know Their Way_ is a community of young Syrian digital artists, designers, bloggers and activists who aim both to gather and provide inspiration for the Syrian struggle for freedom.

The project started as a Facebook page on Feb 26, 2011, to open the door for an analysis of Syria’s situation and where it was heading, as we were able to see a change coming to Syria with the wider and bigger change hitting other countries in the area. We all had one goal: we all support the democratic change, political discourse and the media of the revolution.

That was before the revolution started. Then, after the revolution in Syria officially started, other pages and organizations were working on getting the news out and sharing it on Facebook and Twitter. We felt that it was our duty to do something, to get more involved.

We thought one way of doing this would be to find a different way of transferring the news to and from the people, using all the available methods of media and working with activists on the ground, aiming to provide a political and theoretical view about daily events in Syria. We wanted to focus more on the human side of the revolution, the people, the Syrians, and wanted to provide the revolution with art that would be noticed and communicate the Syrian face to the world and to the Syrians themselves.

We are doing this through modern art and technology in a simple, straightforward way that everyone can understand this. Our work is inspired on the one hand by the activists on the ground and on the other hand by supporting them with practical ideas and theoretical thoughts of the everyday life that they are experiencing. We try to present our works of art in a way that makes it close to the street and away from the “art salon” type. To do so, we to use elements from Syrian folklore and language, formulating them in an open way that reflects the human heritage rather than using complex texts, simplifying the complex political concepts by formulating them in short phrases and in a popular manner or sometimes even in funny phrases. On the other hand, trying to keep a degree of depth and avoiding shallowness.

Our work is divided into various overlapping fields. For example some art pieces are based on the mixing idea; we take a well-known painting and merge it with Arabic calligraphy to show the humanistic dimension of the revolution, expressing elements that people in the streets concerned with, trying to reflect their voices. We also have work that uses art and beauty to provide the people with ways to peacefully re-evaluate, using history and experience. An example of this work would be the art that depends on the aesthetic dimension to provide practical ideas to the Syrian people. Supporting them in the non-violent revolution (movement) against the regime.

We target the audience of the silent (neutral) people who have yet not decided to take sides, by offering them political views and different ideas about the revolution in relation to political events in Syria—and sometimes in the region. We open the door to more thoughts and ideas within (and from) the whole society and so these groups of people will not feel left out of the “future Syria” that we dream of and fight for, with an independent youth media that would be able to make their voices heard in public space regardless of what it is or in what category it fits.

Links: http://www.youtube.com/syrianintifada https://www.facebook.com/Syrian.Intifada?sk=info https://twitter.com/#!/search/%40sha3eb3aref http://www.flickr.com/photos/3aref/?saved=1 http://sha3b3aref.blogspot.com/
194683.biography: _Syrian People Know Their Way_ is a digital community of young Syrian digital artists, designers, bloggers and activists that aim to both gather and provide inspiration for the Syrian struggle for freedom.

194689.name: The Johnny Cash Project
194689.description:
_The Johnny Cash Project_ is a global collective public art project. Inspired by individually supplied frames of archival footage and through the use of a custom drawing tool, participants are invited to create and share their vision of the Man in Black. These unique and personal portraits are then strung together and played in sequence over the song “Ain’t No Grave,” creating a moving, ever-evolving homage to the musical icon. The result: an evolving, crowd-sourced animated music video, rising from a sea of one-of-a-kind portraits.

Links: http://www.thejohnnycashproject.com/
194689.biography: **The Johnny Cash Project** was conceived of and created by Chris Milk and Aaron Koblin. Aaron Koblin (US) is an artist and designer who works with data and digital technologies. Chris Milk (US) is an music video director and photographer. There have been more than a million users on the site, with hundreds of thousands of contributions. Participants include fans of Johnny Cash, passionate artists, illustrators and regular old Joes. The project is open to anyone who is interested in participating. Submissions are moderated to make sure they are not offensive but are otherwise accepted into the project.

194693.name: Texting for Democracy
194693.description:
_Kubatana_ uses e-mail, SMS and post to communicate with a wide and diverse network of Zimbabwean individuals and organizations. Our SMS membership of over 30,000 subscribers is distributed across the country, with a third based in Harare, a third in Zimbabwe’s other cities and towns and a third in rural areas and growth points.

This reach makes us particularly able to take advantage of the immediacy and interactivity of SMS and mobile communications. Our SMS survey is regularly used as a two-way communication tool, in which people share their feedback, tips and suggestions with us, and through which we invite feedback, opinions and observations on timely and relevant topics.

_Kubatana_ uses Clickatell’s online bulk SMS service to send out text messages to our subscribers. The sender ID facility on Clickatell enables us to set the sender identity that the messages are sent from. In our case, this is the phone number of the dedicated SMS line at our office. _Kubatana_ has used this two-way SMS feedback channel in a number of ways in the past year, to “crowd source” opinion and information and to help develop a broader picture of local and national events.

For example, in February 2011 we received a phone call from a trusted civil-society ally, informing us of violence in central Harare. We sent out a text message to our subscribers informing them of this report, advising them to be careful and asking them to submit their reports and observations. We received over 200 replies from subscribers, some of whom were in the city center at the time, and some of whom were using the opportunity to report on the violence they were experiencing in Harare and farther afield. This feedback enabled us to build a picture of events taking place and report on them on our community blog.

In early 2012, Harare and other cities were increasingly experiencing typhoid cases—at an extent atypical for Zimbabwe. We sent out a text message to our subscribers asking how typhoid had affected their communities and what they thought government should do. We received around 200 responses. We then used the free online mapping capacity on ArcGIS to plot these comments, which centered around Harare but were also distributed around the country.
_Kubatana_ hopes increasingly to use mapping and data visualization techniques to share information from our subscribers and to create an even greater sense of community within our membership. In our experience, Zimbabweans have limited avenues through which to express themselves freely and therefore greatly value the two-way communications platform _Kubatana_ provides through email, SMS and other new and traditional media.

Links: www.kubatana.net
194693.biography: **The Kubatana Trust of Zimbabwe** (ZW) aims to strengthen the use of e-mail and Internet strategies in Zimbabwean NGOs and civil society organizations. _Kubatana_ makes human rights and civic education information accessible from a centralized, electronic source.

194707.name: iHub - Nairobi's Innovation Hub
194707.description:
Kenya has set up a robust telecommunications infrastructure and high-capacity international gateways. The country has also made remarkable progress putting an ICT policy framework and implementation strategy in place, complete with measurable outcomes and time-frames.

In conjunction with this rapidly growing number of mobile and Internet users, supporting government policy and infrastructure, the number of computer science and IT students graduating each year continues to increase both in public and private universities. This seems to indicate great potential in ICT not only for current growth in the country but sustained future growth as well.

One quickly emerging digital community is _iHub_, which was opened in March 2010. _iHub_ can boast of more than 6,000 virtual members, who interact via the web platform, 240 green members, who physically access the space, and nine red members, who pay for a semi-permanent desk space for a period of six to 12 months. _iHub_ is a network and meeting place that enables Kenya’s innovators to bring their ideas to fruition. Through _iHub_, the technology community, industry, academia, investors and venture capitalists can meet, share ideas and collaborate. The centre is the first of its kind to operate in Africa. It allows technologies to progress from the ideas stage to becoming real products and the key to its effectiveness is open innovation—the process of combining internal and external ideas, as well as internal and external paths to market, to advance the development of new technologies.

Links: ihub.co.ke
194707.biography: The **iHub** management team consists of passionate, hard-working people who genuinely care about the community because they are part of it. The management team exists to facilitate and support the community but the community themselves are the heart behind *iHub*. The iHub advisory board is made up of five people from the Nairobi tech community: Riyaz Bachani, Wananchi executive, now in charge of Wazi WiFi; Josiah Mugambi, co-founder of Skunkworks, works at Nokia Siemens; Rebeccah Wanjiku, technology reporter and founder of Fireside Communications; Conrad Akunga, blogger, co-founder of Mzalendo and highly respected software architect; Erik Hersman, technology blogger and co-founder of Ushahidi.

194714.name: Lorea
194714.description:
_Lorea_ is a seedbed of free social networks linked by federation protocols that allow them to communicate. These networks run on software designed and built by and for non profits, members of the public and groups involved in social change. _Lorea_Lorea_Lorea_ is not just software, but also a technical and political tool for the federated web, bringing back autonomy, freedom and total control over our data and our memory to the hands of the users of social networking sites themselves. The federation knocks down the walls of the panopticon 2.0 run by corporations and political interests, and defends the neutrality of networks as a fundamental architectural principle.

_Lorea_ arises from an informal collective of people concerned about security and privacy issues on the social web. Since 2009 this developer community has grown and is now formed by virtually all kinds of people inhabiting various online networks. Hence, amongst _Lorea_ developers we don't speak about service "users" but of "inhabitants" of a transformative project: several thousand people who knowingly use our networks, many of them active in IT development , server maintenance, error reporting and solving, documentation, project support and dissemination. _Lorea_ survives daily via the work of a community which organises by means of an online version of a democratic people's assembly. It is based on mutual cooperation, promoting free culture and social innovation.

The project is aimed at civil society as a whole, i.e. citizens and social collectives and political change organisations that are motivated by the desire to interact, share, change things together, devise solutions. We seek to address all people and groups who value their online identities and their security and privacy . We value the right to freedom of expression, and the right to share information and knowledge and do so within a free and neutral social web. _Lorea_ offers a non-profit alternative to regain our technological sovereignty in the world of social networks.

Links: www.lorea.org
194714.biography: **Lorea**. The team was launched during the Hackmeeting, the annual gathering of hackers in Spain, in October 2009. At this meeting groups administering the _Lorea_ based Arte Libre Digital (ALD) and the social network N-1 converged and decided to join forces to further develop free, secure, federated and self-managed social networks. Our technical team is composed of more or less 10 people but that number is variable. We have 3 people who are more concerned with documentation issues, translation, presentation and workshops.

194780.name: Das Superhirn
194780.description:
Die Idee zu einem gemeinsamen Filmprojekt mit Stefan Ludwig und der damaligen 3E entstand schon ein Schuljahr vor der tatsächlichen Realisierung. Stefan Ludwig hat als Filmemacher und Drehbuchautor schon viel mit Kindern und Jugendlichen gearbeitet. Wir überlegten uns einen Arbeitstitel und einen inhaltlichen Ausgangspunkt, der „Meine Stadt der Zukunft“ war. Unser Ziel und die Aufgabenstellung an die SchülerInnen war es, einen Kurzfilm mit selbst gebauten Kulissen und realen Figuren zu machen.

Die SchülerInnen haben in Teams von 4 bis 5 Personen ihre Geschichte entwickelt, dazu die Hauptfigur und die Kulissen entworfen und gebaut. In vielen Gesprächen wurden die Geschichten gesammelt und zu einem Hauptgeschehen zusammengesetzt. So wurde aus den einzelnen unabhängigen Ideen eine zusammenhängende, einheitliche Story der ganzen Klasse, die in ein Drehbuch umgeschrieben wurde.

Die Kulissen wurden im Rahmen des BE-Unterrichtes dreidimensional gebaut und aufwändig gestaltet. An zwei langen Drehtagen wurden auf der Bühne des Festsaals der Schule die Kulissen abgefilmt und die Szenen vor einem Green-Screen gedreht, vertont und synchronisiert. Stefan Ludwig hat den Film abschließend geschnitten und die Endbearbeitung gemacht. Das fertige Filmprojekt bekam von der Klasse einstimmig den bezeichnenden Titel.

Links: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mdgo8hOAGDg&feature=related
194780.biography: Die 26 SchülerInnen besuchten zum Projektdurchführungszeitraum die 3E des Wasagymnasiums in Wien 9. Im Rahmen des BE-Unterrichtes wurde mit der finanziellen Unterstützung des Elternvereins und Kultur Kontakt Wien das Filmprojekt _Das Superhirn_ unter der Leitung des Filmemachers Stefan Ludwig und Marlis Cermak realisiert.

194781.name: BioBookCover
194781.description:
Gummibärchen statt Plastik. So lautet die Antwort unserer Projektgruppe „BioBookCover“ auf das aktuelle Plastikproblem. Wir suchten nach einer umweltfreundlichen Alternative zu herkömmlichen Buch- und Heftumschlägen in unserer unmittelbaren Umgebung, der Schule, wo wir unglaubliche Müllberge aus Kunststoff orteten. Als Projektgruppe „BioBookCover“ fanden wir eine gut verdauliche Lösung: Mit Unterstützung der Lehrer für Wirtschaft & Recht und Chemie entwickelten wir in einer langen Forschungs- und Entwicklungsphase eine innovative Antwort auf das Plastikproblem:
Wir produzieren und vermarkten bunte Buch- und Heftumschläge sowie die Schutzhülle „Cortex“ aus kompostierbarem Bioplastik, hergestellt aus pflanzlichen Komponenten. Wie Gummibärchen bestehen auch die Öko-Hüllen aus Wasser, Kartoffelstärke, Gelatine und Lebensmittelfarben. Attraktive Designs in Veilchenfarben, Waldmeistergrün, Kirschrot oder Sonnengelb machen unsere Biocovers seit einiger Zeit zu einem Must-have für alle Bücherliebhaber, die unserer Umwelt etwas Gutes tun wollen.

Um unsere Idee weiter zu professionalisieren, erarbeiten wir derzeit ein unternehmerisches Konzept in Zusammenarbeit mit Innolab von Campus02 Graz. Unser erklärtes Ziel ist es, einen Unternehmenspartner in Österreich zu finden, um in die industrielle Fertigung unserer Biohüllen einsteigen zu können.

Links: www.biobookcover.at
194781.biography: **BioBookCover-Projektgruppe**: Die 14 SchülerInnen besuchen die 8B und 8C-Klasse des BG/BRG Stainach in der Steiermark mit dem Schwerpunkt Wirtschaft und Recht.

194835.name: RiffGrabber
194835.authors: Alin Kalam, Wolfgang Schneiderbauer, Manmeet Singh, Christian Sorko, HTL Ottakring, Peter Paikl
194835.description:
Ziel der Diplomarbeit _RiffGrabber_ war die Entwicklung einer Software, die Gitarrenriffs in Echtzeit transkribiert. Der User kann eine Tonfolge mit der an ein Audio-Interface angeschlossenen Gitarre am Computer (z. B. via Mikrofoneingang) einspielen oder eine Audiodatei im Programm öffnen und wiedergeben. Die Tonfolge wird in Echtzeit vom Programm analysiert, wiedererkannt und aufgezeichnet. Die Töne werden dabei in Form von Tabulaturen (Tabs) notiert. Diese Tabs können dann als Textdokument auf dem Computer gespeichert werden, um sie je nach Bedarf wieder anzeigen zu können.

Ergänzend wurde eine Website[ www.riffgrabber.at](http:// www.riffgrabber.at "www.riffgrabber.at") mit Benutzerverwaltung erstellt, die als Social Network fungiert, wo die User ihre am Computer erstellten Tabs hochladen, anzeigen, abspielen, freigeben, löschen und Tabs anderer User downloaden können. Des Weiteren wurden einige Tonanalyse- bzw. Hilfetools für Gitarristen entwickelt, die besonders für die autodidaktischen Anfänger sehr hilfreich sind: ein Stimmgerät, ein Synthesizer, eine Akkordbibliothek und ein Metronom. Diese Tools gibt es für Windows und als Android-App.

Beim Gitarrespielen ordnet die Software die Noten in Echtzeit auf einem x-y-Notengraf so an, dass der Musiker leicht die einzelnen Oktaven (selbe Noten in anderen Frequenzbereichen, hoch/tief) erkennen kann.

Da es bereits einige Gitarrensoftware auf dem Markt gibt, die sich nur auf die manuelle Tabschreibung konzentrieren, hatte die Gruppe die Idee, eine Software zu schreiben, die eine automatische Tabschreibung in Echtzeit ermöglicht. Besonders Musikern, die in Bands spielen und sich zwangsläufig täglich mit der händischen Tabschreibung auseinandersetzen müssen, kommt die Software sehr entgegen.

Links: http://www.riffgrabber.at/ http://twitter.com/RiffGrabber http://www.facebook.com/RiffGrabber
194835.biography: **Alin Kalam, Peter Paikl, Wolfgang Schneiderbauer, Manmeet Singh und Christian Sorko** besuchen die 5. Klasse der HTBLA-Ottakring in Wien mit dem Schwerpunkt Netzwerktechnik in der Abteilung Informationstechnologie.

194843.name: state of revolution
194843.authors: Agnes Aistleitner, HBLA für künstlerische Gestaltung Linz
194843.description:
Im Jänner 2012, fast ein Jahr nach den größten Protesten in Ägypten, befinde ich mich auf einer Reise durch Kairo – auf den Spuren der Revolution. In einer Gesprächsrunde und in Begegnungen auf offener Straße versuche ich, Aspekte der politischen Ereignisse, des sogenannten „Arabischen Frühlings“ in Ägypten, zu ermitteln.

_Reale Konfrontation trifft auf Internet-Recherche_

In meiner Videoarbeit ermittle ich Informationen zum Thema im Internet, diese Informationen treffen in meiner Arbeit auf den Realbezug.
Wie ist es wirklich? Der Rezipient meines Videos wird virtuell von der Observierung aus der Ferne zur Konfrontation vor Ort geführt.
In etwa 15 Minuten gebe ich Einblick in Eindrücke meiner Reise. Ich dokumentiere die Begegnung mit Studenten und einem Professor in einer Gesprächsrunde, in der über die Revolution gesprochen und philosophiert wird, aber auch die zufälligen Begegnungen auf der Straße, die einen Einblick in das facettenreiche Leben Kairos zeigen, werden festgehalten. Dazwischen stehen meine Recherchen am Computer, die mich als Beobachter aus der Ferne zeigen.

Ich gehe auf die Straße, um den Menschen zu begegnen: Ob durch die Märkte Kairos am Abend, auf der Straße oder am Tahrir-Platz, im Laufe des Videos treffe ich auf unterschiedliche Menschen, die unterschiedliche Meinungen zum Revolutionsgeschehen preisgeben.
In meiner Arbeit beleuchte ich verschiedene Aspekte des Geschehens und versuche, die Komplexität und Dynamik der Angelegenheit für den Betrachter zu verdeutlichen.
194843.biography: **Agnes Aistleitner**, geb. 1993, besucht seit 2007 die HBLA für künstlerische Gestaltung in Linz, die sie im Juni 2012 abgeschlossen hat. 2010 verbrachte sie ein Auslandssemester in Japan. Seit 2009 hat sie zahlreiche Praktika im Kunst-, Mode- und PR-Bereich in Wien, Los Angeles und New York absolviert. Im Jahr 2012 gründet sie die Organisation „Globalcitizen“, in deren Rahmen Mode, Kunst und Veranstaltungen entstehen.

194844.name: Bin Baum mit 2 Stämmen
194844.authors: Stephan Friedl, Asya Serimoglu, Anita Simic, Daniel Wieczorek, Lorena Zorkic, RadioPoly PTS 3, Vienna
194844.description:
_Bin Baum mit 2 Stämmen_ entstand nach intensiver Auseinandersetzung mit unserer Herkunft als Jugendliche mit nichtdeutscher Muttersprache im Rahmen einer Radiosendung von RadioPoly.

Ausgangspunkt war ein Interview, das unser Projektleiter, Helmut Hostnig, als Audiobrief aus Tetovo in Mazedonien mitgebracht hat, in dem sich zwei junge Albanerinnen, die lange Zeit in Österreich verbracht haben, darüber beklagen, dass sie sich in ihrer Heimat nicht mehr wirklich zu Hause fühlen. Das hat uns daran erinnert, dass auch in uns zwei Herzen schlagen: eines für das Land, aus dem wir oder unsere Eltern kommen, und das andere für Österreich, wo wir leben, zur Schule gehen und unsere Zukunft sehen.

Mit dem Videogedicht, dessen Bilder in knappen drei Stunden entstanden sind und das einen Text zur Grundlage hat, den uns der Projektleiter auf den Leib geschrieben und dann die Mutter von Asya ins Gesicht geschminkt hat, wollen wir aufzeigen, dass Integration trotz Migration gelingen kann, wenn unsere multikulturelle Herkunft nicht als Bedrohung, sondern als Bereicherung verstanden wird.

Wen ein detaillierteres Making-of dieser Gedichtvisualisierung interessiert, der sei auf unseren Blog verwiesen:[ http://radiopoly.wordpress.com]( http://radiopoly.wordpress.com " http://radiopoly.wordpress.com")

Links: http://radiopoly.wordpress.com/2011/06/06/bin-baum-mit-zwei-stammen-3/
194844.biography: **RadioPoly** ist ein Pilotprojekt des BMUKK in Kooperation mit dem Medienzentrum Wien und der Polytechnischen Schule Meiselgasse im dritten Wiener Gemeindebezirk und wird seit 2010 vom Projektleiter, Helmut Hostnig, und seinen pädagogischen BetreuerInnen, Gabriela Pranieß und Florian Danhel, mit dem Anspruch geführt, Jugendliche mit Radio als einem Medium der Kommunikation vertraut zu machen.

194854.name: Flat Water Bottle/Evolution of Animation
194854.description:
In meinem Werbe-Film _Flat Water Bottle_ geht es um die Präsentation einer flachen Plastikflasche. Die Animation habe ich in Blender 3D gemacht und anschließend im Programm Pinnacle Studio nachbearbeitet und zusammengeschnitten.

In meinem Film _Evolution of Animation_ geht es um die Geschichte der Animation und des Films. Im Laufe der Geschichte kommt immer der gleiche Charakter vor – ein einfaches Strichmännchen mit Augen. Es beginnt mit einer Stop-Motion-Animation, die in schwarz-weiß aufgenommen ist, in dem der Charakter immer weiter nach rechts geht. Nachdem die Figur hinter einer Mauer verschwindet, kommt sie als Zeichentrick-Charakter wieder heraus. Die 2D–Animation (anfangs auch in schwarz-weiß) habe ich zuerst mit der Hand gezeichnet und dann in dem Programm Toon Boom Animate bearbeitet. In der schwarz-weißen 2D–Welt geht die Figur weiter, und plötzlich kommt aus einem Lautsprecher Musik – das soll für die Entstehung des Tonfilms stehen. Dann fährt ein Pinsel über das Bild, und plötzlich ist das Bild in Farbe, um die Entstehung des Farbfilms zu zeigen. Dann geht der Charakter weiter und verschwindet wieder hinter einer Wand. Als er hervorkommt, ist er in einer 3D–Welt (den 3D–Teil habe ich in Blender 3D gemacht). Anschließend verschwindet er wieder hinter einer Mauer, und danach ist die Animation in rot/blau 3D (mit echter 3D–Brille). Dann wirft die Figur eine Brille vor die Kamera, und das Bild wird schwarz. Am Schluss des Films habe ich ein weißes Licht erscheinen lassen, um zu zeigen, dass sich die Technik immer weiter entwickeln wird.
194854.biography: **Michael Schmidl**, geb. 1998, besucht zurzeit die 8. Schulstufe des BRG 14 Linzerstraße in Wien. Am liebsten arbeitet er an Animationen und Filmen und möchte später Animator oder Regisseur werden. 2010 hat er bereits mit seinem Film _Vom Himmel gefallen_ den u14-Sachpreis bei u19 gewonnen.

194861.name: Balancing Robot
194861.authors: Christian Grill, Magdalena Kranjec, Sonja Stankovic, Maximilian Tabelander, Sasa Vasilijkovic, NMS-Telfs-Dr.-Aloys-Weissenbach
194861.description:
Begonnen hat alles mit Sasa, als dieser im EDV-Raum ein Hinterradteil entdeckte. Sofort kam es ihm in den Sinn, ein Projekt für u19 zu gestalten, und er fragte auch gleich unseren Herrn Fachlehrer Bellony, ob er Zeit hätte, bei dem Projekt mitzumachen. Herr Bellony sagte zu und beauftragte Sasa, noch Schüler zu suchen, die sich beteiligen wollen. Sasa machte sich auf die Suche und sofort waren Christian, Maximilian, Magdalena und Sonja dabei.

Nach langem Überlegen kamen wir auf die Idee, dass unser Roboter einen Motor steuern könnte, der dann die Felge des alten Fahrradteils hin und her bewegt. Ganz oben auf der Felge sollte sich ein Fahrzeug befinden, das nicht herunterrollen darf. Über die Messwerte eines Ultraschallsensors und einer mathematischen Logik wird die Radfelge so mit dem Motor gedreht, dass das Fahrzeug nicht herunterfällt.

Nachdem das bestehende alte Rad für unsere Zwecke bearbeitet worden war, fügten wir einen Stopparm, verschiedene Felgenfahrzeuge und Motorhaltungen hinzu. Dann bauten wir den grauen Motor von Lego ein und errichteten beidseitige Stoppvorrichtungen. Als nächstes änderten wir das Programm so um, dass nicht immer die volle Energie am Motor ist, sondern die Motorleistung sich mit dem Abstand zwischen kleinem Wagen und Sensor ändert. Zum Schluss bauten wir den _Balancing Robot_ auch noch zu einem Geschicklichkeitsspiel um, das man durch ein zusätzliches Lenkrad steuern kann.
194861.biography: Die an diesem Projekt beteiligten Mädchen besuchen die 4. Klasse der NMS-Telfs-Dr.-Aloys-Weissenbach mit dem Schwerpunkt „Sprache“, die Buben gehen in die 4. Klasse mit dem Schwerpunkt „BioTeC“.

194863.name: Impressive Title (Paradise)
194863.description:
Der Trickfilm _Impressive Titel (Paradise)_ soll die Suche nach der Freiheit und der eigenen Identität widerspiegeln. Der Wolf steht symbolisch für den Menschen, denn wie der Wolf ist der Mensch auch ein einsamer Jäger, der zwar die Gesellschaft der Artgenossen braucht, sich selbst aber trotzdem am nächsten ist. Auch der Wolf in dem Film strebt nach etwas, findet es im Leben aber nicht, und dann, als er dem Tode nahe ist, weiß er nicht, ob er denn überhaupt das finden will, was er gesucht hat. Ein Vogel begleitet ihn während seines Lebens – ein Zeichen für Freiheit.

Wie der Wolf im Film verliert auch der Mensch durch die Suche bedeutende Zeit, die ihm auch durch die immer größer werdenden Leistungsansprüche genommen wird. Das Erreichen des Durchschnitts und das Anpassen an das gesellschaftliche Mittelmaß erfordert viel Kraft, und andererseits geht dabei der Individualismus des Einzelnen verloren. In Zukunft sollte der Mensch etwas seines Kontrollbedürfnisses abgeben und sich auf das Hier und Jetzt besinnen, um sich selbst nicht zu verlieren.

Am Anfang standen verschiedene Überlegungen im Raum, wie der Film gemacht werden sollte, bis man sich schließlich darauf festlegte, die Skizzen per Hand zu zeichnen und am Computer mit dem Grafiktablett (Bamboo Pen & Touch) und dem Programm Gimp zu outlinen und zu kolorieren. Der Schnitt wurde mit Adobe Elements 3.0 gemacht. Der Ton wurde aus Gema- und AKM- freien Musikstücken gebastelt.
194863.biography: **Michaela Gehmayr** und **Laura Kaltenbrunner** besuchen derzeit die 5. Klasse des Realgymnasium am Benediktinerstift Lambach. Michaela Gehmayr interessiert sich für Psychologie und philosophische Themen. Laura interessiert sich für Kunst, aber auch für Biologie und möchte, wie Michaela, Medizin studieren.

194888.name: Zukunftswürfel
194888.description:
"Wir wollen berühmt werden!“. Das war der große Wunsch der Schulanfänger, den sie im Rahmen einer Kinderkonferenz äußerten. Aus diesem Grund entschlossen wir uns für die Teilnahme am Projekt u19, bei welchem die Kinder eigene Zukunftsideen entwickeln und präsentieren können.

In den letzten Wochen arbeiteten wir nun intensiv an der Entwicklung interessanter Ideen und Erfindungen. Daraus ergaben sich schlussendlich sechs Themenbereiche, die auf jede Seite des Würfels aufgeteilt wurden und in kleinen Heften anzusehen sind: gelb – Gesundheit; orange – Essen; blau – Arbeit; lila – Wohnung; grün – Zeitreise; rot – Zeitdauer.
194888.biography: Die Projektgruppe besteht aus 18 SchulanfängerInnen des Kindergartens Auwiesenstraße in Linz.

194924.name: ConnectIn(g)
194924.authors: Dino Grgic, Magnus Reinstadler, Franz Reinstadler, Robin von Mendel
194924.description: Das Projekt _ConnectIn(g)_ ist innerhalb von zwei Wochen entstanden. Obwohl es ein Schulprojekt ist, wurden im Grunde alle Inhalte außerhalb der Schulzeit erstellt. Die Animation _ConnectIn(g)_ ist ein Werbespot für ein fiktives Zukunftsprodukt, welches einem ermöglicht, so gut wie alles per Gedanken zu steuern. Auf lockere Art und Weise soll sich der Werbespot mit dem Pro und Kontra einer solchen Erfindung beschäftigen. So wird zum Beispiel die Überwachung der Daten, die auch jetzt schon grenzwertige Bereiche erlangt hat, kritisiert. Anhand des übertriebenen Beispiels einer Erfindung, bei der weitaus mehr und intimere Daten anfallen, soll auf die Problematik eines leichtfertigen Umgangs mit Daten aufmerksam gemacht werden. Die Charaktere, die Texte, alle Gegenstände, die im Video vorkommen wurden mit Autodesk Maya erstellt, und die Logos wurden mit Adobe Illustrator und Adobe Photoshop erstellt. Mit Adobe Premiere wurde alles zusammengeschnitten. Auf Grund des hohen Zeitdrucks, innerhalb von zwei Wochen neben dem Schulalltag das Projekt rechtzeitig für den Wettbewerb fertig zu kriegen, sind noch ein paar Fehler, in dem Video, die leider nicht mehr ausgebessert werden konnten.
194924.biography: Die vier Schüler besuchen gemeinsam die 7. Klasse des Bundesoberstufenrealgymnasiums Bad Hofgastein mit musisch-kreativem Schwerpunkt.

194953.name: Weltrekord für eine bessere Welt
194953.description:
Soziales Engagement gehört in unserer Schule selbstverständlich dazu. Unser Weihnachtsprojekt 2011 war aber gleichzeitig der Versuch, einen bestehenden Weltrekord zu verbessern. Aus den gesammelten Spendengeldern sollte die längste Münzschlange der Welt, gelegt aus 1-Cent-Münzen, entstehen.

Ab Jänner 2011 waren wir mit dem Sammeln von Spendengeldern beschäftigt: im Familien- und Bekanntenkreis, durch Aufstellen von Spendendosen in Kaufhäusern, Betrieben und öffentlichen Einrichtungen, bei Gottesdiensten in den Heimatpfarren, durch verschiedene Aktionen (Karaokeabende, Kuchenbuffets, Ostereierfärben, Straßenmusik, Bastelarbeiten …), Firmensponsoring. Parallel mussten die gesamten Spenden in 1-Cent-Münzen gewechselt werden.

In der Zeit von 5. bis 8. Dezember wurden die bis dahin gesammelten 4,5 Millionen 1-Cent-Münzen (entspricht 10,6 Tonnen) in der Stadthalle Kirchdorf und in den Turnsälen unserer Schule aufgelegt. Dabei arbeiteten zum Teil mehr als 200 SchülerInnen gleichzeitig. Es wurde streng darauf geachtet, dass die Münzen eine durchgehende Linie bilden und nebeneinander liegende Reihen sich nicht berühren. Am 9. Dezember wurde eine Münzschlangenlänge von rund 75,24 km notariell bestätigt. Damit war der aktuelle Weltrekord übertroffen.

Mit den nun zur Verfügung stehenden 45.000 Euro werden Projekte für Straßenkinder, Landlosenunterstützung, Wasserschutz, Familienförderung, behinderte Kinder in Brasilien, Bolivien und Kenia unterstützt. Mit einem Teil des Geldes wird aber auch sozial bedürftigen Menschen in Kirchdorf geholfen.

Links: www.cent4record.at
194953.biography: Die rund 850 SchülerInnen, die an dem Projekt mitgewirkt haben, besuchen die ersten bis achten Klassen des Bundesrealgymnasiums und Bundesoberstufenrealgymnasiums in Kirchdorf an der Krems.

194955.name: Fragment Planet
194955.description:
_Fragment Planet_ ist ein Real-Time-Strategy-Game. Im Gegensatz zu den gängigen Strategiespielen habe ich das klassische Terrain durch fliegende Inseln ersetzt. Man kann entweder im Survival-Modus im Team gegen gegnerische Angriffswellen, oder im normalen Modus gegeneinander kämpfen. Ein Tutorial ist im Spiel integriert, allerdings ist es englisch, da ich das Spiel im Internet veröffentlichen möchte. Am Ende der Sommerferien 2011 habe ich mit der Entwicklung von _Fragment Planet_ begonnen. Insgesamt habe ich fast 2.500 Stunden an dem Spiel gearbeitet.

Nachdem die Erde bei einem Experiment, auf der Suche nach einer neuen, unerschöpflichen Energiequelle, zerstört wurde, bekämpfen sich die Überlebenden, um fliegende Inseln zu erobern und so ihr eigenes Fortbestehen zu sichern. Mithilfe von zurückentwickelten Flugmaschinen, im Steampunk-Stil, erweitern sie ihre Basen und bauen Armeen, um den Vorstoß ihrer Kontrahenten zu verhindern. Die Wegwerfgesellschaft und das Verschwendertum vor der Katastrophe haben zur Vernichtung der gesamten Erde geführt. Die Überlebenden sind gezwungen, einen neuen naturverbundenen Lebensstil zu entwickeln, doch manchen fällt das schwerer als anderen. Im Laufe der zukünftigen Entwicklung werde ich zwei weitere Fraktionen einführen, wobei eine den alten Lebensstil vollständig weiterlebt und so ein Risiko für alle anderen darstellt. Noch mehr als heutzutage sind die letzten Menschen verpflichtet zu lernen, mit der Natur im Einklang zu leben.

Links: http://www.indiedb.com/games/fragment-planet
194955.biography: **Simon Stix**, geb. 1994, besucht das BRG Fadingerstraße in Linz und hat 2009 ein Semester lang durch das Projekt „Schüler/innen an die Unis“ an der Johannes Kepler Universität Informatik studiert. In seiner Freizeit setzt er sich seit Jahren mit vielen Bereichen am Computer auseinander, u. a. Programmieren, 3D Modellieren und Soundtrack komponieren. Seine Hobbies sind die oben genannten Aktivitäten und selbstverständlich Computerspielen, sowohl als Freizeitbeschäftigung, als auch als Inspirationsquelle für die eigene Arbeit.

194957.name: iTanky
194957.description:
_iTanky_ ist ein kostenloses, zweidimensionales Panzerspiel für das iPhone. Es gibt viele abwechslungsreiche Level, computergesteuerte Panzer und einen Mehrspielermodus, um Freunde herauszufordern. Das Ziel ist es, am Schlachtfeld am längsten zu überleben und möglichst wenig beschädigt zu werden. Zuerst wählt man einen Panzer und eine Karte aus. Während des Spiels kann man Items sammeln, um z. B. neue Waffen zu bekommen. Im Einzelspielermodus sind die gegnerischen Panzer computergesteuert.

Mit dem Mehrspielermodus kann man gegen Freunde per Wifi oder Bluetooth spielen. Viele weitere Funktionen werden im nächsten Update geliefert, wie z. B. neue Waffen und Items, ein Online-Map-Editor, um neue Level zu gestalten.

Die komplette Physik-Engine und das Partikelsystem wurden von mir selbst entwickelt. Für die Karten habe ich einen Level-Editor programmiert, der in jedem gängigen Browser verwendet werden kann. Man kann die verschiedenen Kartenelemente per Drag&Drop in das Feld ziehen und verschieben und anschließend die Karte am iPhone herunterladen.

Links: http://facebook.com/iTankyApp http://itanky.com
194957.biography: **Felix Krause**, geb. 1994, besucht die HTL Wiener Neustadt, interessiert sich für Programmierung, Robotik, Tennis und Golf. 2010 hat er Österreich bei der Robocup Weltmeisterschaft in Singapur im Soccer Junior Wettbewerb vertreten. Sein Berufsziel ist Entwickler in einem kalifornischen Start-up Unternehmen zu werden. 2011 hat er für drei Monate bei 6Wunderkinder an Wunderlist und Wunderkit gearbeitet und für seine _Bikemap App_ eine Anerkennung bei u19 gewonnen. 2012 gewann er mit seinem Team den europäischen Botball-Robotik-Wettbewerb.

194966.name: Quadrocopter
194966.description:
Ziel des Projektes war die Realisierung eines flugfähigen Roboters, der sich per Funktechnik manuell sowie computergesteuert in einem Raum bewegen kann. Bei den Robotern handelt es sich um mehrere auf dem AeroQuad-Projekt basierende Quadrocopter. Für uns war hier vor allem die Unabhängigkeit von Teilprodukten und deren Weiterentwicklungen wichtig, um ein stetiges Weiterentwickeln des Projektes sicherstellen zu können. Ein weiterer wichtiger Punkt für die Umsetzung dieses Bildungsprojekt ist die fast ausschließliche Verwendung von frei verfügbarer und veränderbarer Soft- und Hardware.
Der Flugroboter empfängt Steuerdaten übermittelt dieser wiederum alle verfügbaren Sensorwerte. Die Kommunikation findet dabei über ein WLAN-Netz statt, um eine Steuerung ohne zusätzliche Elektronik zu ermöglichen. Für das manuelle Steuern des Quadrocopters steht dem Piloten eine Android-Applikation zur Verfügung.

Für das autonome Fliegen im Raum wird mittels Kameras und auf dem Roboter angebrachter Sensoren die Positionsbestimmung des Roboters bestimmt. Dadurch soll es möglich sein, einen Computer selbstständig Routen und Flugmanöver planen und ausführen zu lassen.

Links: http://quadrocopter.drseus.eu/
194966.biography: **Lukas Pfeifhofer** und **Tanja Roschanz** besuchen gemeinsam die Abschlussklasse der HTL Mössingerstraße in Kärnten mit dem Schwerpunkt Technische Informatik. Lukas Pfeifhofer, geb. 1993, interessiert sich für Softwareentwicklung und wird ab Herbst 2012 Technische Informatik studieren. Tanja Roschanz, geb. 1992, wird auch ein technisches Studium beginnen, jedoch in einer etwas anderen Richtung, der Architektur.

194996.name: handsome
194996.authors: Felix Brandstetter, Gregor Eckmayr, Valentina Heinisch, William Mikulaschek, Killian Sochor, C.LOUD, Anna Neubauer
194996.description: Die Jugendlichen der Partizipations- und Medieninitiative C.LOUD setzten sich im Zuge des Videoprojektes _handsome_ intensiv mit Themen wie traditionellen Geschlechterrollen, gesellschaftlichen Konventionen, kulturellem Pluralismus und nonverbaler Kommunikation auseinander. Die in diesem gedanklichen Prozess erarbeiteten Erkenntnisse und Einsichten setzten sie mit „helfenden Händen“ Erwachsener und Kinder unterschiedlichen Geschlechts, Alters und unterschiedlicher Herkunft in einem 90-sekündigen Video um. Die Motivation für dieses Projekt gründete auf der Frage nach immer noch existierenden Vorurteilen gegenüber Liebespaaren, die nicht zu hundert Prozent der Norm entsprechen. So scheinen gleichgeschlechtliche Paare, Beziehungen zwischen Menschen unterschiedlicher Herkunft oder mit großem Altersunterschied in unserer Gesellschaft immer noch nicht hinreichend akzeptiert zu werden – was fehlt, ist Toleranz. Die Idee zur gestalterischen Umsetzung mit der ausschließlichen Abbildung von Händen war schnell gefunden, eine tiefergehende Auseinandersetzung mit dem Begriff „Toleranz“ zeigte jedoch, dass dieser für von Intoleranz betroffene Gruppen mittlerweile negativ konnotiert war, da Toleranz lediglich das stillschweigende Hinnehmen gewisser Umstände meint und nicht die positiv assoziierte Gleichstellung. Weiters wurde das ursprüngliche Thema der Liebespaare von den Jugendlichen bald als zu eng gefasst empfunden und somit um eine Vielzahl von mit den Händen darstellbaren Ausdrücken erweitert. Bei der Produktion des Videos waren die beteiligten Erwachsenen angesichts der technischen und gestalterischen Kompetenz der Jugendlichen wohl am meisten verblüfft.
194996.biography: Bei** C.LOUD** produzieren Jugendliche ihre Medien selbst. Welches Medium dabei benutzt wird, ist ganz egal: Video, Audio, Blogs – alles ist recht um ihre Meinung nach außen zu tragen. Denn Ziel dieser Initiative ist es, Erwachsenen klar zu machen, dass Jugendliche etwas zu sagen haben und als Teil der Gesellschaft ihr Mitspracherecht wahrnehmen.

195006.name: Designing Zero-Energy Building Components with Smart Thermobimetal
195006.description:
Challenging the traditional presumption that building skins are static and inanimate, this applied research project examines the replacement of this convention with one that posits the prosthetic layer between man and his environment as a responsive and active skin. Using sheet thermobimetals (TBM), a smart material that automatically curls when heated, iand Nitinol, a wire material that shrinks when heated, building surfaces can self-ventilate and reduce its dependency on mechanical air conditioning. With today’s digital technology and driving interest in sustainable design, this simple material can transcend its currently limited role as a mechanical device to a dynamic building surface material as well as expand the discourse of the performative architecture.

We want to develop two codependent systems in an effort to heightened performance of thermobimetal and Nitinol combinations: an interactive, hybrid system of the two dynamic materials operating simultaneously and a compatible system of oscillating performance where one material performs while the other remains static. The results of these two systems will be applied to a curtain wall glass panel system and to a bris-soleil surface intended for easy installation in commercial applications. With the use of complex digital softwares, structural and performance models will determine the optimal geometry. It is likely that these off-the-shelf softwares have to be custom altered to be useful to the process. In some cases, scripting will be method of choice. The combination of these new technologies with traditional systems and materials will produce forms that are otherwise impossible to imagine.

Links: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-Ms5qoMO3gQ
195006.biography: **Doris Sung** (US). After receiving her BA at Princeton University and M.Arch. at Columbia University, Doris Sung worked in various offices in cities across the U.S. before arriving in Los Angeles in 2001. She developed her research focus while teaching at University of Southern California (USC), the Southern California Institute of Architecture (SCI-Arc), University of Colorado and the Catholic University of America. In 1999, she opened her office, dO|Su Studio Architecture, and soon received many AIA and ASID awards for her work.

195016.name: qaul.net - tools for the next revolution
195016.description:
_qaul.net_ implements a redundant open communication principle that directly allows Wi-Fi-enabled computers and mobile devices to form a spontaneous network. Chat and Twitter functions as well as movie streaming become accessible independently of the Internet and cellular networks. _qaul.net_ spreads like a virus and an open-source community may modify _qaul.net_ as needed.

Digital means of communication are shaping our times. We are now able to follow revolutionary upheavals and dramatic natural catastrophes almost in real time. Yet the seemingly unlimited flow of information covers up our actual communication conditions.

t times of communication blackouts in Egypt, Burma or Tibet and the large power outages often caused by natural disasters, _qaul.net_ has taken on the challenge of critically investigating individual communication conditions while exploring new horizons together.

During the demonstrations in Egypt in January 2011, all Internet and mobile phone connections were shut down completely for six days. This blackout marked a caesura, as did other Internet crackdowns, such as those in Myanmar in 2007, Tibet in 2008, Iran and the Uighur territories in 2009 as well as in Libya in 2011. Also during the massive earthquakes in Haiti in 2010 and Japan in 2011, cellular antennas did not work and the remaining networks became overloaded – this meant that people in distress could not call for help.

Free network connections for everyone have often been discussed. Mesh networks such as _Funkfeuer_ are based on OLSR (Open Link State Routing). And although wireless cards increasingly support ad-hoc modes, they have failed to spread because of a lack of the necessary configurations and standards. Then self-networking becomes a matter of trial-and-error, which makes it – for all practical purposes – inconsequential next to the growing list of commercial providers and their systematic elimination of competitors.

_qaul.net_ implements OLSR, transferring the network directly to wireless devices, and combines server and router software with applications. Network and operation become one. Open-source software are available under the terms of the GPL (GNU Public License) and so may be used free of charge as well as developed further.

Nowadays, Wi-Fi routers form a dense network and if modified properly even have a range of up to 300 kilometers. Yet _qaul.net_ is not primarily about connecting routers but individual computers and mobile devices. The focus is on the neighborhood and collaborating, and this results in much denser networks. Moreover, spontaneous networks between different devices may be established at any time. Network access is not central but passed on like a virus. When users gain Wi-Fi access with _qaul.net_, they can download and install the software directly via this connection. Anyone who has a Wi-Fi-enabled device can participate, expand an existing network or create their own.

In the digital age we are informed by communication conditions that are prerequisites of freedom of speech and information. _qaul.net_ creates tools with which we can jointly probe general design options. This communication tool can bridge gaps in the infrastructure or spread spontaneously in the event of a power outage. And even when it is used just for fun, _qaul.net_ sensitizes people to the infrastructure, conditions and dependencies – and offers an incentive to try new forms of networking.

The word “qaul” is Arabic and means statement, speech or word and is pronounced like the English word “call”. _qaul.net_ reverses the maxim of global and free communication, and – from the perspective of the here and now – looks out into the neighborhood and from there out into the big wide world. As a tribute to the Arab insurgents, this project works like a group of activists who have joined forces and so dare to test their own potential for action as a beacon against a dominant, seemingly immovable power structure.

Links: http://www.qaul.net/a12

They have received awards from, e.g., Ars Electronica, Transmediale, the Saxon State Ministry for Science and the Arts, Swiss Federal Office of Culture, Migros Cultural Percentage, Canton of Zurich, CYNETART and EMARE.

195068.name: Matopy
195068.description:
_Matopy_ is changing the world by revolutionizing the way we interact with the web.

As babies we are listening all the time, and most people can speak by the age of three, but we only become competent at reading and writing when we reach seven or eight. _Matopy_ will provide a more natural way of accessing any online content, which does not require a monitor, a keyboard or even a desk. In the not-too-distant future, the recipe you are following online will be read aloud to you by _Matopy_ while your hands are covered in flour and egg.

It’s time for the web to speak.

_Matopy_ uses sound to present information in the way a graphic designer uses color, layout and style to convey information beyond the text of a page. We use audio cues, multiple voices and sound effects to convey context and add meaning to the textual content, giving a richer, deeper experience of the web. We are effectively embellishing the spoken word just as the graphic designer does to the written word.

For instance, headings would be spoken in a different voice to subheadings, and body text would be spoken by a third voice (perhaps a woman for the heading, a man for the subheading, and a second woman for the body text). Links would be implied by sound effects and potentially by changes to the tonal qualities of the voice or the background music. Color changes could be achieved in the same way.

The final result is to have a beautiful, absorbing, interactive and fun audio experience that is as rich and as individual as the visual experiences on the web today. In the long term we see people being able to personalize their audio sites just as they do today with themes for their blogs. Larger companies will be able to tailor their brands and their corporate identities with polished soundtracks, voiceovers and audio interaction.

Links: http://www.matopy.com/ getaudioweb.com
195068.biography: **Sam Jewell** (US) is the ideator of _Matopy_ and has a deep understanding of the visually impaired community. He has an MA and MEng from Cambridge and MIT and an MA and MSc in innovation design engineering, RCA.

195694.name: Duku Spacemarines
195694.description:
_Duku Spacemarines_ is a short animated film about a mosquito. No, it’s rather the story of a Chinese man hacking the American capitalist system. Or is it about chickens? Actually it is the story of a story. A scenario that strives after the high standards of Hollywood, with explosions. And so the animation, from the glitch to the glow, never mind if there is nothing to say, cinema has visual effects.
_Duku Spacemarines_—a 2012 graduation film from the department of digital art of the University of Paris 8—was handmade in a typical Parisian apartment, with a table, a kitchen, and a small living-room filled with four computers, eight screens and four guys who go under the name of La Mécanique du Plastique.

Links: http://lamecaniqueduplastique.fr
195694.biography: La Mécanique du Plastique (FR). As a collective of four French independent artists, La Mécanique du Plastique produce curious, short animated films mixing various techniques. After graduating in fine art, ancient Greek, computer science and computer graphics, our professional activities consist in programming, painting, music and digital art.

195708.name: Snail Trail
195708.description:
A snail invents the wheel and goes through a cultural evolution to finally get back to its origin.

The basic idea of the _Snail Trail_ is inspired by processes of exponential acceleration, which can be observed at different levels. Thus the evolution of life proceeds at an extremely slow pace for more than three billion years, until it suddenly seems to explode in the Cambrian period. The tools of human beings progress relatively little during the Stone Age until there is a rapid cultural development during the Holocene.

Nowadays, a similar acceleration process is generated by the exchange of information through the Internet. From this perspective, the exponential spiral on a snail shell may almost appear like a miraculous wink of nature.

The animation is based on a laser sculpture (https://vimeo.com/27659555), which has a somehow purer and darker feeling than the film. For me the challenge was to find the right tone for the film, to make it into something other than a mere copy of the laser installation. It took me some time to realize that I had to free my mind from the original character and to give space to an evolution. Finally, the film turned out much brighter and more colorful than I had imagined in the beginning.

Links: www.philippartus.com
195708.biography: Philipp Artus (DE), born 1982, grew up in Bremen/Germany and began studying art at the École des Beaux Arts in Nantes, France. He continued his autodidactic studies of animation and music theory in Portugal and is currently finishing his graduation project at the Academy of Media Arts in Cologne, Germany. His experimental animations and site-specific installations explore the manifestations of life through movement, sound and imagery. He composes audiovisual experiences that unite playful elements with minimalist structures, timeless themes with contemporary observations, turbulent acceleration with contemplative silence. His projects have been shown in various museums, festivals and galleries around the world.

195775.name: Rollin' Safari
195775.authors: Anna Habermehl, Constantin Paeplow, Kyra Buschor
195775.description:
_Rollin’ Safari_ is a series of four short clips about bloated African animals that have huge difficulty living a normal life. The clips are a student project created by Constantin Paeplow, Kyra Buschor and Anna Habermehl and produced by Valentina Brüning and Anna Habermehl as trailers for the 2013 International Festival of Animated Film in Stuttgart.

Kyra and Constantin started brainstorming in October 2011, their initial idea being to tell the story of a hunter who comes across a fat, rolling deer that, because of its shape, is incapable of controlling itself. They imagined what a wildlife documentary would be like if all animals in it were round and what scenarios might occur. In November 2011 Anna Habermehl joined the team as the third director and together they decided to produce several funny clips of various round animals. The directors’ biggest inspiration was numerous popular wildlife documentaries as _Our Planet_, _Planet Earth_ or Grzimek’s _Serengeti Shall Not Die_.

Links: https://www.facebook.com/RollinWild
